definition_zh: 讲述；叙述；为影片配解说
definition_en: to tell a story in speech or writing, giving events in order, or to be the voice that explains a film
core_image: 祖母坐在火炉旁，把事情一件一件按顺序讲给孩子听
scene: 旅途中大巴司机的麦克风一直没响，直到导游开始给游客讲这座古城的来历，车厢才安静下来。The guide began to narrate the story of the old city, and the whole bus fell quiet.
sceneCN: 这里 narrate 是「讲述、叙述」（第 1 个义项：把事情按顺序讲出来）；句意：导游开始讲述这座古城的往事，整车人都安静了下来。

pos.zh: 讲述；叙述；给影片配解说

derivatives.zh: 由 narrate 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「叙述、讲述」
由 narrate 加表示施动者的后缀 -or 构成，义为「讲述者、叙述者」
与 narrate 同源，借形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「叙事、故事；叙事的」
由 narrate 加 -able 构成，义为「可以被叙述的」

senses.title: To tell a story
senses.definition: to give an account of events in speech or writing, usually in the order they happened
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面讲述事情的经过，通常按发生先后顺序
senses.example: She narrated the events of that night calmly.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静地讲述了那天晚上发生的事情。
senses.why: Latin narrare meant to tell or recount, so the verb keeps the plain act of turning events into words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 narrare 意为「讲述、复述」，所以这个动词保留了最朴素的动作：把发生的事情变成话语。

senses.title: To be the voice of a film
senses.definition: to speak the explanatory words of a film, broadcast or slide show
senses.definitionCN: 为影片、广播或幻灯片朗读解说词
senses.example: A famous actor will narrate the wildlife documentary.
senses.exampleCN: 一位著名演员将为这部野生动物纪录片配解说。
senses.why: The modern media sense keeps the telling, but moves the speaker from the room into the soundtrack.
senses.whyCN: 现代媒介的用法保留「讲述」，只是把说话的人从房间里搬到了片子的声音里。

senses.title: To tell it in full detail
senses.definition: to set out an account with its details in order, so that the listener can follow it
senses.definitionCN: 把细节按顺序交代清楚，让听的人能顺着听下来
senses.example: In the report he narrated every step of the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 他在报告里把实验的每一个步骤都叙述了一遍。
senses.why: Recounting in Latin also meant going through a matter point by point, so the verb carries the idea of a full, ordered account.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语「复述」本身也含有「一件事一件事过一遍」的意思，所以这个动词带着「完整、有序叙述」的成分。

intro.en: Narrate comes from Latin narrare, to tell or recount, which is generally linked to gnarus, knowing.
intro.cn: narrate 来自拉丁语 narrare（讲述、复述），一般认为它与 gnarus（知晓的）同源。

items.en: Narrare means to tell, recount or relate a series of events.
items.cn: 拉丁语 narrare 意为讲述、复述、把一系列事情说出来。

items.en: The participle stem narrat- gives every later form of the word its base.
items.cn: 分词词干 narrat- 为这个词之后的各种形式提供基础。

items.en: It is generally connected with gnarus, knowing, and with noscere, to learn; the link is reconstructed.
items.cn: 一般认为它与 gnarus（知晓的）、noscere（学习、认识）相连；这一联系属于重构。

items.en: The Latin verb passes through French forms that travellers and writers carried on.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词经由法语的各种形式，被旅人和作家带向别处。

items.en: Narrate enters English as a learned verb, but the first date is uncertain.
items.cn: narrate 作为书面语动词进入英语，但最早出现的年代不确定。

items.en: Film and broadcasting add the job of narrating pictures.
items.cn: 电影与广播给它增加了「为画面配解说」的新工作。

note.en: Narrate belongs to the narr- family of telling words and sits near the ordinary verbs for saying and describing.
note.cn: narrate 属于 narr- 一族「讲述」词，并与表示说、描述的普通动词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of telling a story
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词：叙述、讲述的行为

entries.definition: the person who tells a story
an account of events, or a story
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词与形容词：叙事、故事；叙事的

entries.definition: to tell a story or describe what happened
entries.definitionCN: 近义动词：讲述、复述经过

entries.definition: to tell a story or give details of an event
entries.definitionCN: 近义动词：讲述、细说事情的经过

entries.definition: to say what something is like
entries.definitionCN: 近义动词：描述，侧重呈现样子而非事件顺序

normalIntro.en: Narrate is the telling verb of the narr- family, and every member of the family keeps that act of recounting.
normalIntro.cn: narrate 是 narr- 词族里表示「讲」的动词，族中每个词都保留了「复述」这个动作。

normal.en: Narrate, narration and narrator share one stem: the verb does it, one noun is the act, the other is the doer.
normal.cn: narrate、narration 与 narrator 共用一个词干：动词做这件事，一个名词是行为本身，另一个是做事的人。

normal.en: Latin narrare meant to recount, so to narrate is to set events down in order.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 narrare 意为复述，所以 narrate 就是把事情按顺序排列出来。

normal.en: The narrate family is often used with story, events and account.
normal.cn: 这一组词常与 story、events、account 等表示故事与叙述的名词连用。

normal.en: The stem narrat- appears in narrated and narrating, so the endings only change the grammar.
normal.cn: 词干 narrat- 出现在 narrated 与 narrating 里，词尾只改变语法作用。

normal.en: A film can be narrated, which is why a documentary needs a narrator.
normal.cn: 影片可以配解说，所以纪录片总需要一位 narrator。

abstract.en: Picture a grandmother by the stove, giving the evening bead by bead, like a string of events.
abstract.cn: 想象祖母坐在炉边，把事情一颗颗串起来，像串念珠一样按顺序讲。

abstract.en: See a hand drawing a line with arrowheads, one event after another, each pointing to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手画出一条带箭头的线，一件事接着一件事，每一段都指向下一段。

abstract.en: See a finger moving down a long list, ticking every line in turn so nothing is left out.
abstract.cn: 想象有人拿一根手指，沿着一条长长的清单往下点，一件事都不漏。

examples.en: The witness narrated the accident in careful detail.
examples.cn: 目击者非常仔细地叙述了事故经过。

examples.en: He narrated the audiobook with a warm, unhurried voice.
examples.cn: 他用温暖而不紧不慢的声音朗读了这本有声书。

examples.en: Children learn to narrate their day before they learn to write it down.
examples.cn: 孩子们先学着讲述自己的一天，之后才学会把它写下来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿来说」——把事情「拿来说」一遍，就是讲述；这只是谐音联想，与拉丁语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 gnarus（知晓的，一般认为与 noscere「认识」同源）→ 拉丁语 narrare（讲述、复述）→ 分词词干 narrat- → 英语 narrate，核心义是「把事情按顺序说出来」。同族有 narration（叙述）、narrative（叙事）、narrator（叙述者）。

sensesIntro.en: Narrate begins with the plain telling of events, widens to the voice that explains a film, and also covers a careful account given detail by detail.
sensesIntro.cn: narrate 先指把事情讲出来，再扩展到为影片担任解说的声音，也涵盖把细节一一交代清楚的完整陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grandmother telling the evening bead by bead by the stove.
core.cn: 核心意象：祖母在火炉旁把事情一件一件讲给孩子听。

branches.en: Giving an account of events is the plain verb sense.
branches.cn: 把事情讲出来是动词的普通义。

branches.en: The voice on a soundtrack does the same telling for pictures.
branches.cn: 影片里的旁白声音在为画面做同样的讲述。

branches.en: Telling with every detail is the careful, ordered version of the same act.
branches.cn: 把每个细节都讲出来，是同一个动作最仔细、最有条理的版本。

branches.en: A story and a full account differ only in how much detail the teller chooses.
branches.cn: 讲故事与详细陈述，区别只在于讲述者选择铺多少细节。

branches.en: A film narrator must keep the order clear even while the pictures carry the detail.
branches.cn: 影片旁白即使有画面承担细节，也必须把顺序交代清楚。

intro.en: Narrate is a Latin-derived verb: the stem narr- carries the telling, and the endings -ate, -ion, -or and -ive build its family.
intro.cn: narrate 是源自拉丁语的动词：词干 narr- 承载「讲述」，词尾 -ate、-ion、-or、-ive 构成它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin narrare means to tell or recount, and its participle stem narrat- is the base of the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 narrare 意为讲述、复述，它的分词词干 narrat- 是英语这一词族的基础。

items.example: Gnarus is thought to be the deeper root.
items.exampleCN: gnarus 被认为是更深的词根。

items.example: Narrare is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: narrare 是动词的直接来源。

items.example: The stem narrat- builds the English forms.
items.exampleCN: 词干 narrat- 构成英语的各种形式。

items.example: Narrate is the bare verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: narrate 是词族里的基本动词。

items.example: The ending -ate makes the learned verb narrate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成书面语动词 narrate。

items.example: The suffix -ion forms narration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 narration。

items.example: The suffix -or forms narrator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 narrator。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms narrative.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ive 构成 narrative。

items.example: The suffix -able forms narratable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 narratable。

items.meaning: the act of telling a story
items.example: Narration is the act the verb names.
items.exampleCN: narration 是动词所指的行为。

definition_zh: 叙述者；讲述者；（影片、小说的）旁白；解说员
definition_en: the person who tells a story, either in a book and film or aloud as a voice, giving events in order
core_image: 银幕外一个声音，从第一句旁白开始把整场故事牵起来
scene: 字幕还没出现，幕布后面先响起一个低沉的声音，把片头那段历史一句一句地说给全场观众听，故事就这样开始了。A low voice from behind the curtain began to tell the old story, and it was this unseen narrator that carried the whole film.
sceneCN: 这里 narrator 是「旁白、叙述者」（第 1 个义项：讲故事、念旁白的那个声音）；句意：幕布后面一个低沉的声音开始讲述往事，正是这位看不见的叙述者撑起了整部影片。

pos.zh: 叙述者；讲述者；旁白；解说员

collocations.phrase: the voices of narrator and characters

derivatives.zh: narrator 的基础动词，去掉施动者后缀 -or 得到，义为「讲述」
由 narrate 加 -ion 构成，义为「叙述」，即 narrator 所做的事
与 narrator 同源，义为「叙事；故事」，即 narrator 讲出的东西
由 narrator 加 -ial 构成，义为「叙述者的、与叙述者有关的」

senses.title: The voice that tells
senses.definition: the person or voice that tells, and sometimes explains, the events of a film or programme
senses.definitionCN: 为影片或节目讲述、有时解释事情的说话人或声音
senses.example: The narrator introduces each scene of the documentary.
senses.exampleCN: 解说员为纪录片的每一个场景作介绍。
senses.why: Latin narrare means to tell, and the Latin suffix -or marks the person who does the telling, so the narrator is simply the teller.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 narrare 意为讲述，拉丁语后缀 -or 标记做这件事的人，所以 narrator 就是那位讲述者本身。

senses.title: The telling voice in a book
senses.definition: the character or voice that tells the story of a novel or poem
senses.definitionCN: 小说或诗作里讲故事的那个角色或声音，不一定等于作者
senses.example: The narrator of the novel is a boy of twelve.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的叙述者是一个十二岁的男孩。
senses.why: Fictional telling needed a name for whoever holds the story, so the same doer noun moved into literature.
senses.whyCN: 虚构作品需要给「掌握故事的那个声音」一个名字，于是这个表示施动者的名词进入了文学。

senses.title: The person who reads aloud
senses.titleCN: 朗读的人；有声书播讲者
senses.definition: a person who reads a book or text aloud for others to hear
senses.definitionCN: 为他人朗读书籍或文字的人
senses.example: A professional narrator reads every chapter with a different voice.
senses.exampleCN: 一位专业播讲者用不同的声音朗读每一章。
senses.why: The doer noun also fits anyone who performs the telling, even when the words belong to somebody else.
senses.whyCN: 这个施动名词同样适用于任何把讲述表演出来的人，即使那些话原本属于别人。

intro.en: Narrator comes from Latin narrator, a teller, built from narrare, to tell, and the person suffix -or.
intro.cn: narrator 来自拉丁语 narrator（讲述者），由 narrare（讲述）加表示人的后缀 -or 构成。

items.en: Narrare means to tell or recount a series of events.
items.cn: 拉丁语 narrare 意为讲述、复述一系列事情。

items.en: The noun narrator names the person who does that telling.
items.cn: 名词 narrator 用来称呼做这件事的那个人。

items.en: Latin -or marks the doer, the same suffix as in actor and doctor.
items.cn: 拉丁语后缀 -or 标记施动者，与 actor、doctor 中的后缀相同。

items.en: The family takes the participle stem narrat- plus the person ending -or.
items.cn: 这个词族用分词词干 narrat- 加表示人的词尾 -or。

items.en: Narrator enters English as a learned noun for the teller of a tale, but the first date is uncertain.
items.cn: narrator 作为书面语名词进入英语，指故事的讲述者，但最早出现的年代不确定。

items.en: The noun spreads to film voice-overs and to the fictional voice of a novel.
items.cn: 该名词进一步扩展到电影旁白与小说的虚构叙述声音。

note.en: Narrator is the doer noun of the narr- family and sits near the ordinary words for tellers, writers and speakers.
note.cn: narrator 是 narr- 词族里的施动名词，并与表示讲述者、作者、发言人的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: to tell a story
entries.definitionCN: 基础动词：讲述，narrator 正是做这个动作的人

entries.definition: the act of telling a story
a story or account of events
the writer of a book
entries.definitionCN: 作者：写书的人，与叙述者并不总是同一个人

entries.definition: a person who speaks or makes a speech
entries.definitionCN: 说话者；发言人：泛指开口说话的人

entries.definition: narration heard over the picture in a film
entries.definitionCN: 画外音：电影中覆盖在画面上的旁白

normalIntro.en: Narrator is narrate plus the Latin doer ending -or, so the word points straight at the person who tells.
normalIntro.cn: narrator 就是 narrate 加上拉丁语表示施动者的词尾 -or，所以这个词直接指向讲故事的那个人。

normal.en: The ending -or marks the doer, as in actor and doctor, so a narrator is the one who tells.
normal.cn: 词尾 -or 标记做事的人，如同 actor 与 doctor，所以 narrator 就是讲述的人。

normal.en: The same stem gives narrate, narration and narrative, and only the ending decides the job.
normal.cn: 同一个词干给出 narrate、narration 与 narrative，只有词尾决定它扮演什么角色。

normal.en: A narrator may be the voice of a film, a character in a book, or the person reading aloud.
normal.cn: narrator 可以是影片的旁白、书中的角色，也可以是朗读的人。

normal.en: An unreliable narrator is one whose account the reader cannot wholly trust.
normal.cn: unreliable narrator 指读者不能完全相信其说法的叙述者。

normal.en: The plural narrators splits a story between several voices.
normal.cn: 复数 narrators 表示一个故事由好几个声音分担。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow behind a screen, holding a book, while the audience watches the moving pictures.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布后面有一个握书的影子，观众看的是动的画面，说话的却是它。

abstract.en: Imagine a single thread pulled through page after page, tying every scene to the next.
abstract.cn: 想象一根线从一页穿到另一页，把每一个场景都和前一个系在一起。

abstract.en: See a name on the cover fading, and a voice stepping forward to take the story over.
abstract.cn: 想象封面上作者的名字渐渐淡去，一个声音走上前来接管这个故事。

examples.en: The narrator of the memoir never names herself.
examples.cn: 这本回忆录的叙述者始终没有说出自己的名字。

examples.en: A calm narrator guided us through each scene of the museum tour.
examples.cn: 一位平静的解说员带我们看完了博物馆导览的每一个场景。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a triumph of its unreliable narrator.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说的成功在于其不可靠的叙述者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那瑞特」像外号；也可以记「拿来说的人」——把故事拿来说的那个人就是叙述者。这只是谐音拆词联想，与拉丁语词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 narrare（讲述）→ 拉丁语 narrator（讲述者）＝ 分词词干 narrat- + 施动者后缀 -or（同 actor、doctor）→ 英语 narrator，核心义「做讲述这件事的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Narrator starts with the voice that tells and explains a film, then the fictional teller inside a book, and finally anyone who reads aloud.
sensesIntro.cn: narrator 先指为影片讲述、解释的那个声音，再指小说里虚构的讲述者，最后指任何当众朗读的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a voice from behind the screen that ties the whole story together.
core.cn: 核心意象：银幕外一个声音，把整场故事牵起来。

branches.en: The explaining voice of a film is the media sense.
branches.cn: 影片中解释画面的声音是媒介义。

branches.en: The character who tells the tale is the literary sense.
branches.cn: 书中讲故事的角色是文学义。

branches.en: The person who reads aloud performs the telling with the voice.
branches.cn: 朗读的人用声音把讲述表演出来。

branches.en: Both a film voice and a reader lend their voice to someone else words.
branches.cn: 影片旁白与朗读者的声音都在替别人的话发声。

branches.en: Every narrator holds a thread that the audience follows from scene to scene.
branches.cn: 每位叙述者都握着一根线，观众顺着它从一个场景走到下一个。

intro.en: Narrator is built from the Latin stem narrat- plus the doer suffix -or, and it shares that stem with narrate, narration and narrative.
intro.cn: narrator 由拉丁词干 narrat- 加施动者后缀 -or 构成，并与 narrate、narration、narrative 共用同一个词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin narrare means to tell, and Latin narrator names the teller; -or is the common doer ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 narrare 意为讲述，拉丁语 narrator 指讲述者，-or 是常见的施动者词尾。

items.example: The stem narrat- is shared by the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 narrat- 由整个词族共用。

items.example: Narrare supplies the meaning of telling.
items.exampleCN: narrare 提供「讲述」的含义。

items.example: Latin narrator is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 narrator 是直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -or turns a telling into a teller.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 把「讲述」变成立「讲述者」。

items.example: The verb is what the narrator does.
items.exampleCN: 动词表示叙述者所做的事。

items.example: Narration is the act behind the person.
items.exampleCN: narration 是那个人背后的行为。

items.example: The narrative is what the narrator tells.
items.exampleCN: narrative 是叙述者讲出的东西。

items.example: The adjective narratorial describes a voice into which the author steps.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 narratorial 用来描述作者走进的那个声音。

items.example: Actor shows the same -or in action.
items.exampleCN: actor 展示了同一个 -or 词尾的用法。

items.example: Doctor carries the same doer ending.
items.exampleCN: doctor 带着同一个施动者词尾。

definition_zh: （河流、航道）可通航的；（水域）可用于航行的；可驾驶通过（车辆、船只等）的；可浏览、可操作的（网页、界面）
definition_en: wide or deep enough for ships to travel on; able to be steered through; easy to move around in or find your way through
core_image: 一条被清理过的河道，船头切开水面，一路顺畅驶向远处
scene: 春季融雪之后，河道水位上涨、淤泥被冲走，小船又能一路驶到下游港口。 After the spring melt, small boats could once more reach the port because the river had become navigable.
sceneCN: 这里 navigable 是「可通航的」（第 1 个义项：河流或航道宽深到足以让船只通行）；句意：春季融雪之后，河道变得可通航，小船又能一路驶到港口。

pos.zh: 可通航的；（水域）可航行的
可驾驶通过的；可穿行的
（网页、界面）可浏览、可操作的

derivatives.zh: 由名词词干加 -ate 构成的动词，义为「航行；导航」
形容词加 -ity 构成，义为「可通航性；可操作性」
词干加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「航行；导航」
动词加施事后缀 -or 构成，义为「航海者；领航员」
navigation 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「航行的；导航的」

senses.title: Deep and wide enough for ships
senses.definition: wide and deep enough for ships or boats to sail along, used of a river, canal, or channel
senses.definitionCN: 指河流、运河或水道宽深足够，船只可以顺水而行
senses.example: The lower reaches of the river are navigable all year.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河的下游全年都可通航。
senses.why: The Latin root navis means ship, and the -able suffix means able to, so the core image is water that can carry a ship.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 navis 意为「船」，后缀 -able 表示「能够」，所以核心意象就是「能够承载船只的水面」。

senses.title: Able to be steered across
senses.definition: wide or clear enough for a vehicle, boat, or person to steer through without obstruction
senses.definitionCN: 足够宽或足够畅通，车辆、船只或人可以驾驶穿过而不受阻
senses.example: The flooded tunnel was still navigable for small trucks.
senses.exampleCN: 积水的隧道对小货车来说仍可通行。
senses.why: Once able to carries a ship, the same logic lets it carry any vessel or vehicle through a space.
senses.whyCN: 既然「能够」可以承载船只，同样的逻辑就能扩展到任何运载工具，于是指任何空间都可驾驶穿过。

senses.title: Passable on foot
senses.definition: of a difficult place such as a jungle, marsh, or crowd, able to be walked or moved through
senses.definitionCN: 指丛林、沼泽或人群等难以通过的地方，可以用步行或移动的方式穿过
senses.example: After weeks of rain, the track was barely navigable on foot.
senses.exampleCN: 连下几周雨之后，那条小路几乎无法步行通过。
senses.why: A person also steers a course, so a place someone can pick a way through becomes navigable.
senses.whyCN: 人也在「驾船前行」般地择路，于是任何能让人找到出路的地方都可称作 navigable。

senses.title: Easy to browse or use
senses.definition: of a website, document, or interface, easy to move around in and find what you need
senses.definitionCN: 指网站、文档或界面，容易在其中来回移动并找到所需内容
senses.example: The site is clean and easy to navigate for new visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个网站界面干净，新来的访客也很容易浏览。
senses.why: Moving through pages is imagined as steering through water, so a clear design is a navigable space.
senses.whyCN: 在页面之间移动被想象成在水上驾船，因此清晰的设计就是一种「可航行的空间」。

senses.title: Legally open for passage
senses.definition: open by law or treaty to ships or travellers, as a body of water or a border route
senses.definitionCN: 依法律或条约向船只、行人开放的水域或边境通道
senses.example: The treaty keeps the strait navigable for all nations.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约使这条海峡对所有国家保持通航。
senses.why: Whether water can carry a ship is decided not only by depth but also by who is allowed to use it.
senses.whyCN: 水面能否行船，不只取决于水深，也取决于谁被允许使用它，于是义项延伸到法律层面的开放。

senses.title: Workable in practice
senses.definition: of a plan, argument, or set of rules, clear enough to work through and follow
senses.definitionCN: 指计划、论证或规则清晰到能够据此推进和遵循
senses.example: Her proposal was detailed enough to be navigable by a small team.
senses.exampleCN: 她的提案足够细致，小团队也能照着推进。
senses.why: The journey metaphor widens again: a route that can be sailed is a course of action that can be followed.
senses.whyCN: 旅程隐喻再次扩展：能航行通过的路线，也就是可以照着走的行动路线。

senses.title: Of a horse, able to be ridden
senses.definition: of a horse, able to be steered and ridden safely
senses.definitionCN: 指马匹能够被安全地驾驭和骑乘
senses.example: The young mare was calm and navigable for novices.
senses.exampleCN: 这匹小母马性情平稳，新手也能驾驭。
senses.why: Riding is steering a living vehicle, so an animal that can be controlled is navigable in this older sense.
senses.whyCN: 骑马就是在驾驭一个活的交通工具，因此能被控制的动物在这个较旧的用法里也是 navigable。

senses.title: Of a mind, able to follow
senses.definition: of speech or writing, clear enough for a listener or reader to follow the line of thought
senses.definitionCN: 指言谈或文字清晰，听众或读者能够跟住思路
senses.example: His lecture was dense but navigable for anyone who took notes.
senses.exampleCN: 他的讲座内容密集，但只要记笔记，思路还是跟得上的。
senses.why: Finally the journey is inside the mind: a route of thought that a reader can trace is navigable.
senses.whyCN: 最后旅程走进了头脑：读者能够循迹而行的思路之路，就是 navigable。

intro.en: Navigable joins the Latin root navis, ship, with the suffix -able, able to, and its nearest relative is the verb navigate, to steer a course.
intro.cn: navigable 由拉丁语词根 navis（船）加后缀 -able（能够）构成，最亲近的同族词是动词 navigate（航行、导航）。

items.en: A reconstructed root behind Latin navis relates to the idea of a boat or ship.
items.cn: 拉丁语 navis 背后有一个重构形式词根，与「船」的概念相关。

items.en: Navis means ship, and navigare means to sail, literally to drive a ship.
items.cn: navis 意为船，navigare 意为航行，字面是「驾驶船只」。

items.en: The adjective navigabilis is formed from navigare plus -bilis, able to be.
items.cn: 形容词 navigabilis 由 navigare 加 -bilis（能够被……）构成。

items.en: English begins to use the word for rivers and channels open to shipping.
items.cn: 英语开始用这个词描述可供船只通行的河流与水道。

items.en: Engineering and law extend the word to tunnels, passes, and open waterways.
items.cn: 工程与法律领域把该词扩展到隧道、山口和开放水道。

items.en: Digital use applies the word to websites and interfaces that are easy to move around in.
items.cn: 数字时代又把该词用于指易于在其间穿行浏览的网站与界面。

note.en: Navigable pairs with its verb navigate and with water words such as passable and navigational, and it is opposed to impassable.
note.cn: navigable 与动词 navigate 以及 passable、navigational 等水域词同时出现，它的反义是 impassable。

entries.definition: to steer a course or find the way
relating to the guidance of ships or aircraft
entries.definitionCN: 与船只、飞机导航相关的

entries.definition: the quality of being navigable
able to be travelled along or crossed
impossible to travel along or cross
entries.definitionCN: 无法通过的；不能通行的

entries.definition: having little depth, so hard for large ships
entries.definitionCN: 浅的；因为太浅而难以行大船

normalIntro.en: Navigable is built from navis, ship, and the suffix -able, so read it as able to carry a ship.
normalIntro.cn: navigable 由 navis（船）与 -able（能够）拼成，可以读作「能承载一只船的」。

normal.en: A navigable river is one deep and wide enough for boats.
normal.cn: navigable river 指足够宽深、能让船通过的河流。

normal.en: Keep the waterway navigable means keep it clear of silt and ice.
normal.cn: keep the waterway navigable 就是保持水道不被淤泥和冰堵住。

normal.en: The verb navigate is the closest family word and shares the ship root.
normal.cn: 动词 navigate 是最亲近的同族词，共享「船」这一词根。

normal.en: Impassable is the direct opposite of navigable for a route.
normal.cn: 就路线而言，impassable 是 navigable 的直接反义。

normal.en: A user friendly website is described as easy to navigate or navigable.
normal.cn: 用户友好的网站会被形容为 easy to navigate 或 navigable。

abstract.en: Picture a dredger lifting mud so a barge slips through the channel.
abstract.cn: 想象清淤船把淤泥挖走，驳船于是顺水滑过河道。

abstract.en: Imagine a clear path cut through thick reeds toward open water.
abstract.cn: 想象在茂密苇丛中开出通往开阔水面的一条通道。

abstract.en: See a reader tracing a clear line of argument with a finger.
abstract.cn: 想象读者用手指顺着一条清晰的论证线索往下走。

examples.en: Only a short stretch of the canal is still navigable.
examples.cn: 这条运河只剩下短短一段仍可通航。

examples.en: Engineers dredged the harbour mouth to keep it navigable.
examples.cn: 工程师疏浚了港口入口，使其保持可通航。

examples.en: The new library app is far more navigable than the old website.
examples.cn: 新的图书馆应用比旧网站好用得多，浏览起来顺畅得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拿位搁」——船要「拿」到合适的「位」置才能「搁」下通行，记作可通航；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 navis（船）+ navigare（驾驶船只、航行）→ navigabilis（可航行的）→ 英语 navigable，核心义「能够承载船只前行」。

sensesIntro.en: This word starts with water deep enough for a ship, widens to any space a vehicle or person can cross, and ends as a metaphor for websites, plans, and lines of thought that can be followed.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指足够深、能让船通行水面，继而扩展到任何运载工具或人可以通过的空间，最后成为可用于网站、计划与思路等「能够走通」之事物的隐喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dredged channel in which a ship can sail all the way through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条经过疏浚、船只可以一路驶过的航道。

branches.en: The water and legal senses both ask whether a ship may and can pass.
branches.cn: 水域义与法律义都在问：船只能不能、可不可以通过。

branches.en: Land and crowd senses move the image from ships to vehicles and people.
branches.cn: 陆地与人群义把意象从船转移到车辆和人身上。

branches.en: Digital, practical, and mental senses all treat a route that can be followed.
branches.cn: 数字义、务实义与心智义都把「可以走通的路线」当作核心。

branches.en: The horse sense is the oldest riding extension of the steering image.
branches.cn: 马的义项是「驾驭」意象在骑乘上最古老的延伸。

branches.en: All three keep the -able promise that movement is possible and smooth.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都保留 -able 的承诺：移动是可行且顺畅的。

intro.en: Navigable is a Latin compound of navis, ship, the verb navigare, and the suffix -able, and English builds navigate, navigation, navigator, and navigability on the same core.
intro.cn: navigable 是拉丁语复合词，含 navis（船）、动词 navigare 与后缀 -able，英语在同一核心上构成 navigate、navigation、navigator 与 navigability。

latinIntro.en: Latin navis means ship and navigare means to sail or steer, so every English form keeps a ship at its centre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 navis 意为船，navigare 意为航行、驾驶，因此英语各形式都以「船」为中心。

items.example: Navis is the root behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: navis 是整个词族的词根。

items.meaning: to sail, to steer a ship
items.example: Navigare literally means to drive a ship.
items.exampleCN: navigare 字面意为驾驶船只。

items.example: The suffix -able turns navigare into navigable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 把 navigare 变成 navigable。

items.meaning: to steer a course or find a way
items.example: Navigate keeps the steering sense of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: navigate 保留了拉丁动词的「驾驶」义。

items.meaning: the act of steering or guiding
items.example: Navigation names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: navigation 指航行、导航这一行为。

items.example: The suffix -or marks the person.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 表示人。

items.example: Navigational equipment guides the ship.
items.exampleCN: 导航设备为船只引路。

items.example: The suffix -ity names the abstract quality.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 表示抽象属性。

items.example: The prefix im- makes impassable the opposite of navigable.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 使 impassable 成为 navigable 的反义。

definition_zh: 接近；邻近；近距离；亲密、亲近；（性质或程度上的）近似、接近
definition_en: the state of being close in space, time, relationship, or quality
core_image: 两把椅子几乎贴着放，中间只留一道窄缝
scene: 火车到站前的片刻，站台上的人都能感到列车的临近。 When the train was about to arrive, everyone on the platform could feel its nearness.
sceneCN: 这里 nearness 是「临近、接近」（第 1 个义项：时间或空间上的靠近）；句意：火车即将到站时，站台上的每个人都能感到它的临近。

pos.zh: 接近；临近；近距离
亲密；亲近
近似；接近（程度）

derivatives.zh: 基础词，构成 nearness 的形容词、副词与变化词性，义为「近的；接近」
near 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「几乎；差不多」
near 的比较级，义为「更近的」

senses.title: Closeness in space or time
senses.definition: the condition of being a short distance or a short time away from something
senses.definitionCN: 与某物相距不远，或与某个时刻相隔不久的状态
senses.example: The nearness of the storm kept everyone indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨近在眼前，大家都待在屋里。
senses.why: The root near is of unknown origin but has always meant close, and -ness turns that comparative closeness into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 词根 near 词源不明，但一直都表示「近」，后缀 -ness 把这种「靠近」变成抽象名词。

senses.title: Closeness in relationship
senses.definition: a warm and familiar closeness between people
senses.definitionCN: 人与人之间温暖而熟悉、无须客套的关系
senses.example: There was a quiet nearness between the two old friends.
senses.exampleCN: 两位老朋友之间有一种安静的亲近。
senses.why: If someone is near you in space, the heart follows the body and the same word names emotional closeness.
senses.whyCN: 若有人身体靠近你，心也会跟着靠近，于是同一个词用来命名情感上的亲近。

senses.title: Closeness in quality
senses.definition: the state of being almost the same as something else in nature, value, or degree
senses.definitionCN: 在性质、价值或程度上与另一事物几乎相同的状态
senses.example: The nearness of their results surprised the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 两组结果如此接近，让整个团队都很吃惊。
senses.why: Two things close in value are close in the same sense as two things close in space, so the image moves from distance to degree.
senses.whyCN: 数值相近就是「靠近」，与空间上靠近是同一意象，于是画面从距离转到程度。

senses.title: Closeness to an event
senses.definition: the fact of an event or moment being about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 某一事件或时刻即将发生的事实
senses.example: The nearness of the exam made the students quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 考试将近，学生们都安静下来。
senses.why: A coming event is imagined as an object moving toward you, and the gap shrinking is called nearness.
senses.whyCN: 即将发生的事被想象成一个向你移动的物体，间距缩小便称为 nearness。

senses.title: Closeness of attention
senses.definition: the quality of careful, detailed attention given to a subject
senses.definitionCN: 对某个对象给予细致、周到的观察或关注
senses.example: The drawn nearness of her field notes made them valuable.
senses.exampleCN: 她的野外笔记写得很贴近现场，因此很有价值。
senses.why: To look closely you move near, so a detailed view is literally a near view.
senses.whyCN: 要看清楚就得靠得近，因此细致的观察本质上就是「贴近的观察」。

senses.title: Nearness in place of origin
senses.definition: the degree to which two people or groups are closely related
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或两个群体在亲属关系或关联上的紧密程度
senses.example: The nearness of kinship explained their loyalty.
senses.exampleCN: 这份亲缘之近解释了他们的忠诚。
senses.why: Kin are people who stand close within the family tree, and nearness measures exactly that proximity.
senses.whyCN: 亲属就是在家族谱系中站得很近的人，nearness 正好度量这种靠近的程度。

senses.title: A narrowing gap
senses.definition: the state of getting close to someone or something, especially of a pursuer or a danger
senses.definitionCN: 正逐渐靠近某人或某物的状态，尤指追逐者或危险的逼近
senses.example: The hunters noticed the nearness of the deer before they saw it.
senses.exampleCN: 猎人还没看见鹿，就先察觉到了它的逼近。
senses.why: Nearness also names a gap that is shrinking, not only one that is already small.
senses.whyCN: nearness 不只指已经很小的间距，也指正在缩小的间距。

intro.en: Nearness is the noun of the adjective near plus the native suffix -ness, and the deeper origin of near itself is uncertain.
intro.cn: nearness 是形容词 near 加本土后缀 -ness 构成的名词，而 near 本身的更深词源来源不确定。

items.en: The comparative near comes from neah, meaning close, itself from a root nēhwaz.
items.cn: 比较级 near 来自古英语 neah（近），其更早词根为 nēhwaz。

items.en: Neah already covered both distance in space and closeness in kinship.
items.cn: neah 已经同时涵盖空间距离与亲属上的亲近。

items.en: Near settled into modern spelling and meaning as a form of the old comparative of nigh.
items.cn: near 定型为现代拼写与词义，它本是 nigh 的旧比较级形式。

items.en: The suffix -ness forms the abstract noun nearness from the adjective.
items.cn: 后缀 -ness 由形容词构成抽象名词 nearness。

items.en: Nearness extends to time, degree, kinship, and careful observation.
items.cn: nearness 扩展到时间、程度、亲缘与细致观察等领域。

note.en: Nearness is the closeness noun of near, and it sits beside closeness, proximity, and intimacy while close looks at them.
note.cn: nearness 是 near 的「接近」名词，与 closeness、proximity、intimacy 同行，对手是最远的距离。

entries.definition: a short distance away
almost, but not quite
the comparative of near
the state of being close in space or feeling
nearness in space or time
the state of being far away

normalIntro.en: Nearness is simply near plus -ness, so every thing or feeling that can be called near has a nearness.
normalIntro.cn: nearness 就是 near 加 -ness，凡是能称作 near 的人、物或感受，都各有一个 nearness。

normal.en: Nearness in time is common with events such as exams and storms.
normal.cn: nearness in time 常与考试、暴风雨等事件搭配。

normal.en: The nearness of the sea meaning is a collocation drawn from place.
normal.cn: the nearness of the sea 这类搭配直接取自地点。

normal.en: Nearly is near plus -ly and means almost, so keep the two apart.
normal.cn: nearly 是 near 加 -ly，意为几乎，要与 nearness 区分开。

normal.en: Nearness to is the usual pattern for distance, as in nearness to town.
normal.cn: 表示距离时惯用 nearness to 这一结构，例如 nearness to town。

normal.en: Proximity is the formal synonym and appears in scientific writing.
normal.cn: proximity 是正式的同义词，常用于科学写作。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs set so close that their arms nearly touch.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子摆得很近，扶手都快碰上了。

abstract.en: Imagine footsteps in the hall getting louder as they approach.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里的脚步声随着逼近而越来越响。

abstract.en: See two numbers on a ruler almost at the same mark.
abstract.cn: 想象尺子上两个数字几乎落在同一个刻度上。

examples.en: The nearness of the hospital makes the district popular with families.
examples.cn: 医院近在咫尺，使这个街区很受家庭欢迎。

examples.en: He spoke with a quiet nearness that put everyone at ease.
examples.cn: 他说话带着一种安静的亲近感，让大家都放松下来。

examples.en: The nearness of their opinions made debate unnecessary.
examples.cn: 他们的意见十分接近，因此没必要争论。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼尔尼斯」——名字念起来像在身边喊人，人在身「边」，就是近；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古英语 neah（近），来自更早的重构形式 nēhwaz；其比较级演变为 near，再加 -ness 构成 nearness，核心义「靠近的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Nearness begins with physical and temporal closeness, moves to closeness of feeling and quality, and widens to coming events, careful observation, and kinship.
sensesIntro.cn: nearness 从空间与时间上的靠近出发，转入情感与性质上的相近，再扩展到事件的迫近、用心的观察与血缘的亲近。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two chairs pushed so close that the gap almost disappears.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把椅子推得很近，中间几乎不留缝。

branches.en: Space and time both read closeness as a small gap.
branches.cn: 空间与时间都把靠近读作「间距很小」。

branches.en: Feeling and kinship make the gap a matter of people.
branches.cn: 情感与亲缘把这种间距变成人与人之间的关系。

branches.en: Quality is compared on the same ruler as distance.
branches.cn: 性质上的比较与距离比较共用同一把尺子。

branches.en: Looking closely is moving near, so attention has a nearness.
branches.cn: 看得仔细就是靠得近，所以专注本身也有 nearness。

branches.en: All three depend on a gap that is small or getting smaller.
branches.cn: 这三个义项都依赖一个很小或正在缩小的间距。

intro.en: Nearness is a native English word: the old adjective stem near with the suffix -ness, and the family also has nearly and nearer.
intro.cn: nearness 是本土英语词：古老的形容词词干 near 加后缀 -ness，同族还有 nearly 与 nearer。

latinIntro.en: Neither near nor nearness is Latin; the family is native Germanic, so the deeper root is a reconstructed form rather than a Latin word.
latinIntro.cn: near 与 nearness 都不是拉丁词，这一词族来自本土日耳曼语，更深词根只是重构形式，而不是某个拉丁词。

items.example: The suffix -ness turns near into nearness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 把 near 变成 nearness。

items.example: Near is the base of the noun.
items.exampleCN: near 是这个名词的基础词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms nearly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 nearly。

items.example: Nearly does not mean being close.
items.exampleCN: nearly 并不是「靠近」的意思。

items.example: The suffix -er forms nearer.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 nearer。

items.example: Nigh is the older base of near.
items.exampleCN: nigh 是 near 更早的基础形式。

items.meaningCN: 近的（nigh 是 near 的古旧同源形式）
items.example: Nigh is the older form that gave the comparative near.
items.exampleCN: nigh 是更古老的形式，它的比较级后来演变为 near。

items.example: Nearer states a shrinking gap.
items.exampleCN: nearer 表达正在缩小的间距。

definition_zh: 疏忽的；粗心大意的；不负责任的；（法律）有过失的；疏于照管的（如疏于看管孩子）
definition_en: failing to take proper care or give proper attention, especially in a way that may cause harm
core_image: 一个人背身走开，身后散落着被忽略的器物
scene: 司机开车时始终没从手机上抬起头，撞上路边的护栏，事后被认定有过失。 The driver never looked up from his phone and was found negligent after he hit the guard rail.
sceneCN: 这里 negligent 是「疏忽的、有过失的」（第 1 个义项：未尽到应有的注意义务）；句意：司机开车时始终没从手机上抬起头，撞上路边护栏后被认定有过失。

pos.zh: 疏忽的；粗心大意的
（法律）有过失的；负有责任的
不负责任的；疏于照管的

derivatives.zh: 形容词词干加名词后缀 -ence 构成，义为「疏忽；过失」
形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「疏忽地；有过失地」
同一拉丁词根的另一支，义为「忽视；照料不周」
动词 neglect 加后缀 -ful 构成，义为「疏忽的；不关心的」
同一词根加 -ible 构成，义为「可忽略不计的」

senses.title: Failing to take proper care
senses.definition: not giving proper attention or care to what one is doing
senses.definitionCN: 对自己正在做的事情没有给予应有的注意或谨慎
senses.example: The negligent driver missed the warning sign completely.
senses.exampleCN: 那名疏忽的司机完全没看见警示牌。
senses.why: Latin neglegere is neg plus legere, not picking up, so the image is a duty left lying on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neglegere 是 neg（不）加 legere（拾取），意为「没有拾起」，所以意象是被丢在地上的责任。

senses.title: Legally at fault
senses.definition: judged to have broken a legal duty of care toward others
senses.definitionCN: 被认定违反了对他人应尽的注意义务
senses.example: The hospital was found negligent in its handling of the case.
senses.exampleCN: 该医院在处理此案时被认定有过失。
senses.why: Law turns everyday carelessness into a verdict, naming the person who failed the duty negligent.
senses.whyCN: 法律把日常的粗心变成判决，把违反注意义务的人称为 negligent。

senses.title: Not looking after someone
senses.titleCN: 疏于照管的；不负责任的
senses.definition: failing to give proper care to a child or dependent in your charge
senses.definitionCN: 对自己照管的孩子或受扶养者没有给予应有的照料
senses.example: Neighbours said the guardians were negligent for leaving the child alone.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居们说监护人把孩子单独留下是疏于照管。
senses.why: The same unpicked duty applies to people: the caring work is simply left undone.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「责任没被拾起」也适用于人：照护的工作被撂在那里没做。

senses.title: Careless in style or manner
senses.definition: relaxed and casual to the point of seeming careless, in appearance, dress, or manner
senses.definitionCN: 在外表、衣着或举止上随性放松，以至于显得漫不经心
senses.example: He wore a negligent knot in his tie and laughed at the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 他领带系得很随意，还嘲笑着那些规矩。
senses.why: Physical carelessness became a fashionable ease in the eighteenth century, borrowing the word for relaxed dress.
senses.whyCN: 十八世纪的「身体上的不讲究」变成了一种时髦的洒脱，于是借这个词形容随意的穿着。

senses.title: Lacking careful attention in work
senses.definition: producing work with mistakes or gaps because proper attention was not given
senses.definitionCN: 因没有给予应有的注意而使工作出现错误或缺口
senses.example: A negligent proofreading pass let three errors through.
senses.exampleCN: 一次粗疏的校对放过了三处错误。
senses.why: Whatever the task, the failure is the same: the careless eye never picks up what it should.
senses.whyCN: 无论什么任务，失误都一样：粗心的人始终没有把该拾起的东西拾起来。

senses.title: Omitted by oversight
senses.definition: left out or unaddressed because someone failed to notice it
senses.definitionCN: 因为某人的疏忽而未被注意到、被遗漏或未予处理
senses.example: The neglected staircase was a negligent omission in the safety plan.
senses.exampleCN: 被忽视的那段楼梯是安全方案里因疏忽造成的遗漏。
senses.why: What is not picked up is also not dealt with, so a small oversight leaves a gap behind.
senses.whyCN: 没被拾起的东西也就没被处理，因此一个小小的疏忽会留下缺口。

senses.title: Not enforced or maintained
senses.titleCN: （制度、维护）执行不力以致失守的
senses.definition: of a duty, rule, or system, enforced loosely or kept in poor condition through lack of care
senses.definitionCN: 指职责、规则或系统因缺乏照管而执行松懈、维持不善
senses.example: Negligent maintenance of the fences let the sheep wander off.
senses.exampleCN: 围栏维护疏忽，让羊群走散了。
senses.why: When attention is not paid to a system, the system drifts, and we call that drift negligent.
senses.whyCN: 当没人把注意力「拾起」放到某个系统上，系统就会失序，这种失序就叫 negligent。

senses.title: Dismissive of warnings
senses.definition: showing no interest in or respect for advice after being warned
senses.definitionCN: 在被提醒之后仍对劝告不予理会、不加尊重
senses.example: Officials were negligent of the repeated safety warnings.
senses.exampleCN: 官员们对反复出现的安全警示不予理会。
senses.why: To be negligent of a warning is to leave it lying where it fell, unheeded.
senses.whyCN: negligent of 某个警告，就是把它丢在原地不加理会。

intro.en: Negligent comes from Latin neglegere, to disregard, formed from neg, not, and legere, to pick up, and it reached English through Old French.
intro.cn: negligent 来自拉丁语 neglegere（不理睬），由 neg（不）与 legere（拾取）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Legere means to gather or pick up, with neg giving not pick up.
items.cn: legere 意为收集、拾取，加上 neg 就成了「不拾取」。

items.en: Neglegere means to disregard or neglect, and neglegens describes one who neglects.
items.cn: neglegere 意为忽视、不管，neglegens 用来形容疏忽的人。

items.en: Negligentia, the abstract noun, already sits beside legal and moral complaint.
items.cn: 抽象名词 negligentia 已经与法律、道义上的指责联系在一起。

items.en: Negligent enters English from French, used for carelessness and legal fault.
items.cn: negligent 经由法语进入英语，用于表示粗心与法律上的过失。

items.en: The word also describes relaxed dress and manner as a fashionable ease.
items.cn: 该词又被用来形容随性的衣着与举止，成为一种时髦的洒脱。

items.en: Legal use fixes negligent in the law of negligence, while careless remains the everyday word.
items.cn: 法律用法把 negligent 固定在过失法领域，而日常仍多用 careless。

note.en: Negligent shares the Latin root of neglect and negligence, and it is a formal near synonym of careless.
note.cn: negligent 与 neglect、negligence 共享拉丁词根，是 careless 的正式近义词。

entries.definition: failure to take proper care
in a careless or culpable way
too small to matter, from the same root as ignore
entries.definitionCN: 可忽略不计的；与疏忽同根，但由「可被忽视」而来

entries.definition: not giving enough attention to avoid mistakes
acting with no regard for possible harm
showing careful and persistent effort

normalIntro.en: Negligent is the adjective of a duty not picked up: neg means not and legere means to pick up.
normalIntro.cn: negligent 是「没有拾起责任」的形容词：neg 表示「不」，legere 表示「拾取」。

normal.en: Be negligent in doing something is the standard pattern for a failed duty.
normal.cn: be negligent in 加动名词是表示「失职」的常用结构。

normal.en: Negligence is the noun and needs no extra letter before the -ence.
normal.cn: 名词是 negligence，接 -ence 时拼写不再多出字母。

normal.en: Negligible shares the root but means too small to notice, not careless.
normal.cn: negligible 同根，但意思是「小到不用理会」，而不是粗心。

normal.en: Diligent is the mirror opposite, built on dis plus legere, choosing a thing with care.
normal.cn: diligent 是镜像反义，由 dis 加 legere 构成，意为用心挑选。

normal.en: In law, negligent drivers face a claim of negligence.
normal.cn: 在法律上，negligent 的司机会面临 negligence（过失）之诉。

abstract.en: Picture a dropped glove in the road that nobody stoops to pick up.
abstract.cn: 想象路中间掉了一只手套，没有人弯腰去捡。

abstract.en: See a guard leaving a door unlocked on the way home.
abstract.cn: 想象一名警卫在下班回家时没锁门。

abstract.en: Imagine a report with a blank page left in by mistake.
abstract.cn: 想象一份报告里因疏忽留下一整页空白。

examples.en: The company was negligent in its handling of private data.
examples.cn: 这家公司在处理私人数据时存在疏忽。

examples.en: She was judged negligent but not criminally responsible.
examples.cn: 她被认定有过失，但不负刑事责任。

examples.en: Officials were negligent about repairs for months before the collapse.
examples.cn: 在坍塌之前的好几个月里，官员们对维修都疏于处理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那个立尽」——那个人站着却不「立」起责任，事事「尽」不到位，就是疏忽；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 neg（不）+ legere（拾取、收集）→ neglegere（不拾取、忽视）→ neglegens 及其派生 negligentia → 古法语 negligent → 英语 negligent，核心义「没有拾起应负的责任」。

sensesIntro.en: Negligent starts with simple carelessness, narrows into legal fault, and widens again to neglect of children, of style, of work, and of warnings.
sensesIntro.cn: negligent 从一般的粗心开始，收窄为法律上的过失，再扩展到对孩子、仪态、工作与警告的疏于照管。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a duty left on the ground because nobody stooped to pick it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份责任躺在地上，因为没有人弯腰去拾起。

branches.en: Failing attention in doing and in producing work share one careless eye.
branches.cn: 做事和做活儿都疏忽，用的是同一双漫不经心的眼睛。

branches.en: Law makes carelessness a formal verdict of fault.
branches.cn: 法律把粗心变成正式的过错认定。

branches.en: People and systems left uncared for drift into disrepair.
branches.cn: 无人照管的人和系统都会渐渐失序。

branches.en: Style borrows the word for a fashionable lack of care.
branches.cn: 风格象征性地借用了这个词，表示一种时髦的不讲究。

branches.en: What is unpicked is left behind, whether a duty or a warning.
branches.cn: 没被拾起的东西都会被留在原地，无论是一份责任还是一句警告。

intro.en: Negligent is built from the Latin prefix neg and the root legere, and English around it has negligence, negligently, neglect, and negligent in legal use.
intro.cn: negligent 由拉丁前缀 neg 与词根 legere 构成，英语围绕它有 negligence、negligently、neglect，并在法律用法中固定下来。

latinIntro.en: Latin neg means not and legere means to pick up or gather, so neglect and negligent both say the thing was never picked up.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neg 意为不，legere 意为拾取、收集，因此 neglect 与 negligent 都在说「那件东西从未被拾起」。

items.example: The prefix neg- gives the negating force.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 neg- 带有否定义。

items.example: Legere is the root behind neglect and diligent.
items.exampleCN: legere 是 neglect 与 diligent 背后的词根。

items.meaningCN: 表示「正在……的人或物」的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ent forms negligent from the participle.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ent 由分词构成 negligent。

items.example: The suffix -ence forms negligence.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ence 构成 negligence。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms negligently.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 negligently。

items.example: Neglect is the verb sibling of negligent.
items.exampleCN: neglect 是 negligent 的动词同族。

items.example: Negligible means small enough to ignore.
items.exampleCN: negligible 意为小到可以忽略。

items.structure: English adjective, from dis plus legere
items.example: Diligent has the same root but a positive prefix.
items.exampleCN: diligent 词根相同，前缀却是正面的。

items.example: Neglectful is the everyday adjective form.
items.exampleCN: neglectful 是日常使用的形容词形式。

definition_zh: 新古典主义的；新古典派的；新古典的
definition_en: following the orderly, balanced style of ancient Greece and Rome, either in the arts or in economic theory
core_image: 一座白色石柱大厅，柱式与山花都仿古希腊神庙，室内却摆着现代的灯
scene: 市中心那座仿古建筑有着整齐的白色立柱和三角形山花，造型取自古希腊神庙。The neoclassical building in the city centre has clean white columns and a triangular roof taken from Greek temples.
sceneCN: 这里 neoclassical 是「新古典主义的；仿古典风格的」（第 1 个义项：艺术与建筑中面向古希腊罗马的复兴风格）；句意：市中心那座新古典主义建筑有着洁净的白色立柱，屋顶的三角形造型取自希腊神庙。

pos.zh: 新古典主义的；新古典派的；仿古典风格的

derivatives.zh: neo- + classic + -ism，义为「新古典主义」，指艺术与建筑中的这一流派
neo- + classic + -ist，义为「新古典主义者」，指该流派的创作者
合成术语，义为「新古典经济学」，是现代主流经济学的核心框架之一
基础形容词，义为「古典的」，源自拉丁语 classicus，是 neoclassical 的核心部分
classic + -ism，义为「古典主义」，是 neo- 所「新」的那一派风格

senses.title: Art and architecture of the late 1700s and 1800s
senses.titleCN: 新古典主义风格（艺术与建筑）
senses.definition: showing the clear lines, balance, and calm restraint of ancient Greek and Roman art, as revived in Europe from the mid-1700s
senses.definitionCN: 呈现出古希腊罗马艺术那种线条清晰、平衡、克制的特点，这一风格自十八世纪中叶起在欧洲复兴
senses.example: The museum is housed in a neoclassical building with a long colonnade.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆设在一座带长柱廊的新古典主义建筑里。
senses.why: Neo- means new and classical means of the highest ancient rank, so the word literally names a new return to the ancient style.
senses.whyCN: neo- 意为「新」，classical 意为「属于最高等级的古典」，所以这个词字面上就是「重新回到古典」。

senses.title: Deliberately plain and symmetrical
senses.definition: described broadly as orderly, symmetrical, and free of ornament, even when not a strict historical copy
senses.definitionCN: 泛指讲究秩序、对称、没有多余装饰，即使并非严格复刻历史样式
senses.example: Her neoclassical furniture favours flat surfaces and straight lines.
senses.exampleCN: 她那套新古典风格的家具偏爱平整的台面与笔直的线条。
senses.why: Classical order prized measure over decoration, and the new version keeps that restraint as a general style.
senses.whyCN: 古典的秩序重视分寸而非堆砌装饰，复兴版本把这种克制保留为一种通行的风格。

senses.title: Music that looks back to classical forms
senses.titleCN: 音乐上回归古典形式的
senses.definition: describing music that borrows the forms and balance of the classical period, often after a freer romantic era
senses.definitionCN: 形容借用古典时期的曲式与平衡感的音乐，常出现在较自由的浪漫主义时期之后
senses.example: The composer turned neoclassical in his later symphonies.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作曲家在晚期的交响曲中转向了新古典主义。
senses.why: The arts all took turns returning to old forms, so music inherited the same label for its own revival.
senses.whyCN: 各门艺术都轮流回到旧形式，音乐便也沿用了这个标签来称呼自己的复兴。

senses.title: Economics built on markets and rational choice
senses.titleCN: 新古典经济学（以市场与理性选择为核心）
senses.definition: relating to a school of economics that treats prices and choices as the result of people acting rationally in markets
senses.definitionCN: 与一个经济学流派相关，该流派把价格与选择看作人们在市场中理性行动的结果
senses.example: The report rests on neoclassical assumptions about how buyers behave.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告建立在关于买家行为的新古典假设之上。
senses.why: The term was reused in economics for a newer version of the classical idea that markets organise themselves.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用了这个标签，指对「市场能自行调节」这一古典观念的新版表述。

senses.title: Revival of older theory in any field
senses.titleCN: 其他学科中旧理论的复兴
senses.definition: describing a renewed version of an earlier, usually formal or traditional school of thought
senses.definitionCN: 形容早先某一学派（通常是形式化或传统的）重新焕发的新版本
senses.example: Neoclassical grammar teaching came back into fashion.
senses.exampleCN: 新古典式的语法教学又流行起来。
senses.why: Whenever a discipline restates an old framework in modern terms, the same neo prefix does the work.
senses.whyCN: 任何学科只要用现代语言重述旧框架，都会用上同样的 neo 前缀。

senses.title: Grand and formal in manner
senses.definition: used loosely to describe something grand, formal, and slightly old fashioned in its manner
senses.definitionCN: 泛泛形容事物气派、正式，并带一点过时的味道
senses.example: The invitation had a neoclassical, almost imperial tone.
senses.exampleCN: 那份请柬带着新古典式、近乎帝王般的口吻。
senses.why: Ancient temples were meant to impress, and any echo of that grandeur can be called neoclassical in style.
senses.whyCN: 古希腊神庙本就用于震慑人心，凡是带有这种气派色彩的东西，在风格上都可以称作新古典。

senses.title: A modern copy with ancient rules
senses.titleCN: 按古法建造或创作的新作
senses.definition: describing something new that has been built or made strictly according to the rules of ancient design
senses.definitionCN: 形容严格依照古代设计法则新建或新作的东西
senses.example: It is a neoclassical facade on a very modern concrete frame.
senses.exampleCN: 那是在非常现代的混凝土框架上加了一层新古典式外墙。
senses.why: The new part of neo is literal here: the form is old, but the building and its materials are modern.
senses.whyCN: 这里 neo（新）是实指：样式是旧的，但建筑本身与所用材料都是现代的。

senses.title: A label for a whole period of taste
senses.titleCN: 代表某一时期审美的（历史分期用语）
senses.definition: used by historians as a period label for the taste that swept Europe from the later 1700s into the 1800s
senses.definitionCN: 历史学中用作时期标签，指十八世纪后期至十九世纪席卷欧洲的审美趣味
senses.example: The neoclassical period followed the playful decorative style before it.
senses.exampleCN: 新古典时期紧随此前那种活泼的装饰风格而来。
senses.why: A style that lasts long enough becomes an era, and the adjective turns into the name of a period.
senses.whyCN: 一种风格延续得足够久就成了一整个时代，这个形容词于是变成时期的名称。

intro.en: Neoclassical is a learned three-part formation: Greek neos, Latin classicus, and the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: neoclassical 是学术性的三段式构词：希腊语 neos、拉丁语 classicus，再加形容词词尾 -al。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written as newo means new, and it survives in Greek neos and Latin novus.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构的词根写作 newo，意为「新的」，在希腊语 neos 与拉丁语 novus 中都留下了痕迹。

items.en: Neos means new or young, and it becomes the prefix neo- in later borrowing.
items.cn: 希腊语 neos 意为新的、年轻的，后来作为前缀 neo- 进入其他语言。

items.en: Classicus describes a citizen of the highest class, and by extension a writer or work of the first rank.
items.cn: classicus 原指最高等级的公民，引申为第一流的作家或作品。

items.en: Classic and classical enter English for the works and standards of ancient Greece and Rome.
items.cn: classic 与 classical 进入英语，指古希腊罗马的作品与标准。

items.en: Neo- joins classical, and neoclassical names the revival of ancient forms after the baroque and rococo eras.
items.cn: neo- 与 classical 结合，neoclassical 用来称呼巴洛克与洛可可之后对古代形式的复兴。

items.en: Economics adopts neoclassical for a rational-choice school, and later art and music critics reuse the term.
items.cn: 二十世纪经济学用 neoclassical 指称理性选择学派，后来的艺术与音乐评论也沿用了这个词。

note.en: Neoclassical is built from classical with the Greek prefix neo-, and it is often confused with newer, modern, and revived styles.
note.cn: neoclassical 是 classical 加希腊前缀 neo- 构成，常与「新的」「现代的」「复古的」等说法混淆。

entries.definition: of ancient Greek and Roman culture
a shorter variant of the same adjective
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的缩写形式，比 neoclassical 少一个词尾

entries.definition: the neoclassical movement or style
entries.definitionCN: 新古典主义运动或风格

entries.definition: a glowing gas used in lamps
entries.definitionCN: 氖气，常用于灯管；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: someone who follows classical principles
entries.definitionCN: 古典主义者；遵循古典原则的人

entries.definition: bringing back an older style or belief
entries.definitionCN: 复兴旧风格或旧信仰的

entries.definition: following long established practice

normalIntro.en: Neoclassical is three pieces: Greek neo- for new, Latin classicus for first rank, and the suffix -al.
normalIntro.cn: neoclassical 由三段组成：希腊语 neo-（新）、拉丁语 classicus（第一流）和后缀 -al。

normal.en: Neo- appears in neolithic, neoclassical, and neologism, always adding new.
normal.cn: neo- 出现在 neolithic、neoclassical、neologism 中，总是表示「新」。

normal.en: Neoclassical architecture fills cities with columns, domes, and pediments.
normal.cn: neoclassical architecture 让城市里布满立柱、圆顶与山花。

normal.en: Neoclassical economics studies markets through rational choices.
normal.cn: neoclassical economics 用理性选择来研究市场。

normal.en: Neoclassicism is the movement and neoclassical the adjective that describes it.
normal.cn: neoclassicism 是那场运动，neoclassical 是描述它的形容词。

normal.en: Neoclassical returns to classical rules, but with the word new in front of them.
normal.cn: neoclassical 回归古典法则，但把「新」字放在前面。

abstract.en: Picture a white marble hall of columns lit by electric lamps.
abstract.cn: 想象一座白色大理石的柱廊大厅，却被电灯照亮。

abstract.en: See a Roman temple standing beside a glass office block.
abstract.cn: 想象一座罗马神庙紧挨着玻璃写字楼。

abstract.en: Think of an old rulebook copied neatly into a new notebook.
abstract.cn: 想象一本旧规则被工整地抄进新的笔记本。

examples.en: The city hall is a neoclassical building from the nineteenth century.
examples.cn: 市政厅是一座十九世纪的新古典主义建筑。

examples.en: Neoclassical economics assumes that people choose rationally.
examples.cn: 新古典经济学假设人们会理性地做选择。

examples.en: Her paintings show a neoclassical taste for order and calm.
examples.cn: 她的画作体现出新古典审美对秩序与宁静的偏爱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你欧·克拉斯·斯口」——新（neo）的古典（classical）规矩，把欧陆古风又摆回眼前，就是 neoclassical；谐音联想，非词源。

root: 希腊语 neos（新的）→ 前缀 neo- + 拉丁语 classicus（第一等的、古典的）→ classical（古典的）+ 拉丁来源形容词词尾 -al → neoclassical（新古典的），核心义「新的古典」。

sensesIntro.en: Neoclassical names a revival of ancient art first, then a general taste for order, then parallel revivals in music, economics, and other fields.
sensesIntro.cn: neoclassical 首先指艺术的古典复兴，接着泛指对秩序的偏好，最后延伸到音乐、经济学等学科的平行复兴。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an ancient temple rebuilt with modern light inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座仿古神庙，内部却亮着现代灯光。

branches.en: New copies of old temple forms are the founding sense.
branches.cn: 用古神庙形式拼出新的作品，是这个词最初的义项。

branches.en: Order, calm, and grandeur survive as a general manner of taste.
branches.cn: 秩序、宁静与气派作为一般的审美格调延续下来。

branches.en: Music borrows the label for its own return to classical forms.
branches.cn: 音乐借用这个标签，指自己回归古典形式。

branches.en: Economics and other fields restate old frameworks in new terms.
branches.cn: 经济学等学科用新术语重述旧框架。

branches.en: A lasting taste becomes a period label in history books.
branches.cn: 一种持久的趣味在史书里变成了时期名称。

intro.en: Neoclassical is a three-part borrowing: the Greek prefix neo-, the Latin root classical, and the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: neoclassical 由三部分拼合而成：希腊前缀 neo-、拉丁来源的 classical 以及形容词后缀 -al。

latinIntro.en: The core comes from Latin classicus, which meant a citizen of the highest class.
latinIntro.cn: 词的核心部分来自拉丁语 classicus，原意是最高等级的公民。

items.example: The prefix neo- forms neoclassical.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 neo- 构成 neoclassical。

items.example: Classicus is the source of classic.
items.exampleCN: classicus 是 classic 的来源。

items.example: Classic becomes classical.
items.exampleCN: classic 可以加 -al 变成 classical。

items.example: Classical art is the model to revive.
items.exampleCN: 古典艺术是被复兴的典范。

items.example: The suffix -al forms classical.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 classical。

items.example: Neoclassical joins new and classical.
items.exampleCN: neoclassical 把「新」与「古典」合在一起。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms neoclassicism.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 构成 neoclassicism。

items.example: Neoclassicism swept through Europe.
items.exampleCN: 新古典主义席卷欧洲。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms neoclassicist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成 neoclassicist。

items.example: The architect was a strict neoclassicist.
items.exampleCN: 那位建筑师是一位严格的新古典主义者。

definition_zh: 紧张；神经质；焦虑不安；拘谨
definition_en: the feeling or state of being tense, easily worried, or visibly uneasy
core_image: 一根被拉得又紧又细、一碰就颤的神经，人站在讲台前手心冒汗
scene: 轮到她上台报告时，她一遍遍抚平衣角，声音也发紧。As she rose to give her report, a wave of nervousness made her press her palms flat against her skirt.
sceneCN: 这里 nervousness 是「紧张；焦虑不安」（第 1 个义项：面对众人或重要场合时心里发紧、身体也跟着紧绷）；句意：当她站起来做报告时，一阵紧张让她把双手按在裙子上。

pos.zh: 紧张；焦虑不安；神经质；拘谨

derivatives.zh: 由名词 nerve 加形容词后缀 -ous（充满……的）构成，义为「紧张的；容易担忧的」
nervous + -ly（以……的方式），义为「紧张不安地」
基础名词，义为「神经；勇气」，是 nervous 的词根
nerve + -y，口语义为「紧张兮兮的」，英式口语还可指「厚脸皮的」
un- + nerve + -ing，由动词 unnerve 构成，义为「使人发怵的」

senses.title: Tension in the body
senses.definition: a physical feeling of tightness and restlessness, as when the hands shake or the voice goes tight
senses.definitionCN: 身体发紧、坐立不安的感觉，如手发抖、声音发紧
senses.example: His nervousness showed in the way he kept fidgeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直在动来动去，暴露出内心的紧张。
senses.why: The noun comes from nerve, a strand of the body that is strung tight and carries every signal at once.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 nerve（神经），神经绷得又紧又细，把一切信号同时放大，身体于是跟着发紧。

senses.title: Worry before an event
senses.definition: uneasy apprehension about something that is going to happen, such as an exam or an interview
senses.definitionCN: 对即将发生的事情（如考试或面试）感到不安和担忧
senses.example: Nervousness before the interview kept her awake all night.
senses.exampleCN: 面试前的紧张让她一夜没睡。
senses.why: Nerves react before a threat arrives, so the noun shifts from the body to the mind already waiting for trouble.
senses.whyCN: 神经在危险真正到来之前就作出反应，于是这个词从身体感受移到「提前担心」的心理状态。

senses.title: A tense disposition
senses.definition: a lasting tendency to be jumpy, easily startled, and quick to worry
senses.definitionCN: 一种持续的、容易受惊、动不动就担忧的性格倾向
senses.example: Her nervousness made even small decisions exhausting.
senses.exampleCN: 她的神经质让她连做小决定都精疲力尽。
senses.why: If nerves tug at every moment, the trait stops being a passing episode and becomes part of a person.
senses.whyCN: 如果神经时时刻刻都紧绷，这种紧张就不再是一时一刻的情绪，而成了人身上的恒定特质。

senses.title: Being shy and awkward
senses.definition: a shy, self-conscious manner in social situations, often shown by avoiding eye contact
senses.definitionCN: 在社交场合中害羞、不自在的样子，常表现为回避眼神接触
senses.example: There was a shy nervousness in the way she introduced herself.
senses.exampleCN: 她自我介绍时带着一种害羞的拘谨。
senses.why: Being watched makes the nerves prick, so the word also names the awkwardness of standing in front of others.
senses.whyCN: 被人注视时神经会一阵阵发刺，于是这个词也用来指站在众人面前的局促不安。

senses.title: Situational unease
senses.definition: mild general unease in a particular setting, such as a silent classroom or a dark street
senses.definitionCN: 在特定环境中（如安静的教室或昏暗的街道）产生的轻微整体不安
senses.example: A vague nervousness settled over the empty hall.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的大厅里弥漫着一种莫名的不安。
senses.why: Nerves respond to a whole setting rather than a single cause, so the noun can name a mood hanging over a place.
senses.whyCN: 神经会把整个环境都当成刺激源，而不是只对一个原因起反应，所以这个词也能指弥漫在某个场所里的气氛。

senses.title: Eagerness with nerves
senses.definition: a mixture of excitement and jittery energy, as before a performance or a race
senses.definitionCN: 表演或比赛前兴奋与慌乱交织的状态
senses.example: The swimmers bounced on their toes, filled with nervousness and joy.
senses.exampleCN: 游泳运动员踮着脚蹦跳，既紧张又欢快。
senses.why: The same tight string can hum with eagerness, so nervousness can also carry a positive, charged sense.
senses.whyCN: 同一根绷紧的弦也能奏出兴奋的声音，因此 nervousness 有时也带有正面、充满能量的意味。

senses.title: Unease in a group
senses.definition: a shared, contagious unease spreading through a crowd, team, or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在人群、团队或会议中蔓延开来的紧张气氛
senses.example: You could feel the nervousness spreading through the audience.
senses.exampleCN: 你能感觉到紧张情绪在观众中蔓延。
senses.why: One set of nerves affects the next, so the noun grows from one person into a group mood.
senses.whyCN: 一个人的紧张会传给下一个人，于是这个词就从个人状态扩展为群体氛围。

senses.title: Anxiety seen as disorder
senses.definition: an older or medical-sounding term for a state of chronic mental anxiety
senses.definitionCN: 较旧或带医学术语味道的说法，指长期性的精神焦虑状态
senses.example: Doctors of that era spoke of nervousness rather than anxiety.
senses.exampleCN: 那个年代的医生说的是 nervousness，而不是焦虑。
senses.why: Older medicine blamed the nerves for what we now call anxiety, and the noun still echoes that usage.
senses.whyCN: 旧时的医学把如今称为「焦虑」的症状归咎于神经，这一用法至今仍留在这个词里。

intro.en: Nervousness is English building at home: Latin nervus and the English word nerve plus the adjective suffix -ous and the noun suffix -ness.
intro.cn: nervousness 是英语本土组合出来的词：拉丁语 nervus 与英语 nerve，加上形容词后缀 -ous 和名词后缀 -ness。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written as sneh1wri means a sinew or bowstring.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构的词根写作 sneh1wri，意为筋、腱或弓弦。

items.en: Nervus means a sinew, tendon, or thong, and by extension strength.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、腱或皮条，引申为力量。

items.en: English learns nerve from Latin and by the early 1600s means a sinew or a cord, giving the string image.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语借入 nerve，到十七世纪初指筋腱或绳索，由此获得「绷紧的弦」这一意象。

items.en: By the 1600s nerve also means the body part that carries feeling, the nerve, and from it comes the sense of courage.
items.cn: 十七世纪时 nerve 又指传递感觉的身体组织，即「神经」，并由此引申出「勇气」的意思。

items.en: Nervous, formed with -ous, first means sinewy, and then describes someone whose nerves are easily upset.
items.cn: 由 nervous 加 -ous 构成的形容词最初意为「筋脉发达的」，后来转而形容神经容易受刺激的人。

items.en: Ness creates the abstract noun nervousness, naming the state rather than the person.
items.cn: nervousness 由后缀 -ness 把这个形容词变成抽象名词，指状态而不是指人。

note.en: Nervousness sits with nerve, nervous, and nervously, and competes with anxiety, unease, and tension.
note.cn: nervousness 与 nerve、nervous、nervously 同族，并与焦虑、不安、紧绷等词相邻。

entries.definition: tense or easily worried
in a tense or uneasy way
a fibre that carries feeling, or courage
a strong feeling of worry or dread
a mild feeling that something is wrong
a state of being stretched tight or strained

normalIntro.en: Nervousness is nerve plus ous plus ness: a bundle of tight nerves turned into an abstract state.
normalIntro.cn: nervousness 就是 nerve 加 ous 再加 ness：一团绷紧的神经，被说成一种状态。

normal.en: Nerve is the string, -ous makes it full of string, and -ness names the result.
normal.cn: nerve 是弦，-ous 表示「充满弦的」，-ness 再把这种性质变成名词。

normal.en: Overcome nervousness is the standard phrase for getting past stage fright.
normal.cn: overcome nervousness 是克服怯场的标准说法。

normal.en: A wave of nervousness sweeps over a crowd before a big match.
normal.cn: 大赛开始前，一阵紧张会扫过整个人群。

normal.en: Compare nervous and nervously: the adjective describes the person, the adverb the action.
normal.cn: 对比 nervous 与 nervously：形容词修饰人，副词修饰动作。

normal.en: Nervous once meant sinewy, so the same word still carries a tight, cord-like picture.
normal.cn: nervous 最初意为筋脉发达的，所以这个词至今仍带着绳子绷紧的画面。

abstract.en: Picture fingers pulling a guitar string until it hums and shakes.
abstract.cn: 想象手指把吉他弦越拉越紧，弦开始震颤作响。

abstract.en: See a speaker gripping the edge of a lectern, knuckles white.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲者抓着讲台边缘，指节发白。

abstract.en: Think of a room where everyone is holding their breath at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子里所有人同时屏住呼吸。

examples.en: She speaks in public without any sign of nervousness.
examples.cn: 她在公开场合讲话时没有任何紧张的迹象。

examples.en: Nervousness before the exam made his hands cold.
examples.cn: 考前的紧张让他的双手冰凉。

examples.en: The coach taught the team to use nervousness as energy.
examples.cn: 教练教队员把紧张当作能量来用。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内窝死 · 耐斯」——心里越窝越紧、神经直发颤，就是 nervousness；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 nervus（筋、腱、弓弦）→ 英语 nerve（筋；神经；勇气）→ nervous（紧张的，-ous「充满」）→ nervousness（-ness 抽象名词后缀），核心义「绷紧的弦」。

sensesIntro.en: Nervousness starts as a tight body feeling, spreads into worry about coming events, then into a disposition, and finally into moods of a place or a group.
sensesIntro.cn: nervousness 从身体的发紧出发拓展：先是事前的担忧，然后是持久的性情，最后还能指某个场所或群体的整体气氛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a nerve pulled tight like a string, trembling at the slightest touch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根像琴弦一样绷紧的神经，轻轻一碰就颤动。

branches.en: The trembling body and the worrying mind are the two everyday senses.
branches.cn: 身体的颤抖与心里的担忧是日常最主要的两个义项。

branches.en: A lasting trait is the nerves trembling all the time.
branches.cn: 持久特质就是神经一直在颤。

branches.en: Shyness and stage excitement are the same tension seen from outside and inside.
branches.cn: 拘谨与赛前的兴奋，是同一份紧张从外面看和从里面看。

branches.en: Unease can fill a setting or a whole crowd.
branches.cn: 不安可以填满一个场所，也可以传遍一群人。

branches.en: The medical sense keeps the oldest blame on the nerves.
branches.cn: 医学义项仍保留着把问题归咎于神经的旧说法。

intro.en: Nervousness is built from nerve plus -ous and -ness, two of the most productive English suffixes.
intro.cn: nervousness 由 nerve 加 -ous 与 -ness 构成，这两个都是英语高产的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin nervus means a sinew or thong, and it also gives the English word nerve.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nervus 意为筋、腱或皮条，英语 nerve 即由此而来。

items.example: Nerve gives the base meaning.
items.exampleCN: nerve 提供基础含义。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ous forms nervous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 nervous。

items.example: Nervous adds the adjective sense.
items.exampleCN: nervous 增加形容词义。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms nervousness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 nervousness。

items.example: Nervousness is the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: nervousness 是抽象名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms nervously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 nervously。

items.example: She smiled nervously.
items.exampleCN: 她紧张地笑了笑。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unnerve.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unnerve。

items.meaningCN: 使人失去信心的；令人发怵的
items.example: The silence was unnerving.
items.exampleCN: 那片寂静令人发怵。

definition_zh: 令人恼火的；麻烦缠身的；棘手的
definition_en: annoying and irritating to deal with, like a plant covered in stinging hairs
core_image: 伸手去拔一丛荨麻，手背立刻被细小的刺毛扎得又痛又痒
scene: 项目审批的文件在几个部门之间来回转了半年，每位经办人都叹气说难办。The nettlesome paperwork kept circling between offices, and every clerk who touched it sighed.
sceneCN: 这里 nettlesome 是「棘手的；令人恼火的」（第 1 个义项：事情像荨麻一样一碰就扎手，让人又烦又难处理）；句意：那份让人恼火的文件在各个办公室之间转来转去，每个碰过它的职员都叹气。

pos.zh: 令人恼火的；麻烦缠身的；棘手的

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「荨麻」，即叶片布满蜇毛的植物；也可作动词表「激怒」
nettle + -ed，义为「被激怒的；恼火的」，由动词 nettle 的分词而来
合成名词，义为「大荨麻」，是 nettle 最常见的具体指称
合成名词，义为「荨麻疹」，因皮肤出现类似蜇伤的疹子而得名

senses.title: Irritating to deal with
senses.definition: annoying and hard to handle, making people impatient or angry each time they try
senses.definitionCN: 令人厌烦又难以处理，每次下手都让人不耐烦或恼火
senses.example: Fixing the wiring turned out to be a nettlesome job.
senses.exampleCN: 修电线最后成了一件又烦又棘手的事。
senses.why: Nettle is a plant that stings anyone who grabs it, so the suffix -some turns the sting into a quality of a task.
senses.whyCN: nettle 是荨麻，谁去抓它就会被蜇，后缀 -some 让这种「扎手」变成事情本身的属性。

senses.title: Causing constant small pains
senses.definition: producing repeated minor hurts or setbacks rather than one big disaster
senses.definitionCN: 带来一连串小伤害或小挫折，而不是一次大灾难
senses.example: The nettlesome delays added up to a lost week.
senses.exampleCN: 这些不断冒出来的小延误累积起来，白白耽误了一周。
senses.why: The nettle leaves many tiny hairs that each sting once, so the word suggests many small pricks rather than one blow.
senses.whyCN: 荨麻的细毛一根根各蜇一下，于是这个词暗示的是一连串细小的刺痛，而非一次重击。

senses.title: A difficult decision
senses.definition: describing a choice or question where every option has a painful drawback
senses.definitionCN: 形容每种选择都带有难受代价的决定或问题
senses.example: They face a nettlesome choice between jobs and family.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在工作和家庭之间面临一个棘手的选择。
senses.why: Every branch of the nettle stings, just as every option in a hard decision costs something.
senses.whyCN: 荨麻的每个方向都有刺，正如难题里每个选项都要付出代价。

senses.title: Annoying people
senses.definition: describing a person or their behaviour as provoking and hard to put up with
senses.definitionCN: 形容某人或其行为惹人厌烦、难以忍受
senses.example: His nettlesome questions irritated the whole panel.
senses.exampleCN: 他那些惹人烦的问题让整个评审组都很恼火。
senses.why: Since nettle as a verb means to provoke, -some turns it into the quality of provoking others.
senses.whyCN: 动词 nettle 本就有「激怒」之意，加上 -some 就变成「爱惹人」的性质。

senses.title: Tricky to touch
senses.definition: sensitive and dangerous to approach, like a subject best left alone
senses.definitionCN: 敏感而危险，最好别去碰，像一块不能触碰的禁区
senses.example: It is a nettlesome subject that few reporters dare to raise.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一个很少有记者敢提的刺手话题。
senses.why: The sting comes only from touching, so the word also names things that punish anyone who reaches for them.
senses.whyCN: 荨麻的刺痛只在触碰时发生，所以这个词也指「谁碰谁就吃亏」的事物。

senses.title: Growing without being asked
senses.definition: spreading and returning again and again, like weeds that refuse to stay gone
senses.definitionCN: 不断蔓延、反复冒回来，像除不尽的杂草
senses.example: Nettlesome weeds kept coming back in the flower bed.
senses.exampleCN: 花坛里那些除不尽的杂草一次次长回来。
senses.why: Nettles spread by strong underground roots, so the image also carries the idea of trouble that keeps regrowing.
senses.whyCN: 荨麻靠发达的根茎蔓延，因此这个词也带有「麻烦剪不断、理还乱」的意思。

senses.title: Not quite stinging in a medical sense
senses.definition: describing a feeling or symptom that lightly stings or prickles, used in mostly figurative writing
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种轻微刺痛或刺痒的感觉，多用于比喻性文字
senses.example: A nettlesome itch spread along his forearm.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵刺痒顺着他的前臂蔓延开来。
senses.why: The literal plant sting survives as a figure for any prickling discomfort, even without real nettles.
senses.whyCN: 非字面的荨麻蜇痛保留为一种比喻，用来指任何针刺般的轻微不适。

senses.title: Troublesome in public life
senses.definition: describing a policy, dispute, or rule that keeps causing friction in public debate
senses.definitionCN: 形容政策、纠纷或法规在公共讨论中不断引发摩擦
senses.example: Tax reform remains a nettlesome issue in every election.
senses.exampleCN: 税制改革在每次选举中都是一个刺手的老问题。
senses.why: When many people grab the same problem and each gets stung, the word suits quarrels that never quite end.
senses.whyCN: 当众人争相去处理同一个问题、人人被扎一下，这个词就适合形容那些始终难以了结的争执。

intro.en: Nettlesome is a native English compound of the plant name nettle and the adjective suffix -som, now spelled -some.
intro.cn: nettlesome 是英语本土构成的词，由植物名 nettle（荨麻）与形容词后缀 -som（今写作 -some）组成。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written as ned means to tie or bind, and the plant name is often connected with the twisted stem.
items.cn: 一般认为可重构的词根写作 ned，意为捆、系；植物名常被认为与其拧络的茎有关。

items.en: Netele names the stinging plant, spelled with an e between -t- and -l-.
items.cn: 古英语 netele 指这种会蜇人的植物，在 t 与 l 之间多一个 e。

items.en: Netele loses the middle vowel and settles into the modern shape nettle.
items.cn: 中古英语时期中间的元音脱落，拼写固定为 nettle。

items.en: Nettlesome uses the old Germanic suffix -som, now spelled -some, meaning of the kind or characterized by, as in burdensome and tiresome.
items.cn: nettlesome 用到的后缀 -som 来自日耳曼语，意为「具有……性质的」，与 handsome、burdensome 同源。

items.en: Nettle as a verb means to sting or provoke, and the plant name gives the sting image a grammar of its own.
items.cn: nettle 作动词时意为蜇、激怒，植物名由此拥有了自己的动词用法。

items.en: Nettlesome appears as an adjective meaning irritating and troublesome, most often in formal or journalistic writing.
items.cn: nettlesome 作为形容词出现，意为令人恼火、麻烦棘手的，多见于正式或新闻文字。

note.en: Nettlesome stays close to the plant nettle and its family, and it sits near words for annoying and difficult things.
note.cn: nettlesome 与植物 nettle 及其词族关系紧密，同时与表示「烦人」「棘手」的词相邻。

normalIntro.en: Nettlesome is nettle plus some: a thing that has the nettle quality, ready to sting.
normalIntro.cn: nettlesome 就是 nettle 加 some：具有荨麻性质的东西，随时会蜇人。

normal.en: Nettle is the plant, and stinging nettle is its most common full name.
normal.cn: nettle 是植物，stinging nettle（大荨麻）是它最常见的全称。

normal.en: To nettle someone is to annoy them, so nettled means annoyed.
normal.cn: nettle 某人就是激怒某人，所以 nettled 意为「被激怒的」。

normal.en: The suffix -some also appears in troublesome and burdensome.
normal.cn: 后缀 -some 也出现在 troublesome 与 burdensome 里。

normal.en: A nettlesome problem keeps stinging each time someone tries to fix it.
normal.cn: a nettlesome problem 就是每次有人想解决都会被「扎」一下的问题。

normal.en: Nettle rash names the itchy red bumps caused by nettle stings.
normal.cn: nettle rash 用荨麻蜇伤后的红疹来命名荨麻疹。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener reaching into a clump of green leaves and pulling back a red hand.
abstract.cn: 想象园丁伸手伸进一丛绿叶，随即缩回了一只通红的手。

abstract.en: See a tangled wire that shocks you every time you touch it.
abstract.cn: 想象一根缠成一团的电线，每碰一次就被电一下。

abstract.en: Think of a weed that grows back the day after you pull it out.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵你刚拔掉的杂草，隔天又长回来。

examples.en: Finding a fair answer to the complaint was nettlesome.
examples.cn: 为这起投诉找一个公平的答复相当棘手。

examples.en: The new software has a few nettlesome quirks.
examples.cn: 这款新软件有几个令人恼火的小毛病。

examples.en: The whole project became nettlesome once the budget shrank.
examples.cn: 预算一缩减，整个项目就变得麻烦缠身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「捏疼 · 撒姆」——伸手一捏就被扎疼，捏得直皱眉，就是 nettlesome（令人恼火的）；谐音联想，非词源。

root: 古英语 netele（荨麻，源自可重构词根 ned「捆绑」）+ 日耳曼语后缀 -som（今 -some，意为「具有……性质的」）→ nettlesome（像荨麻一样扎手的、恼人的）。

sensesIntro.en: Nettlesome begins with a literal nettle sting and then widens: repeated small pains, hard choices, annoying people, sensitive subjects, weeds that return, and public quarrels.
sensesIntro.cn: nettlesome 从荨麻蜇人的实感出发，逐步扩展：反复的小刺痛、难选的决定、烦人的人和事、碰不得的话题、除不尽的杂草，以及公共生活中难以了结的争执。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching for nettles and drawing back from the sting.
core.cn: 核心意象：伸手去抓荨麻，被扎得缩回手来。

branches.en: The main sense: things and people that irritate.
branches.cn: 主要义项：令人恼火的事与人。

branches.en: Small repeated pains and prickle-like discomfort keep the literal sting alive.
branches.cn: 反复的小痛与刺痒感保留了字面上的蜇痛。

branches.en: Hard choices and untouchable subjects are nettles nobody wants to grab.
branches.cn: 难题与禁区，都是谁都不想伸手去抓的荨麻。

branches.en: Roots that keep regrowing give the sense of trouble that will not stay away.
branches.cn: 不断复生的根茎带来「麻烦去而复返」的意味。

branches.en: Public quarrels repeat the pattern on a national scale.
branches.cn: 公共争执把这种模式放大到国家层面。

intro.en: Nettlesome joins the Old English plant name nettle with the descriptive suffix -some.
intro.cn: nettlesome 把本土植物名 nettle 与描述性后缀 -some 结合在一起。

latinIntro.en: This is a Germanic and Old English word, not a Latin one, and Latin kept its own name for nettle, urtica.
latinIntro.cn: 这是日耳曼语与古英语的词，并非拉丁语来源；拉丁语对荨麻有自己的称呼 urtica。

items.example: Nettle is the base word.
items.exampleCN: nettle 是基础词。

items.example: His remarks nettled her.
items.exampleCN: 他的话激怒了她。

items.example: A nettling remark spoiled the mood.
items.exampleCN: 一句恼人的话破坏了气氛。

items.example: The suffix -some forms nettlesome.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -some 构成 nettlesome。

items.example: Nettlesome describes a trying problem.
items.exampleCN: nettlesome 描述令人头疼的问题。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms nettled.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 nettled。

items.example: She looked nettled by the question.
items.exampleCN: 她似乎因这个问题而恼火。

items.example: Trouble gives troublesome.
items.exampleCN: trouble 构成 troublesome。

items.example: Troublesome shares the -some suffix.
items.exampleCN: troublesome 共享 -some 后缀。

items.example: Burdensome is another -some adjective.
items.exampleCN: burdensome 是另一个以 -some 结尾的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms nettling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 nettling。
