definition_zh: 神经痛（沿神经走向发作的剧烈疼痛）；一种以剧痛为特征的病症
definition_en: sharp, severe pain that follows the course of a nerve, or any disease marked by such pain
core_image: 一条神经像一根通了电流的细线，整条线路都在发烫刺痛
scene: 深夜，老人捂着眼睛从床上坐起，一阵刀割般的剧痛沿着半边脸窜到太阳穴。She blamed her dental work, but the doctor said the flashes across her cheek were neuralgia.
sceneCN: 这里 neuralgia 是「神经痛」（第 1 个义项：沿神经走向发作的、针刺或刀割般的剧痛）；句意为她以为是牙科治疗引起的，医生却说脸颊上那一道道闪痛是神经痛。图中可辨识物件：台灯、止痛药瓶、捂着半张脸的手。

pos.zh: 医学名词：神经痛；尤指三叉神经痛、坐骨神经痛一类的神经源性剧痛

collocations.zh: 患神经痛；饱受神经痛之苦

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「神经痛的；神经源性疼痛的」
同含希腊 neuron 词根，但后缀来自另一条词根，义为「神经官能症」，与神经痛并非同族
共享 neuron 词根，由「神经」加「研究」后缀构成，义为「神经病学」
共享 neuron 词根，义为「神经科医生」，是常处置 nerve pain 的人

senses.title: Sharp pain along a nerve
senses.definition: a sudden, sharp and often stabbing pain that runs along the path of a nerve
senses.definitionCN: 沿神经走向突然发作、尖锐如刺的疼痛
senses.example: The pain shot up his jaw in brief, electric flashes: that was neuralgia, not toothache.
senses.exampleCN: 疼痛沿下颌短促地电击般窜上来，那是神经痛，不是牙痛。
senses.why: Greek neuron meant a cord or sinew, and algos meant pain, so at its narrowest a neuralgia is a pain situated along a nerve cord rather than in an organ or a wound.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 neuron 指「索、筋、神经」，algos 指「疼痛」，所以最狭义的神经痛就是痛在神经索上、而非痛在某个器官或伤口里。

senses.title: A named medical disorder
senses.titleCN: 作为一种病症的神经痛
senses.definition: a recognised disease, such as trigeminal neuralgia or postherpetic neuralgia, whose main feature is nerve pain
senses.definitionCN: 一种被医学命名的疾病，如三叉神经痛或疱疹后神经痛，其主要特征就是神经源性疼痛
senses.example: Postherpetic neuralgia can persist for months after a shingles rash has faded.
senses.exampleCN: 带状疱疹的皮疹消退后，疱疹后神经痛仍可能持续数月。
senses.why: Once doctors could name the nerve involved, the word stopped describing a symptom and started labelling a diagnosis that patients carry for years.
senses.whyCN: 当医生能说出具体是哪条神经受累之后，这个词就从描述一个症状，变成给一个病人要背负多年的诊断贴标签。

senses.title: The classical non-cord sense
senses.titleCN: 古典时期「与腱有关的痛」
senses.definition: the older clinical use in which neuralgia referred to pain associated with tendons, ligaments and fibrous tissue rather than with nerve trunks
senses.definitionCN: 较早的临床用法：指与腱、韧带等纤维组织有关的疼痛，而不是神经干本身的疼痛
senses.example: In early nineteenth-century writing, neuralgia could name a fibrous pain later renamed fibrositis.
senses.exampleCN: 在十九世纪初的文献里，神经痛还可指后来改称纤维组织炎的纤维性疼痛。
senses.why: Neuron also covered sinews and tendons, so early clinicians used the word for fibrous pain, and only later did the nerve-trunk sense win.
senses.whyCN: neuron 在古代还兼指筋与腱，所以早期医生用这个词指纤维性疼痛；「神经干」义是后来才占上风的。

senses.title: Figurative nerve-pain
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：刺入神经的痛
senses.definition: a sharp, stabbing mental or emotional pain, described as though it ran along a nerve
senses.definitionCN: 把尖锐、突如其来的精神或情感痛苦比作沿神经窜走的疼痛
senses.example: Every line of the letter brought a fresh neuralgia of regret into her chest.
senses.exampleCN: 信上的每一行都在她胸口激起新的、神经痛般的悔意。
senses.why: Because the word already means pain that darts along a path, writers borrow it for grief and shame that seem to travel through the body in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义就是沿某条路径窜走的疼痛，作家便借它形容仿佛同样在体内游走的悲伤与羞愧。

senses.title: A neuralgia of the nerves goes loose
senses.titleCN: 引申联想：神经一松就乱放电
senses.definition: an informal picture of any condition in which a damaged or frayed nerve sends sudden, pointless alarm signals
senses.definitionCN: 一种通俗联想：受损或磨损的神经不断发出突然而无用的警报信号
senses.example: She described the tingling after the injury as a little neuralgia running down her wrist.
senses.exampleCN: 她把受伤后那种刺麻感形容成顺着手腕跑下来的一点神经痛。
senses.why: The word names pain that comes from the wire itself rather than from damage at its end, and this everyday picture helps people explain odd short stabs and tingles.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指的痛来自线路本身，而非线路末端的损伤；这种日常理解正好帮人解释那些莫名的一闪而过的刺痛与发麻。

intro.en: Neuralgia is a Modern Latin coinage that joins Greek neuron (nerve, cord) with Greek algos (pain). It is a learned medical compound rather than a word inherited through Old French, and dates given below are approximate.
intro.cn: neuralgia 是新拉丁语中的学术造词，由希腊语 neuron（神经、索）与希腊语 algos（疼痛）结合而成。它是人为构成的医学复合词，并非经古法语承袭而来；下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuron meant cord, sinew or tendon and was also used for the nerves; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: neuron 意为索、筋或腱，也被用来指神经；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Algos meant pain or distress and became a productive second element in Greek and later medical compounds.
items.cn: algos 意为疼痛、痛苦，后来在希腊语及后世的医学复合词里成为能产的第二个成分。

items.en: The French physician Francois Chaussier is generally credited with coining neuralgie in about 1801, and English adopted the form soon afterwards.
items.cn: 一般认为法国医生沙西耶在 1801 年前后创造了法文 neuralgie，英语随后很快借用了这个形式。

items.en: Early doctors applied the word to fibrous pain later called fibrositis; as knowledge of nerves grew, the nerve-trunk sense took over.
items.cn: 早期的医生用它指后来称为纤维组织炎的纤维性疼痛；随着对神经的认识加深，神经干义逐渐占上风。

items.en: English now uses the word mainly in fixed disease names such as trigeminal neuralgia, while doctors often prefer the plainer term nerve pain.
items.cn: 现代英语主要把这个词用在三叉神经痛这类固定病名中，医生日常更常用更朴素的说法「神经痛」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek nerve stem neuron; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of pain, which differ in where the pain is thought to come from.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕希腊「神经」词干 neuron 构成的词；近义组收其他类型的疼痛，区别在于疼痛被认为源自何处。

entries.definition: describing pain that shoots along a nerve, or a place where such pain strikes.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述沿神经窜走的疼痛，或指这种疼痛发作的部位。

entries.definition: Inflammation of a nerve; its ending -itis marks inflammation, not pain alone, so it is a cousin, not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 神经炎，即神经的炎症；词尾 -itis 标记炎症而非单纯的疼痛，所以它是近亲而非同义词。

entries.definition: An older term for a mental disorder with no clear physical cause; it shares only the opening letters and its ending comes from another root.
entries.definitionCN: 旧术语，指无明显躯体原因的精神障碍；它只与神经痛共享开头几个字母，词尾来自另一词根。

entries.definition: The everyday term for pain arising from damaged or irritated nerves; plainer and less clinical than neuralgia.
entries.definitionCN: 对神经受损或受刺激所致疼痛的日常说法，比神经痛一词更朴素，临床色彩更淡。

entries.definition: Pain running from the lower back down the leg along the sciatic nerve; a specific case of nerve pain.
entries.definitionCN: 沿坐骨神经从腰部向下肢放射的疼痛，是神经痛的一种具体情形。

entries.definition: A recurrent severe headache, often one-sided; it is a named headache disorder rather than a nerve condition.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发作的剧烈头痛，常偏于一侧；它是被命名的头痛疾病，而非神经病变。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Greek stems neuron and algos, the real disease names the word appears in, and the real contrast with the plainer phrase nerve pain.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的记忆钩子使用真实的希腊词干 neuron 与 algos、这个词实际出现的真实病名，以及它与朴素说法「神经痛」之间的真实对照。

normal.en: neuron plus algos: nerve plus pain, the two halves of the word say exactly what it means.
normal.cn: neuron 加 algos：神经加疼痛，两半合起来就是这个词的意思。

normal.en: The trigeminal nerve serves the face, so trigeminal neuralgia is lightning across one cheek.
normal.cn: 三叉神经管面部，所以三叉神经痛就是一道闪电划过半边脸颊。

normal.en: Postherpetic means after shingles, and the pain can outlast the rash by months.
normal.cn: postherpetic 意为「疱疹之后」，而这种痛可能比皮疹多持续数月。

normal.en: Words ending in -itis, like neuritis, name inflammation; the -algia words name pain.
normal.cn: 以 -itis 结尾的 neuritis 一类词指炎症；以 -algia 结尾的词才指疼痛。

normal.en: Doctors often say nerve pain to patients and keep neuralgia for the diagnosis.
normal.cn: 医生对病人常说「神经痛」，把 neuralgia 留给诊断书。

abstract.en: Picture a single wire running from the jaw up to the temple, and someone flicks the switch once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根电线从下颌一路走到太阳穴，有人把开关拨了一下。

abstract.en: Picture a nerve as a frayed cable that sends sparks where nothing is actually damaged.
abstract.cn: 想象一根磨损的电缆，在没有真正损坏的地方噼啪冒火花。

abstract.en: Picture a fire alarm wired to the wrong corridor: the pain rings far from where the fault began.
abstract.cn: 想象火警器接错了走廊：警报响的地方离真正的故障很远。

examples.en: Her doctor suspected neuralgia after ordinary painkillers did nothing for the flashes in her face.
examples.cn: 普通止痛药对她脸上的闪痛毫无作用后，医生怀疑是神经痛。

examples.en: Trigeminal neuralgia can make even a light touch on the cheek unbearable.
examples.cn: 三叉神经痛能让脸颊上轻轻一碰都难以忍受。

examples.en: Older medical texts used neuralgia for fibrous pain that later received a different name.
examples.cn: 早期的医学文献用 neuralgia 指纤维性疼痛，这种疼痛后来换了一个名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「牛拉尔加」：牛拉着车，鞭子抽在神经上，一路都是刺痛的疼；这只是谐音联想，切勿当作词源。

root: 希腊语 neuron「索、筋、神经」+ 希腊语 algos「疼痛」→ 新拉丁语 neuralgia（一般认为由法国医生沙西耶于 1801 年前后创造）→ 英语 neuralgia，核心义「痛在神经上」。希腊名词的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a precise description of pain located on a nerve, is turned into named diseases, keeps an older fibrous sense, and is then borrowed for figurative stabs and for any odd signal a damaged nerve sends.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词起初精确描述「长在神经上的痛」，随后被用来命名具体疾病，又保留了一层较早的纤维性疼痛义，最后被借去形容比喻意义上的刺心之痛，以及受损神经发出的各种异常信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one nerve strand glowing like a live wire, its whole length aching at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条神经像带电的线发着光，整条线同时在痛。

branches.en: THE SENSATION: the pain itself, located on the nerve rather than in an organ or a wound.
branches.cn: 感觉线：疼痛本身，位置在神经上，而不在某个器官或伤口里。

branches.en: THE DIAGNOSIS: once the affected nerve is named, the pain becomes a disease on a chart.
branches.cn: 诊断线：一旦说出受累的神经，疼痛就变成病历上的一条疾病。

branches.en: THE OLDER USE: neuron also covered sinew, so early clinicians used the word for fibrous pain.
branches.cn: 旧用法线：neuron 也指筋腱，所以早期医生用它指纤维性疼痛。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR: pain that travels along a path becomes a figure for grief and regret.
branches.cn: 比喻线：沿路径窜走的疼痛，成为悲伤与悔恨的喻体。

branches.en: THE WIRE: a damaged nerve firing without cause explains tingles and stabs in everyday talk.
branches.cn: 线路线：受损神经无故放电，在日常说法里解释那些刺麻与闪痛。

intro.en: Neuralgia is a two-part medical compound: the Greek stem for nerve in front, and the Greek stem for pain behind.
intro.cn: neuralgia 是两段式医学复合词：前面是希腊语「神经」词干，后面是希腊语「疼痛」词干。

latinIntro.en: Neuralgia is New Latin, not classical Latin: it was assembled in the early nineteenth century from two Greek elements, and both pieces keep their Greek forms.
latinIntro.cn: neuralgia 是新拉丁语而非古典拉丁语：它在十九世纪初由两个希腊语成分拼成，两段都保留了希腊语形态。

items.example: The front half of the word names the nerve.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的前半段指神经。

items.example: The combining form builds dozens of medical terms.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式构成几十个医学术语。

items.meaningCN: 表示某部位疼痛的后缀
items.example: The suffix names where the pain is felt.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指明疼痛发生在哪里。

items.example: The suffix turns the noun into neuralgic.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成 neuralgic。

items.example: Contrast it with neuritis, which is inflammation rather than pain.
items.exampleCN: 把它与 neuritis 对照，后者指炎症而不是疼痛。

items.example: The suffix forms neurology from the same nerve stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀用同一个神经词干构成 neurology。

items.example: The adjective describes the quality of the pain.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词描述疼痛的性质。

items.meaning: an old term for a mental disorder
items.meaningCN: 精神神经官能症的旧称
items.example: Its ending is not the pain suffix, so it is only a look-alike.
items.exampleCN: 它的词尾不是表示疼痛的后缀，因此只是形近词。

items.meaning: an old name for fibrous pain, now called fibromyalgia
items.meaningCN: 纤维性疼痛的旧名，今称纤维肌痛
items.example: Some nineteenth-century neuralgia cases were later renamed fibrositis.
items.exampleCN: 一些十九世纪的神经痛病例后来被改归纤维组织炎。

latinEntries.structure: neuron, neuri (n., Greek loan in New Latin)

definition_zh: 神经经济学：用脑成像与神经科学方法研究经济决策的交叉学科
definition_en: an interdisciplinary field that combines neuroscience methods, especially brain imaging, with economics to study how people actually make decisions
core_image: 一个人正在选择要买哪件商品，同时旁边的机器把他的脑活动画成一张发亮的图
scene: 实验室里，志愿者面对两个价格标签作选择，邻室的屏幕上同时亮起他的脑部扫描图。Neuroeconomics asks which brain regions are active when a shopper rejects a discount.
sceneCN: 这里 neuroeconomics 是「神经经济学」（第 1 个义项：把神经科学方法用于经济决策研究的交叉学科）；句意为神经经济学研究的是购物者拒绝折扣时哪些脑区处于活跃状态。图中可辨识物件：扫描仪、价格标签、屏幕上的脑图、记录表。

pos.zh: 学科名词：神经经济学；以不可数用法为主，也可指这一学科领域内的研究

collocations.zh: 神经经济学研究（科研活动）
神经经济学与行为经济学

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉词尾加形容词后缀构成，义为「神经经济学的；与神经经济学有关的」
由本词与表示「人」的后缀合成，义为「神经经济学家」
由神经经济学与计量经济学词干合成，义为「神经计量经济学的」
与神经经济学同属消费者神经科学，由「神经」与「营销」合成，义为「神经营销学」
与神经经济学同源的研究方向，由「神经」与「金融」合成，义为「神经金融学」

senses.title: The interdisciplinary field itself
senses.titleCN: 作为交叉学科的神经经济学
senses.definition: the academic field that applies neuroscience methods, especially brain imaging, to questions about economic decision-making
senses.definitionCN: 把神经科学方法（尤其是脑成像）用于经济决策问题的学术领域
senses.example: Neuroeconomics began by asking whether the brain of a buyer really matches the model of a rational agent.
senses.exampleCN: 神经经济学一开始就追问：买主的大脑真的符合理性主体的模型吗。
senses.why: The three Greek pieces say what the field is made of: nerves studied for their own sake, a whole economy approached through the household, and a branch that earns its own name.
senses.whyCN: 三个希腊语成分说清了学科的构成：被专门研究的神经、以「家宅」为本的经济，以及一个独立成名的分支。

senses.title: A school of thought inside economics
senses.titleCN: 经济学内部的一个学派
senses.definition: a research programme that challenges purely mathematical models of choice by testing preferences inside the living brain
senses.definitionCN: 用活体大脑检验偏好、从而挑战纯数理选择模型的研究纲领
senses.example: Neuroeconomics often corrects rational choice theory rather than rejecting it.
senses.exampleCN: 神经经济学往往是在修正理性选择理论，而不是抛弃它。
senses.why: Because the tools are new but the questions are old, the field works as a critique from inside economics rather than as a replacement for it.
senses.whyCN: 工具是新的，问题却是老的，因此这门学科在经济学内部充当批评者，而不是替代品。

senses.title: The brain picture in a decision
senses.definition: the body of evidence about which brain regions light up when people value, choose, gamble or lose
senses.definitionCN: 关于人们在评估、选择、赌博或损失时哪些脑区被激活的一组证据
senses.example: Neuroeconomics links a surge of activity in the reward system to the moment a price feels fair.
senses.exampleCN: 神经经济学把奖赏系统的活动骤然升高，与「觉得价格公道」的那一刻联系起来。
senses.why: Once the field collected enough scans, it became a body of findings in its own right, and the name refers to that evidence as well as to the field.
senses.whyCN: 当汇集了足够多的扫描结果，这门学科本身就成为一组发现，于是名称既指学科，也指这批证据。

senses.title: A toolkit for policy and pricing
senses.titleCN: 用于政策与定价的工具
senses.definition: the practical application of such findings by regulators, firms and designers of public programmes
senses.definitionCN: 监管者、企业与公共项目设计者对此类发现的实务运用
senses.example: Neuroeconomics informed a pension scheme that makes saving the default, because the brain clings to defaults.
senses.exampleCN: 神经经济学为一项「把储蓄设为默认」的养老金方案提供了依据，因为大脑倾向于固守默认。
senses.why: If the brain responds predictably to defaults and losses, the findings can be used to design choices, and the name acquires a practical, applied colour.
senses.whyCN: 如果大脑对默认选项与损失会作出可预测的反应，这些发现就能用来设计选项，名称也随之带上实务应用色彩。

senses.title: A catch-all label
senses.definition: a loose abbreviation for any study mixing brain science with money, stakes or consumer choices, including marketing
senses.definitionCN: 凡把脑科学与金钱、风险或消费选择混在一起的研究（包括营销）都被泛称的宽松标签
senses.example: The label neuroeconomics now covers everything from auction experiments to advertising tests.
senses.exampleCN: 神经经济学这个标签如今从拍卖实验一路覆盖到广告测试。
senses.why: Compound names tend to drift outward; because the field sits between two large subjects, journalists and advertisers stretch the label well past its academic use.
senses.whyCN: 复合名称往往向外漂移；这门学科夹在两大学科之间，记者与广告业者便把这个标签拉得远超学术用途。

intro.en: Neuroeconomics joins the Greek prefix neuro-, meaning nerve, to economics, which descends from Greek oikonomia, household management. The adjective was already in print in the 1980s with an unrelated meaning; the compound in its present sense is generally dated to the 2000s, and the exact first use is uncertain.
intro.cn: neuroeconomics 把表示「神经」的希腊前缀 neuro- 加到 economics 上，后者经拉丁语源自希腊语 oikonomia（治家之术）。这个形容词在二十世纪八十年代已见文献，但当时含义无关；现义的名词一般认为在 2000 年代定型，确切首见来源不确定。

items.en: Neuron meant sinew, cord or nerve, and it supplies the modern combining form neuro-.
items.cn: neuron 意为筋、索或神经，正是现代组合形式 neuro- 的来源。

items.en: Oikos meant household and nemein meant to manage, so oikonomia named the running of a household and later of public affairs.
items.cn: oikos 意为家宅，nemein 意为管理，所以 oikonomia 先指经营家宅，后也指管理公共事务。

items.en: Political economy was shortened to economics in the nineteenth century, giving the base to which neuro- was later attached.
items.cn: 十九世纪政治经济学缩称为经济学，为后来加接 neuro- 提供了基础词。

items.en: The adjective appears in economic writing in the 1980s with meanings such as general economic conditions; these early uses are unrelated to brain research.
items.cn: 这个形容词在二十世纪八十年代的经济写作中已出现，指的是总体经济状况一类的意思；这些早期用法与脑研究无关。

items.en: The noun is generally thought to have settled in the 2000s, as imaging and game experiments were gathered under one heading; the exact first year is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为这个名词在 2000 年代固定下来，当时脑成像与博弈实验被归到同一个名目下；具体首见年份不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the person noun and a statistics-flavoured near-miss; the near-meaning group holds neighbouring fields that each take one part of the brain-and-choice picture.
note.cn: 形近组收形容词、指人的名词，以及一个带统计色彩的近形词；近义组收相邻领域，各自只取「大脑与选择」这幅图景的一部分。

entries.definition: Describes evidence or an approach from the field; it cannot be the name of the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述来自该领域的证据或方法；它不能用作学科本身的名称。

entries.definition: A researcher who works in the field, sometimes trained in economics and sometimes in neuroscience.
entries.definitionCN: 在这一领域工作的研究者，其出身有时是经济学，有时是神经科学。

entries.definition: The statistical side of economics; its middle element means measure, not nerve, so only the ending matches.
entries.definitionCN: 经济学中以统计方法为工具的分支；其中间成分意为「测量」而非神经，只有词尾相同。

entries.definition: Studies how people actually choose, often through experiments; it works from behaviour rather than from scans.
entries.definitionCN: 研究人们实际如何选择，常用实验方法；它从行为出发，而不是从脑部扫描出发。

entries.definition: The commercial use of brain measures to test ads and packaging; it is a paid application, not a discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 用脑部测量测试广告与包装的商业做法；它是一种收费应用，而不是学科。

entries.definition: The broad study of mind, covering perception, memory and reasoning; much wider than decision and money.
entries.definitionCN: 研究心灵的大领域，包括知觉、记忆与推理；远比「决策与金钱」宽泛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here use the real Greek stems behind the two halves, the real neighbour that the field argues with, and the real phrases the subject name appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自两半词背后真实的希腊词干、该领域真正与之争论的邻门学科，以及学科名称实际出现的真实搭配。

normal.en: neuron is nerve and oikonomia is household management, so the word is nerves brought to economic decisions.
normal.cn: neuron 是神经，oikonomia 是治家之术，所以这个词就是「把神经带进经济决策」。

normal.en: The field sits between two universities: a lab in the medical school and a seminar room in the economics department.
normal.cn: 这门学科坐在两所学院之间：医学院的实验室与经济系的讨论课。

normal.en: It argues with rational choice theory, not with economics as a whole.
normal.cn: 它与理性选择理论争论，而不是与整个经济学作对。

normal.en: Econometrics measures with statistics; neuroeconomics measures with scanners, and only the ending sounds alike.
normal.cn: econometrics 用统计测量，neuroeconomics 用扫描仪测量，两词只有词尾听起来相似。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the academic use: a neuroeconomics study, a conference, the field of neuroeconomics.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出学术用法：神经经济学研究、会议，以及这一领域。

abstract.en: Picture a shopper holding two price tags while a screen beside the checkout draws the brain live.
abstract.cn: 想象一位顾客拿着两个价签，收银台旁的屏幕正实时画出他的大脑。

abstract.en: Picture the same question asked twice: once as an equation on a whiteboard and once as a lit region on a scan.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个问题被问两遍：一次是白板上的方程，一次是扫描图上亮起的区域。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge of glass connecting a hospital scanner to a trading floor, people walking across both ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一座玻璃桥连接医院扫描室与交易大厅，人们双向来往。

examples.en: Her thesis applies neuroeconomics to the way farmers decide whether to buy crop insurance.
examples.cn: 她的论文把神经经济学用于研究农户如何决定是否购买农作物保险。

examples.en: Critics say neuroeconomics promises more certainty than a small scanner study can deliver.
examples.cn: 批评者认为，神经经济学许下的确定性，超过一项小规模扫描研究所能兑现的程度。

examples.en: The commission cited neuroeconomics when it made the healthy option the default on a school menu.
examples.cn: 委员会在把健康选项设为学校菜单默认项时引用了神经经济学。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「牛肉economics」：一块牛肉摆在你面前，你盯着它犹豫买不买，机器顺便照了照你的脑袋，算的是脑里的钱包；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 neuron「神经」+ 希腊语 oikonomia（oikos「家宅」+ nemein「管理」，经拉丁 oeconomia 与英语 economics）→ 二十世纪八十年代已有含义不同的形容词 neuroeconomic，现义的名词 neuroeconomics 一般认为在 2000 年代随脑成像与博弈实验结合而成型，首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses follow one line: the field is named, becomes a school of thought that corrects rational choice, turns into a body of scan evidence, is applied to policy and pricing, and finally spreads out as a loose label.
sensesIntro.cn: 五个义项沿一条线展开：学科先被命名，进而成为一个修正理性选择理论的学派，再成为一批扫描证据，被用于政策与定价，最后扩散为一个宽松的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two price tags in one hand, a living brain lit up on a screen beside them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一手举着两个价签，旁边的屏幕上亮着一颗活体大脑。

branches.en: THE NAMING: a Greek nerve stem is fixed to the name of economics, and the field learns to say its own name.
branches.cn: 命名线：希腊「神经」词干接上经济学之名，这门学科学会说出自己的名字。

branches.en: THE DEBATE: the field grows by correcting the rational agent from inside economics.
branches.cn: 论战线：该领域通过在经济学内部修正理性主体而壮大。

branches.en: THE EVIDENCE: scans of reward, loss and choice become a body of findings in their own right.
branches.cn: 证据线：关于奖赏、损失与选择的扫描结果，本身成为一批发现。

branches.en: THE APPLICATION: regulators and firms use the findings to design defaults and prices.
branches.cn: 应用线：监管者与企业用这些发现设计默认选项与价格。

branches.en: THE DRIFT: the label widens to cover any mixing of brains and money.
branches.cn: 漂移线：这个标签被扩大到涵盖一切「大脑加金钱」的组合。

intro.en: The word is a scale-and-subject compound: a Greek nerve prefix in front and the household-derived name of economics behind.
intro.cn: 这个词是「主题前缀加学科名」的复合词：前面是表示神经的希腊前缀，后面是由治家一词演变来的经济学之名。

latinIntro.en: The economics half reached English through Latin oeconomia; the nerve half is Greek neuron latinised as a combining form, and the compound itself is modern.
latinIntro.cn: 「经济学」那一半经拉丁 oeconomia 进入英语；「神经」那一半是拉丁化的希腊 neuron，而整个复合词是现代才有的。

items.meaning: relating to nerves or the nervous system
items.meaningCN: 与神经或神经系统有关的
items.example: The prefix points the study at the living brain.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把研究指向活体大脑。

items.example: Neuron is the ultimate source of the first half.
items.exampleCN: neuron 是前半段的最终来源。

items.example: The compound supplies the oldest layer of the base word.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词提供基础词最古老的一层。

items.meaning: management of an estate or state
items.example: Latin carried the idea into European learned usage.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把这个观念带入欧洲学术用语。

items.meaning: the study of production, trade and resources
items.meaningCN: 研究生产、贸易与资源的学科
items.example: Economics is the base to which the nerve prefix is fixed.

items.example: Econometrics measures with statistics, not with nerves.

definition_zh: 神经科医生；神经病学专家
definition_en: a doctor who is trained to diagnose and treat disorders of the brain, spinal cord and nerves
core_image: 一位医生拿着小锤和手电，在诊室里一点点地问神经：哪条路还通，哪条路断了
scene: 诊室桌上摊着一张人体神经图，医生正在等患者伸出舌头、抬起手臂。The neurologist asked him to walk in a straight line, then tapped his knees with a small hammer.
sceneCN: 这里 neurologist 是「神经科医生」（第 1 个义项：专门诊断和治疗脑、脊髓与神经疾病的医生）；句意为这位神经科医生让他沿直线走，又用小锤敲了敲他的膝盖。图中可辨识物件：神经图、叩诊锤、手电筒、诊室桌。

senses.title: A doctor of the nervous system
senses.definition: a physician who diagnoses and treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, muscles and nerves by clinical examination and medical treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过临床检查与药物治疗来诊断和处理脑、脊髓、肌肉与神经疾病的医生
senses.example: The neurologist tested her reflexes, her balance and the feeling in her feet.
senses.exampleCN: 这位神经科医生检查了她的反射、平衡以及双脚的感觉。
senses.why: The Greek pieces say exactly what such a doctor studies: nerve plus the study of a subject plus the person who practises it.
senses.whyCN: 三个希腊语成分恰好说清这位医生研究什么：神经、对某物的研究，以及从事这门研究的人。

senses.title: The specialist who receives referrals
senses.titleCN: 接诊转诊病人的专科医生
senses.definition: a hospital specialist to whom a family doctor sends a patient when symptoms such as headaches, seizures or numbness need expert assessment
senses.definitionCN: 全科医生遇到头痛、癫痫发作或麻木等需要专家评估的症状时，把病人转诊过去的医院专科医生
senses.example: Her family doctor referred her to a neurologist after the third blackout.
senses.exampleCN: 她第三次晕倒之后，家庭医生把她转诊给了神经科医生。
senses.why: Because general practice cannot carry the whole burden of nerve disease, the profession divided its work, and the specialist with the nerve-trained eye collects the harder referrals.
senses.whyCN: 全科诊所承担不了神经疾病的全部工作，专业便分工，而受过神经训练、眼光更专的那位医生就负责接住较难的转诊。

senses.title: A named hospital post
senses.definition: a formal job title inside a hospital, as in consultant neurologist or paediatric neurologist, tied to a department, a ward and training duties
senses.definitionCN: 医院内部的正式职位称谓，如神经科顾问医师或儿童神经科医生，与科室、病房及带教职责绑定
senses.example: She was appointed consultant neurologist at the district hospital last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天，她被聘任为地区医院的神经科顾问医师。
senses.why: Once a branch of medicine acquires departments, its practitioners acquire posts, and the word becomes a title printed on a door.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某医学分支有了专科，从业者便有了职位，这个词也随之成为印在门牌上的头衔。

senses.title: A member of a learned profession
senses.definition: a recognised member of a professional body or college of neurology, with its own examinations and code of conduct
senses.definitionCN: 某神经病学专业学会或学院的正式会员，有其自己的考试与行为规范
senses.example: Only a qualified neurologist may sign off on the electrode study.
senses.exampleCN: 只有具备资质的神经科医生才能签署这项电极检查的报告。
senses.why: The ancient suffix for one who practises a craft turned into a mark of certification, so the word now names membership as well as skill.
senses.whyCN: 那个表示「从事某种技艺之人」的古老后缀，后来变成一种资格证明，于是这个词既指技艺，也指会员身份。

senses.title: Figurative mind-reader
senses.definition: a joking description of anyone who seems to understand the mind of another person too exactly
senses.definitionCN: 戏称那些仿佛能准确读出别人内心想法的人
senses.example: You did not need to be a neurologist to see what she was thinking.
senses.exampleCN: 不用当神经科医生，也能看出她在想什么。
senses.why: Because the doctor is trained to locate invisible causes inside the head, the word makes a handy joke for someone who seems to read minds.
senses.whyCN: 医生受过在头脑里定位看不见病因的训练，这个词于是成了形容「会看透人心」的现成笑话。

intro.en: Neurologist is neurology plus -ist, the suffix for a person. Neurology joins Greek neuron (nerve) with -logia (the study of), and the English word acquired its clinical sense over the nineteenth century; dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: neurologist 由 neurology 加表示「人」的后缀 -ist 构成。neurology 由希腊语 neuron（神经）与 -logia（研究）结合而成，其英语形式在十九世纪逐渐取得临床含义；下列年代均为约数。

items.en: Neuron meant sinew, cord or tendon and was used by Greek doctors for the nerves; its deeper origin is uncertain.
items.cn: neuron 意为筋、索或腱，希腊医生用它指神经；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: The ending -logia meant the study or account of something, built on logos, word, reason or account.
items.cn: 词尾 -logia 意为对某物的研究或论述，建立在 logos（言词、理性、论述）之上。

items.en: New Latin formed neurologia for the study of nerves, and early uses were often theoretical rather than bedside.
items.cn: 新拉丁语构成 neurologia，指对神经的研究；早期用法多偏理论，而非床边诊疗。

items.en: English neurology took on its clinical sense as hospitals set aside wards for cases with no visible injury.
items.cn: 当医院为查不出外伤的病例专门划出病房时，英语 neurology 取得了临床含义。

items.en: Adding -ist to neurology named the practitioner; the exact first use is uncertain and the word spread quickly after 1870.
items.cn: 在 neurology 之后加 -ist 来命名从业者；确切首见不确定，1870 年后这个词迅速流传。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Greek nerve stem neuron, differing in what each one studies or does; the near-meaning group gathers other specialists a patient with nerve symptoms may be sent to.
note.cn: 形近组收围绕希腊「神经」词干 neuron 构成的词，区别在于各自研究或从事什么；近义组收出现神经症状的病人可能被转去的其他专科医生。

entries.definition: The field of medicine that studies and treats nerve disorders; the study, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 研究并治疗神经疾病的医学领域；它指学科，不指人。

entries.definition: A surgeon who operates on the brain and spinal cord; shares the prefix but the work is cutting, not diagnosing.
entries.definitionCN: 为脑与脊髓动手术的外科医生；共享前缀，但工作是开刀而非诊断。

entries.definition: An old word for a person with a nervous, anxious disposition; it merely starts with the same letters and is never a medical title.
entries.definitionCN: 旧词，指神经质、易焦虑的人；它只是开头字母相同，绝不是医学头衔。

entries.definition: Treats mental illness, mood and behaviour; the two specialties overlap but this one works with the mind rather than with the wiring.
entries.definitionCN: 治疗精神疾病、情绪与行为；两个专科有交叉，但这一位处理的是心智，而不是神经线路。

entries.definition: Examines nerve and brain tissue to identify disease; shares the prefix but answers with a microscope.
entries.definitionCN: 检查神经与脑组织以判定疾病；共享前缀，但靠显微镜给出答案。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for a neurosurgeon; it is the plainer, less formal alternative to the medical title.
entries.definitionCN: 神经外科医生的日常说法，比医学头衔更朴素、更口语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here use the real Greek stems, the real hospital division of labour, and the real phrases printed on appointment letters.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自真实的希腊词干、医院里真实的分工，以及预约信上真实出现的搭配。

normal.en: neuron is nerve, -logia is study and -ist is the person, so the word is the nerve-study person.
normal.cn: neuron 是神经，-logia 是研究，-ist 是人，合起来就是「研究神经的人」。

normal.en: The same root chain runs through the family: neurology, neurological, neurologist.
normal.cn: 同一词根贯穿整个词族：neurology、neurological、neurologist。

normal.en: A neurologist diagnoses and treats; a neurosurgeon cuts, although the two often share a ward.
normal.cn: 神经科医生做诊断与用药，神经外科医生动刀，两者常在同一病房协作。

normal.en: Family doctors refer to a neurologist, so the word rarely appears without a referral.
normal.cn: 家庭医生把病人转诊给神经科医生，所以这个词很少脱离「转诊」语境出现。

normal.en: In Britain the senior post is printed as consultant neurologist.
normal.cn: 在英国，高级职位写作 consultant neurologist。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor with a small hammer and a torch, testing lines of communication one at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一位医生拿着小锤和手电，逐条测试身体的通信线路。

abstract.en: Picture a maze inside the skull and a specialist who has walked it so often that they know every dead end.
abstract.cn: 想象颅骨内的一座迷宫，有位专家走过太多次，熟悉每一个死胡同。

abstract.en: Picture a sign on a door that says both study and doctor, because the same stems give both words.
abstract.cn: 想象门牌上同时写着「学科」与「医生」，因为两个词出自同样的词干。

examples.en: The neurologist explained that the numbness came from a pinched nerve, not from the spine itself.
examples.cn: 神经科医生解释说，那种麻木来自神经受压，而不是脊柱本身出了问题。

examples.en: After two months of dizzy spells, a neurologist finally ordered an MRI.
examples.cn: 接连两个月头晕之后，神经科医生终于安排了磁共振检查。

examples.en: A good neurologist listens to the patient before ordering a single test.
examples.cn: 好的神经科医生会先听病人讲述，然后再决定开检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「牛若李司机」：牛老先生若会开李家的车，路上一有岔口就得问路——他就是专门给身体线路问路的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 neuron「索、筋、神经」+ 希腊语 -logia「研究」（来自 logos「言词、理性」）→ 新拉丁语 neurologia → 英语 neurology（十九世纪取得临床义）+ 表示「从事者」的后缀 -ist → neurologist，核心义「研究并诊治神经的人」。

sensesIntro.en: The word is first a doctor of the nervous system, then the specialist who receives hard referrals, then a hospital post, a certified member of a profession, and finally a joke about reading minds.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指诊治神经系统的医生，再指接收疑难转诊的专科医生，继而是医院里的职位、受认证的专业成员，最后引申为「能读出人心」的玩笑说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a doctor with a small hammer and a torch listening to the wiring of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位医生拿着小锤和手电，倾听身体线路的回话。

branches.en: THE ROLE: the person who examines and treats disorders of brain, cord and nerve.
branches.cn: 角色线：检查并治疗脑、脊髓与神经疾病的人。

branches.en: THE REFERRAL: the specialist at the far end of the note sent by a family doctor.
branches.cn: 转诊线：家庭医生那张便条另一端的专科医生。

branches.en: THE POST: the title on a hospital office door.
branches.cn: 职位线：医院诊室门牌上的头衔。

branches.en: THE PROFESSION: the certificate and college behind the title.
branches.cn: 专业线：头衔背后的资质证明与学会。

branches.en: THE JOKE: anyone who seems to know what is inside your head.
branches.cn: 玩笑线：任何看起来知道你脑子里在想什么的人。

intro.en: The word stacks three pieces: a Greek nerve stem, a Greek stem for study, and a Greek suffix for the person who practises.
intro.cn: 这个词叠了三段：希腊语「神经」词干、希腊语「研究」词干，以及表示「从事者」的希腊语后缀。

latinIntro.en: New Latin neurologia joined Greek neuron and -logia, and the Latin-derived person suffix -ista became English -ist.
latinIntro.cn: 新拉丁语 neurologia 把希腊语 neuron 与 -logia 结合，源自拉丁语的指人后缀 -ista 在英语中变作 -ist。

items.example: The first stem names what the doctor studies.
items.exampleCN: 第一个词干指医生所研究的对象。

items.example: The combining form also builds neurology and neurological.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式还构成 neurology 与 neurological。

items.example: The suffix names a discipline rather than a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名学科，而不指人。

items.example: The English ending forms neurology.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词尾构成 neurology。

items.structure: person suffix of Greek and Latin origin
items.example: The suffix changes a subject into a person.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把学科变成人。

items.example: The suffix forms neurological.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 neurological。

items.example: The suffix forms neurologically.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 neurologically。

items.structure: second element from Old French surgien
items.example: It forms neurosurgeon, the operating cousin.
items.exampleCN: 它构成神经外科医生这一会动手术的近亲词。

items.structure: second element from Greek pathos and -logia
items.example: It forms neuropathologist, who reads tissue under a microscope.
items.exampleCN: 它构成神经病理学家，此人在显微镜下看组织。

items.meaning: of the nervous system or the branch
items.example: Neurological problems are what a neurologist treats.
items.exampleCN: 神经系统问题正是神经科医生要处理的。
