definition_zh: 使中和；使失效；抵消；使中立
definition_en: to make something have no effect, or to make two opposing forces or things cancel each other out
core_image: 一杯酸液里滴入碱液，冒起的泡沫落下后变成平静的中性水
scene: 实验室里，学生小心地把碱液滴进酸液中。In the lab, the student carefully neutralised the acid with an alkali.
sceneCN: 这里 neutralise 是「使中和」（第 1 个义项：用相反性质的物质把酸碱抵消掉）；句意：在实验室里，学生小心地用碱液把酸中和了。

pos.zh: 使中和；使失效；抵消
起中和作用；互相抵消

derivatives.zh: 基础词的中性形式，义为「中立的；中性的」
由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「中和；抵消」
由美式拼写 neutralize 加 -er 构成，义为「中和剂」
加 -er 表示执行者，义为「中和剂；起中和作用者」
由 neutral 加 -ism 构成，义为「中立主义」

senses.title: To cancel out opposite chemical properties
senses.definition: to make an acid or an alkali neither acid nor alkaline by mixing it with something of the opposite kind
senses.definitionCN: 用与酸或碱性质相反的物质混合，使其既不成酸性也不成碱性
senses.example: A spoonful of lime can neutralise the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 一勺石灰就能让土壤中和。
senses.why: The core image is a drop of alkali falling into an acid and settling into still, neutral water, so the word begins in the test tube.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是碱液滴入酸液后归于平静的中性水，所以这个词义从试管开始。

senses.title: To stop something from having an effect
senses.definition: to remove the power or force of something so that it can no longer do any harm or have any effect
senses.definitionCN: 消除某事物的力量或作用，使其不再造成危害或产生效果
senses.example: The drug neutralises the venom within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药能在几分钟内使毒液失效。
senses.why: If opposite substances cancel each other out, then any force can be cancelled by something that opposes it.
senses.whyCN: 既然相反的两种物质可以互相抵消，那么任何力量也能被与之相反的力量抵消。

senses.title: To make a person or force powerless
senses.definition: to make an opponent, a team, or an enemy force unable to act effectively
senses.definitionCN: 使对手、球队或敌军失去行动能力、无法有效发挥
senses.example: The defenders neutralised every attack on the left wing.
senses.exampleCN: 后卫们化解了左路的每一次进攻。
senses.why: A rival is like a charge that must be balanced, so to neutralise someone is to take away their power.
senses.whyCN: 对手像需要被平衡的电荷一样，所以使某人失效就是拿走他的力量。

senses.title: To make a place or person neutral
senses.definition: to make a country, area, or person take no side in a dispute or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 使某个国家、地区或个人在争端或冲突中不站任何一方
senses.example: The treaty neutralised the port and banned warships.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约使这个港口保持中立，并禁止军舰进入。
senses.why: The word also works on people and places: putting them outside the fight is like making them chemically neutral.
senses.whyCN: 这个词也能用之于人和地方：把他们置于争斗之外，就像把他们变成化学上的中性。

intro.en: Neutralise is a verb built from the adjective neutral, which goes back to Latin neuter, meaning neither of the two.
intro.cn: neutralise 是由形容词 neutral 派生的动词，而 neutral 可追溯到拉丁语 neuter（两者皆非）。

items.en: Neuter is a compound of ne, not, and uter, either of the two.
items.cn: neuter 由 ne（不）与 uter（两者之一）合成，字面意为「两者皆非」。

items.en: Grammarians used neuter for the gender that is neither masculine nor feminine.
items.cn: 语法学家用 neuter 指既非阳性也非阴性的中性词性。

items.en: Neutral enters English to describe anyone who takes neither side.
items.cn: neutral 进入英语，形容不站任何一方的人。

items.en: Chemists call a substance that is neither acid nor alkali neutral.
items.cn: 化学家把既非酸性也非碱性的物质称为 neutral。

items.en: The verb neutralise is formed from neutral with the suffix -ise, meaning to make so.
items.cn: 动词 neutralise 由 neutral 加后缀 -ise 构成，意为「使成为……」。

items.en: American English prefers the spelling neutralize.
items.cn: 美式英语多写作 neutralize。

note.en: Neutralise is built on neutral, and it sits close to words of cancelling, countering, and taking no side.
note.cn: neutralise 由 neutral 派生，与「抵消、反制、不站边」一类词义邻近。

entries.definition: not supporting either side in a disagreement
the American spelling of the same verb
the process of making something neutral
the state of taking no side in a conflict
to stop something from having any effect
to reduce the effect of something by acting against it
to make something unable to work

normalIntro.en: Neutralise carries its own explanation: neutral plus ise, to make neutral, so every use describes making something powerless or balanced.
normalIntro.cn: neutralise 自带解释：neutral 加 ise，即「使成为中性」，所以每次使用都在说让某物失去作用或达到平衡。

normal.en: The suffix -ise means to make, so neutralise is to make neutral.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ise 表示「使……」，所以 neutralise 就是「使中性」。

normal.en: The root is Latin neuter, neither one of the two, which is why neutrality means no side.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁语 neuter（两者皆非），这也是 neutrality 表示「不站边」的原因。

normal.en: The noun neutralisation names the process, as in an acid neutralisation reaction.
normal.cn: 名词 neutralisation 指这一过程，如「酸碱中和反应」。

normal.en: One enzyme can neutralise a whole flask of toxin, so the verb often follows words for poisons and threats.
normal.cn: 一种酶就能使一整瓶毒素失效，所以这个动词常接毒素、威胁一类的词。

normal.en: Remember the British s in neutralise and the American z in neutralize.
normal.cn: 记住英式拼写用 s，美式拼写用 z。

abstract.en: Picture a drop of clear liquid falling into a fizzing glass, and the fizz going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴清液落入冒泡的杯中，气泡渐渐平息。

abstract.en: Picture a shield swallowing an arrow, leaving nothing behind but dust.
abstract.cn: 想象一面盾牌吞下箭矢，只留下一阵粉末。

abstract.en: Picture a knight stepping back from both armies and planting a white flag.
abstract.cn: 想象一位骑士退离两军，插下一面白旗。

examples.en: The city tried to neutralise the chemical spill with sand.
examples.cn: 市政府尝试用沙子中和这次化学品泄漏。

examples.en: A good goalkeeper can neutralise the best striker in the league.
examples.cn: 一名优秀门将可以压制联赛中最出色的前锋。

examples.en: The new rules were meant to neutralise the advantage of large firms.
examples.cn: 这些新规定旨在抵消大公司的优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛戳来」——牛角戳来戳去，力气互相抵消，谁也没伤到，就是「使失效」；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ne（不）+ uter（两者之一）→ neuter（两者皆非）→ 英语 neutral（中立的；中性的）→ 加 -ise 构成 neutralise，核心义「使两边力量互相抵消而归于平衡」。

sensesIntro.en: Neutralise begins in the laboratory, where opposite substances cancel each other out; from there it widens to stopping any effect, making a rival powerless, and keeping a place out of a conflict.
sensesIntro.cn: neutralise 始于实验室，那里性质相反的物质互相抵消；由此扩展到消除任何影响、使对手失去威力，以及让某地置身冲突之外。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an acid and an alkali meeting and leaving no trace of a charge.
core.cn: 核心意象：酸与碱相遇后，电荷消于无形。

branches.en: The chemical sense is the literal balancing of opposite charges.
branches.cn: 化学义项是相反电荷的字面平衡。

branches.en: The general sense extends the balance to any harmful force.
branches.cn: 一般义项把这种平衡扩展到任何有害的力量。

branches.en: People, teams, and places can also be made neutral.
branches.cn: 人、球队和地方同样可以被置于中立状态。

branches.en: Both senses share the idea of a force being used up by something opposite.
branches.cn: 两个义项都共享「力量被相反之物耗尽」的观念。

branches.en: A suppressed threat and a defeated player are both made powerless.
branches.cn: 被消除的威胁与被压制的选手同样失去了威力。

intro.en: Neutralise pairs the adjective neutral with the verb suffix -ise, and the whole family rests on the Latin pronoun neuter.
intro.cn: neutralise 由形容词 neutral 与动词后缀 -ise 结合而成，整个词族都建立在拉丁语代词 neuter 之上。

latinIntro.en: Latin ne means not, and uter means either of the two, so neuter means neither of the two.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ne 表示「不」，uter 表示「两者之一」，所以 neuter 意为「两者皆非」。

items.example: The particle ne negates whatever follows it.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定小品词否定其后的成分。

items.example: Uter asks which of the two.
items.exampleCN: uter 用于询问两者中的哪一个。

items.example: Neuter gives the idea of belonging to neither side.
items.exampleCN: neuter 提供「不属于任何一方」的观念。

items.meaning: not taking sides; neither acid nor alkali
items.example: Neutral is the adjective the verb is built on.
items.exampleCN: neutral 是动词所依附的形容词。

items.example: Neutrality names the state that the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: neutrality 表示动词所造成的那种状态。

items.example: The suffix -ise turns the adjective into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ise 把形容词变成动词。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms the noun of the process.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示过程的名词。

items.meaning: to make neutral or of no effect
items.example: Scientists neutralise the waste before it is stored.
items.exampleCN: 科学家在贮存废料前先将其中和。

items.meaning: a substance or person that neutralises
items.example: The lab keeps a spirit neutraliser on the shelf.
items.exampleCN: 实验室架上备着一瓶中和剂。

items.meaning: the policy of taking no side
items.example: Neutralism describes a policy of staying out of disputes.
items.exampleCN: neutralism 描述置身争端之外的方针。

definition_zh: 报童；卖报的男孩
definition_en: a boy or young man who sells newspapers in the street or delivers them to homes
core_image: 天还没亮，街角的男孩抱着一摞报纸，一边跑一边大声叫卖
scene: 清晨的街角，一个男孩把最上面一份报纸举过头顶，大声喊着当天的大新闻。At the corner, a newsboy waved the morning paper above his head and called out the main story.
sceneCN: 这里 newsboy 是「报童」（第 1 个义项：在街头叫卖或投送报纸的男孩）；句意：在街角，一个报童把晨报举过头顶，高声喊出当天的头条。

pos.zh: 报童；卖报的男孩

derivatives.zh: 复合词前半部分的计词，义为「新闻；消息」
复合词后半部分，义为「男孩」
由 news 与 paper 构成的复合词，义为「报纸」
由 news 与 stand 构成，义为「报摊」

senses.title: A boy who sells newspapers in the street
senses.definition: a boy who stands on a street corner or walks through crowds shouting the news and selling papers to passers-by
senses.definitionCN: 站在街角或穿行人群，高声喊出新闻、向路人卖报的男孩
senses.example: A newsboy stood on the corner, shouting the late edition.
senses.exampleCN: 一个报童站在街角，高喊晚报的标题。
senses.why: The word joins news to boy, so the core is a boy whose job is the paper in his arms.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把 news 与 boy 合在一起，核心就是怀里抱着报纸、以此为业的男孩。

senses.title: A boy who delivers papers to homes
senses.definition: a boy who carries newspapers from door to door on a fixed route early in the morning
senses.definitionCN: 清晨沿固定路线挨家挨户投递报纸的男孩
senses.example: Our newsboy left the paper behind the gate every day.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的送报男孩每天把报纸放在大门后面。
senses.why: As papers came to the home, the same compound named the boy who carried them along a fixed route.
senses.whyCN: 随着报纸进入家庭，同一复合词也用来指沿固定路线送报的男孩。

senses.title: A figure of the old street newspaper trade
senses.definition: a stock figure of the age when morning papers were sold on the street, often in stories about city childhood
senses.definitionCN: 早报还在街头叫卖的年代里常见的典型人物，常出现在描写城市童年的故事中
senses.example: The film opens with a newsboy singing through the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 电影从雨中边跑边唱的报童开始。
senses.why: The compound survives in memory and in literature long after the job itself faded.
senses.whyCN: 这份差事消失之后，这个词仍活在记忆与文学之中。

senses.title: The newsboy cap
senses.definition: a soft flat cap with a round crown, so called because it was worn by newspaper boys
senses.definitionCN: 带圆顶的柔软扁帽，因当年报童常戴而得名
senses.example: He wore a tweed newsboy cap and a long coat.
senses.exampleCN: 他戴着一顶花呢报童帽，穿着长风衣。
senses.why: The working boy of the street left his hat behind, so the compound is now a word for that hat.
senses.whyCN: 街头干活的男孩留下了他的帽子，于是这个词现在也指那顶帽子。

intro.en: Newsboy is a compound of news and boy, formed in English and first recorded in the middle of the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: newsboy 是 news 与 boy 构成的英语复合词，首次记录于十九世纪中叶。

items.en: News begins as a plural of new, meaning a report of something that has just happened.
items.cn: news 最初是 new 的复数形式，指刚刚发生之事的消息。

items.en: Boy means a male child, and its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: boy 意为男孩，其更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Printed sheets carrying recent reports turn news into the name of a product.
items.cn: 刊载近期消息的印刷纸张让 news 变成商品之名。

items.en: Cheap daily papers are sold by children on city streets, and the compound newsboy names them.
items.cn: 廉价日报由儿童在街头售卖，复合词 newsboy 用来称呼他们。

items.en: The same word spreads to the delivery boys who carry papers to homes.
items.cn: 同一个词也扩展到把报纸送到顾客家中的送报男孩。

items.en: The job almost disappears, but the newsboy cap keeps the compound alive.
items.cn: 这份差事几乎消失，但报童帽让这个词继续活着。

note.en: Newsboy belongs to the news family, and it sits beside the words for sellers of papers and for boys who work.
note.cn: newsboy 属于 news 词族，与「卖报的人」「做活的男孩」一类词义相邻。

entries.definition: printed sheets giving the news
a small stall where papers are sold
cheap paper used for newspapers
important enough to be reported
any person who sells papers
a person who travels around selling small goods
a person who carries messages or small items

normalIntro.en: Newsboy is a plain compound: the first half is the paper, the second half is the child who carries it.
normalIntro.cn: newsboy 是朴素的复合词：前半是报纸，后半是抱报纸的孩子。

normal.en: The word is news plus boy, so it needs no translation trick.
normal.cn: 这个词就是 news 加 boy，不需要什么翻译技巧。

normal.en: All papers are news things: newspaper, newsstand, and newsprint share the same first half.
normal.cn: 与报纸相关的词都带 news：newspaper、newsstand、newsprint 共用前半部分。

normal.en: The plural newsboys follows the usual rule for words ending in a vowel plus y.
normal.cn: 复数 newsboys 遵循「元音加 y 直接加 s」的规则。

normal.en: The newsboy cap is named after the boy, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 报童帽是以这个男孩命名的，而不是反过来。

normal.en: It is a countable noun, so one says a newsboy or the newsboys on the street.
normal.cn: 它是可数名词，可以说 a newsboy 或 the newsboys on the street。

abstract.en: Picture a small figure in a peaked cap, holding one paper folded under his arm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个戴鸭舌帽的小身影，腋下夹着一份折好的报纸。

abstract.en: Picture the sound of one voice calling the headlines over the traffic.
abstract.cn: 想象一个嗓音压过车流，喊出当天头条。

abstract.en: Picture the bundle on his shoulder, heavier than the boy himself.
abstract.cn: 想象他肩上那一捆报纸，比这个男孩还重。

examples.en: A newsboy ran between the carriages, selling the evening paper.
examples.cn: 一个报童在车厢之间穿行，卖着晚报。

examples.en: In those days, newsboys delivered papers to every street in the district.
examples.cn: 在那些日子里，报童把报纸送到这一带的每条街。

examples.en: He pulled on a flat newsboy cap before stepping outside.
examples.cn: 他出门前戴上一顶扁平的报童帽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛死报」——街头小报总写些离奇消息，男孩们边跑边喊；真正的词源只是 news 加 boy，这只是谐音联想。

root: 英语 news（新闻，由 new 的复数形式发展而来）+ boy（男孩，更早来源不确定）→ 十九世纪中叶合成 newsboy，核心义「抱着一摞报纸在街角卖报或送报的男孩」。

sensesIntro.en: Newsboy names a boy with papers in his arms: first one who calls out on the corner, then one who delivers to doors, then a remembered figure, and finally the cap that figure wore.
sensesIntro.cn: newsboy 指怀抱报纸的男孩：先是街角叫卖者，再是挨家投递者，然后是记忆中的典型人物，最后是他戴的那顶帽子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boy on a street corner with a bundle of papers under his arm.
core.cn: 核心意象：街角的男孩，腋下夹着一捆报纸。

branches.en: The selling sense is the original street job.
branches.cn: 卖报义项是最初的街头差事。

branches.en: The delivery sense grew as papers came into the home.
branches.cn: 送报义项随着报纸走进家庭而生长出来。

branches.en: Memory keeps the boy alive in stories and in the cap named after him.
branches.cn: 记忆让这个男孩留在故事里，也留在以他命名的帽子上。

branches.en: Both working senses share the paper carried and handed over.
branches.cn: 两个工作义项都共享「抱着报纸并交到别人手上」的动作。

branches.en: Both later senses turn the working boy into a shape or a mood.
branches.cn: 两个后起义项都把干活的男孩变成了一种造型或氛围。

intro.en: Newsboy is a two-part compound rather than a word with prefixes and suffixes, so its building blocks are the stems news and boy.
intro.cn: newsboy 是两段式复合词而非带前后缀的词，所以它的构件是词干 news 与 boy。

latinIntro.en: Neither half comes from Latin: news grows from the English new, and the earlier source of boy is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都不来自拉丁语：news 源于英语的 new，而 boy 的更早来源不确定。

items.example: News is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: news 是复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Boy is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: boy 是复合词的后半部分。

items.meaning: a boy who sells or delivers papers
items.example: A newsboy shouted the result from the corner.
items.exampleCN: 一个报童在街角喊出比赛结果。

items.example: Newspaper shares the news half.
items.exampleCN: newspaper 共用 news 这一半。

items.example: Newsstand shares the news half.
items.exampleCN: newsstand 共用 news 这一半。

items.example: Newsprint shares the news half.
items.exampleCN: newsprint 共用 news 这一半。

items.example: The suffix -worthy marks something worth reporting.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -worthy 表示值得报道。

items.example: The plural newsboys keeps the y after a vowel.
items.exampleCN: 复数 newsboys 中 y 前面是元音，因此保留 y。

items.meaning: a soft hat with a peak
items.example: The newsboy cap is named after the working boy.
items.exampleCN: 报童帽是以干活的报童命名的。

definition_zh: 简报；通讯；会员通讯
definition_en: a short printed or emailed report of news sent regularly to a group of people who share an interest
core_image: 一份折成三折的薄纸简报滑进信箱，上面印着俱乐部的名字和本月的消息
scene: 俱乐部每月给每位会员寄一份薄薄的通讯。Every month the club sends its members a short newsletter with the latest results.
sceneCN: 这里 newsletter 是「简报、通讯」（第 1 个义项：定期寄给特定群体的消息小报）；句意：俱乐部每个月给会员寄一份写有最新赛况的简短通讯。

pos.zh: 简报；通讯；会员通讯

derivatives.zh: 复合词前半部分的计词，义为「新闻；消息」
复合词后半部分，义为「信件」
由 news 与 paper 构成，义为「报纸」
由 newsletter 加 -er 构成，义为「编写通讯的人」
由 letter 与 head 构成，义为「信笺抬头」

senses.title: A short report sent to a group
senses.definition: a short report or bulletin containing news of a group, sent at regular intervals to its members or readers
senses.definitionCN: 刊载某个团体消息的简短报告或通报，定期寄给成员或读者
senses.example: The club newsletter lists next month matches.
senses.exampleCN: 俱乐部通讯列出了下个月的比赛。
senses.why: The word is news plus letter, so the core image is a letter whose whole purpose is news.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 news 加 letter，核心意象就是一封专门用来报消息的信。

senses.title: An email bulletin from a company
senses.definition: an email sent regularly by a company, shop, or website to customers to share updates and offers
senses.definitionCN: 公司、商店或网站定期发给顾客、介绍动态与优惠的电子邮件
senses.example: Sign up for our newsletter and get ten percent off.
senses.exampleCN: 订阅我们的通讯，即可享受九折优惠。
senses.why: When letters moved from paper to mailboxes in cyberspace, the same compound described the email bulletin.
senses.whyCN: 当信件从纸张移入网络信箱，同一个复合词便用来指电子邮件通讯。

senses.title: A school or workplace bulletin
senses.definition: a short bulletin printed by a school, college, or workplace to announce events and news to its community
senses.definitionCN: 由学校、学院或单位印发、向社区通报活动与消息的简短刊物
senses.example: The school newsletter came home in his bag every Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 每周五学校通讯都会装在他书包里带回家。
senses.why: Small communities need a light way to share news, so the compounded letter took over this local job.
senses.whyCN: 小社群需要轻便的消息分享方式，这个「报送消息的信」便承担了这份本地职责。

senses.title: A specialist news service for subscribers
senses.definition: a publication sold or given to subscribers who want news and analysis of one narrow field
senses.definitionCN: 面向订阅者出售或赠送、提供某一窄领域新闻与分析的出版物
senses.example: Investors pay for a private newsletter on farm prices.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者付费订阅一份农产品价格的私人通讯。
senses.why: Because it reaches only people who asked for it, the newsletter became a paid product of its own.
senses.whyCN: 因为它只送达主动索取的人，这种通讯本身就变成了一种付费产品。

intro.en: Newsletter is a compound of news and letter, and it first names short news sheets printed on behalf of clubs and companies.
intro.cn: newsletter 是 news 与 letter 构成的复合词，最初指俱乐部或公司印发的简短消息页。

items.en: Litera means a letter of the alphabet, then a written document.
items.cn: litera 指字母，继而指书面文件。

items.en: Lettre means a letter sent to someone.
items.cn: lettre 意为寄给某人的信件。

items.en: Letter enters English as a written message, and news names new happenings.
items.cn: letter 作为书面讯息进入英语，news 则指新发生的事。

items.en: Traders print short news letters for clients who need prices and results.
items.cn: 商人印出简短的消息信，供需要价格与行情的客户阅读。

items.en: The two words fuse into newsletter, a sheet of news for members of a group.
items.cn: 两个词融合成 newsletter，指发给团体成员的消息页。

items.en: The term moves to the email bulletin, which keeps the same name.
items.cn: 该词转而指电子邮件通讯，名称保持不变。

note.en: Newsletter shares the news family and sits beside the words for other short publications and for what arrives by mail.
note.cn: newsletter 同属 news 词族，与其它短刊物以及邮寄品的词义相邻。

entries.definition: printed sheets giving daily news
entries.definitionCN: 每日出版、刊登新闻的报纸

entries.definition: a stall selling papers
a written message sent to someone
the work of writing and sending newsletters
entries.definitionCN: 编写与寄发通讯的工作

entries.definition: a short official statement of news
a printed notice sent to many people
a thin booklet on one subject

normalIntro.en: Newsletter is news plus letter: a letter that carries news instead of private words.
normalIntro.cn: newsletter 就是 news 加 letter：一封不写私事、只报消息的信。

normal.en: The word is news plus letter, and both halves are common words.
normal.cn: 这个词是 news 加 letter，两半都是常见词。

normal.en: All paper words start with news: newspaper, newsstand, and newsletter.
normal.cn: 报纸类的词都以 news 开头：newspaper、newsstand、newsletter。

normal.en: The verb you use with it is subscribe, because a newsletter comes to people who asked for it.
normal.cn: 与它搭配的动词是 subscribe，因为通讯只送给主动订阅的人。

normal.en: Email newsletter and weekly newsletter are the two most common patterns.
normal.cn: email newsletter 与 weekly newsletter 是最常见的两种搭配。

normal.en: Plural is simply newsletters, with no change to the ending.
normal.cn: 复数直接加 s，写作 newsletters。

abstract.en: Picture a folded sheet sliding through a letterbox, its top line shouting a headline.
abstract.cn: 想象一张折好的纸滑进信箱，顶端一行就是醒目的标题。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded noticeboard replaced by one neat sheet handed to every member.
abstract.cn: 想象乱糟糟的公告栏被一张整洁的纸片取代，人手一份。

abstract.en: Picture an inbox with one red badge: the newsletter has arrived again.
abstract.cn: 想象收件箱里亮起一个红点：通讯又来了。

examples.en: The charity sends a newsletter to donors twice a year.
examples.cn: 这家慈善机构每年给捐款人寄两次简报。

examples.en: I unsubscribed from that newsletter after a week.
examples.cn: 一周后我就退订了那份通讯。

examples.en: Her article about the garden appeared in the village newsletter.
examples.cn: 她写的花园文章登在了村里的通讯上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛死勒特」——一头牛被勒得很紧，只好每月把消息写成小报寄出去；真正的词源只是 news 加 letter，这只是谐音联想。

root: 英语 news（新闻；消息，由 new 的复数形式发展而来）+ letter（信件，源自拉丁语 litera、古法语 lettre）→ 十八世纪合成 newsletter，核心义「一封只装消息、定期寄给特定人群的信」。

sensesIntro.en: Newsletter begins as a letter-like sheet of news for a group, then moves to the email bulletin, to school and workplace notices, and finally to paid specialist services.
sensesIntro.cn: newsletter 先指发给团体、像信一样的消息页，再指电子邮件通讯、学校与单位的通报，最后指付费的专业资讯服务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded sheet of news that lands in a letterbox.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张折好的消息纸落进信箱。

branches.en: The group bulletin is the original sense of the compound.
branches.cn: 团体简报是复合词最初的含义。

branches.en: The email bulletin moves the sheet into the inbox.
branches.cn: 电子邮件通讯把这张纸移进了收件箱。

branches.en: Schools and specialist publishers use the same form for local and paid news.
branches.cn: 学校与专业出版方用同一形式做本地消息与付费资讯。

branches.en: Both are issued on a schedule to people who belong or subscribe.
branches.cn: 两者都按固定周期发给成员或订阅者。

branches.en: Both need an active sign-up, so the reader is chosen rather than the street crowd.
branches.cn: 两者都需要主动订阅，读者是被选中的而非街上的人群。

intro.en: Newsletter is a two-part compound of two independent nouns, so its weight falls on the stems news and letter.
intro.cn: newsletter 是两个独立名词构成的复合词，重点在词干 news 与 letter 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin litera, a letter of the alphabet and a writing, gives the second half through Old French lettre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 litera（字母、文字）经古法语 lettre 提供了后半部分。

items.example: News is the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: news 是复合词的前半部分。

items.example: Letter is the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: letter 是复合词的后半部分。

items.example: Litera lies behind both letter and literacy.
items.exampleCN: litera 是 letter 与 literacy 的共同来源。

items.example: The firm mails a newsletter in spring.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司春天寄出一份通讯。

items.example: Newspaper shares the news half.
items.exampleCN: newspaper 共用 news 这一半。

items.example: Newsstand shares the news half.
items.exampleCN: newsstand 共用 news 这一半。

items.meaning: the printed heading of a letter
items.example: The newsletter carries the club name on its letterhead.
items.exampleCN: 通讯的信笺抬头印着俱乐部名称。

items.example: The suffix -er forms newsletterer, a person who makes one.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -er 构成 newsletterer，指编写通讯的人。

items.meaning: to arrange to receive something regularly
items.example: Most readers subscribe to one or two newsletters.
items.exampleCN: 大多数读者订阅一两份通讯。

definition_zh: 新闻纸；白报纸；印在报纸上的文字与报道
definition_en: cheap paper made mainly from ground wood pulp and used for printing newspapers, or the printed matter itself
core_image: 一叠灰白粗糙的纸卷，油墨还没干，沾得手指发黑
scene: 清晨的编辑部里，印刷机还在轰响，成捆的报纸被推下流水线。By dawn the press room smelled of ink and damp newsprint.
sceneCN: 这里 newsprint 是「新闻纸」（第 1 个义项：印刷报纸用的廉价纸张）；句意为天亮时印刷车间里满是油墨和潮湿新闻纸的气味。

pos.zh: 新闻纸；白报纸；印在报纸上的文字或报道

forms.label: 不可数名词（通常无复数）
新闻纸（较少见的可数说法）

derivatives.zh: 本词的第一部分，义为「新闻；消息」
本词的第二部分，义为「印刷；打印」
同一构词方式，义为「简讯；新闻信」
同一词头加 paper 构成，义为「报纸」

senses.title: Cheap paper for newspapers
senses.titleCN: 新闻纸：印报纸的廉价纸
senses.definition: an inexpensive paper made mainly from ground wood pulp and used for printing newspapers
senses.definitionCN: 用磨木浆为主制成的廉价纸张，专门用来印报纸
senses.example: The warehouse held huge rolls of newsprint.
senses.exampleCN: 仓库里堆着巨大的新闻纸卷。
senses.why: News brings the latest and print means pressing marks on paper, so the pair names the paper that carries the news.
senses.whyCN: news 指最新消息，print 指在纸上压出字迹，两者合起来就是承载消息的那种纸。

senses.title: The printed newspaper itself
senses.definition: newspapers as printed sheets, or the writing printed in them
senses.definitionCN: 作为印刷品的报纸，或印在报纸上的文字内容
senses.example: She is famous in print, not just in newsprint.
senses.exampleCN: 她出名靠的是印出来的文字，而不只是报纸本身。
senses.why: Since the paper is the material of the daily press, the word often stands for the newspaper and its printed text by metonymy.
senses.whyCN: 纸张本身是日报的载体，于是用材料代指报纸与报上的文字，这是转喻。

senses.title: A rough surface like newspaper
senses.titleCN: 像报纸那样粗糙的质感
senses.definition: a dull, slightly rough texture or finish resembling that of newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 类似报纸的那种灰白、略粗糙、不反光的质感
senses.example: The designer chose a newsprint finish for the poster.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师给这张海报选了类似新闻纸的质感。
senses.why: The look of that cheap grey paper became a named finish in design, borrowing the visual feel of the material.
senses.whyCN: 那种灰白廉价的纸张外观在设计界成了有名字的质地，借用的正是纸张给人的视觉感受。

senses.title: The world of paper reporting
senses.definition: the printed newspaper industry and its culture, seen as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 作为整体的纸质报业及其文化
senses.example: Many readers still trust newsprint more than online feeds.
senses.exampleCN: 许多读者仍然比信任网络信息流更信任报纸。
senses.why: By a further widening of meaning, the material stands for the whole trade and tradition that prints on it.
senses.whyCN: 意义再扩大一步，材料就代指整个印在它上面的行业与传统，即纸质报业。

senses.title: A pile of old papers
senses.definition: heaps of old newspapers, for example in a recycling drive
senses.definitionCN: 成堆的旧报纸，例如回收活动中的废报
senses.example: The school collected sacks of newsprint for recycling.
senses.exampleCN: 学校收集了好几袋旧报纸去回收。
senses.why: Once read, the cheap paper quickly becomes waste weight, so the word also names the mass of old copies.
senses.whyCN: 读完之后，这种廉价纸很快变成可称量的废料，于是这个词也指一堆堆旧报纸。

intro.en: Newsprint is a modern English compound of news and print, first recorded in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: newsprint 是现代英语把 news 与 print 组合而成的复合词，十九世纪开始有记录。

items.en: Newes is the plural of an old word for something new, giving the modern news.
items.cn: newes 是古词「新事物」的复数形式，后来演变出现代英语的 news。

items.en: Preinte is a mark pressed onto a surface, the ancestor of print.
items.cn: preinte 指压印在表面上的痕迹，是 print 的前身。

items.en: Print names the act of pressing type onto paper, from Latin premere.
items.cn: 中古英语 print 指把铅字压印到纸上的动作，源自拉丁语 premere（压）。

items.en: The noun newsprint is dated to the mid nineteenth century, when cheap mechanical pulp met the daily press.
items.cn: 名词 newsprint 一般认为见于十九世纪中叶，当时廉价的机械木浆正遇上兴起的日报。

items.en: Commercial newsprint becomes a commodity traded by the ton, and recycling gives the word a second life.
items.cn: 二十世纪商业新闻纸成为按吨交易的商品，回收利用又让这个词有了新的用法。

items.en: Modern English also uses newsprint as a loose label for the printed press as a whole.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 newsprint 用作「纸质报业」的泛称。

note.en: Newsprint sits beside news and print, and near the names of the things printed and the trade that prints them.
note.cn: newsprint 由 news 与 print 拼成，与「印出来的东西」和「印这些东西的行业」的称谓相邻。

entries.definition: the rare countable plural of newsprint
entries.definitionCN: 很少使用的可数复数形式；材料义通常不可数，不用复数

entries.definition: a paper printed and sold with news
entries.definitionCN: 报纸；与 newsprint 共享 news 词头，区别在于 newspaper 指成品报纸

entries.definition: to press type onto paper
entries.definitionCN: 印刷；与 newsprint 共享 print 一词

entries.definition: thin sheets used for writing and printing
entries.definitionCN: 纸；泛指书写印刷的材料

entries.definition: soft wet fibre from wood, used to make paper
entries.definitionCN: 木浆；造纸用的湿纤维原料

entries.definition: a small-format popular newspaper

normalIntro.en: Newsprint is simply news plus print: the paper that prints the news.
normalIntro.cn: newsprint 就是 news 加 print：印新闻的那种纸。

normal.en: News plus print gives the paper that prints the news.
normal.cn: news 加 print 就是「印新闻的纸」。

normal.en: Newsprint is cheap, so it is made from ground wood pulp, not fine rags.
normal.cn: newsprint 很廉价，所以用磨木浆而不上等布浆制造。

normal.en: Newsprint is uncountable: you buy it by the ton, not by the piece.
normal.cn: newsprint 是不可数名词：按吨买，而不是按张买。

normal.en: Newspaper is the finished product; newsprint is the material it is made from.
normal.cn: newspaper 是成品报纸；newsprint 是造它的材料。

normal.en: Recovered newsprint is one of the easiest papers to recycle.
normal.cn: 旧新闻纸是最容易回收的纸类之一。

abstract.en: Picture a fat roll of grey paper being fed into a thundering press.
abstract.cn: 想象一大卷灰白纸被送进轰鸣的印刷机。

abstract.en: Imagine ink on that cheap paper rubbing off on your fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象那廉价纸上的油墨蹭到了你的手指上。

abstract.en: Think of reading a report that came straight off the newspaper page, told in the page itself.
abstract.cn: 想象你在读一篇直接印在报页上的报道，由那一页纸本身来讲述。

examples.en: The cost of newsprint has risen sharply this year.
examples.cn: 今年新闻纸的成本大幅上涨。

examples.en: Old newsprint can be recycled into new paper.
examples.cn: 旧报纸可以回收做成新的纸张。

examples.en: The smell of fresh newsprint still reminds him of his first job.
examples.cn: 新鲜新闻纸的气味仍让他想起自己的第一份工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「纽斯普林特」可谐音记作「牛死扑棱」，想象一头牛扑倒在印刷纸卷上；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语复合词：news（新闻）+ print（印刷；压印，源自拉丁语 premere）→ newsprint，字面即「印新闻的纸」。

sensesIntro.en: Newsprint starts as the material for newspapers, widens to the printed paper and its text, then to the industry and finally to heaps of old copies.
sensesIntro.cn: newsprint 从「印报纸的材料」出发，扩展到报纸与报上文字，再到整个纸质报业，最后落到成堆的旧报纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough grey paper roll that takes the smell of ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：一卷灰白粗糙、吃满油墨气味的纸。

branches.en: The material sense is the literal core of the word.
branches.cn: 材料义是这个词字面上的核心。

branches.en: Calling the newspaper newsprint is a metonymy: the material stands for the product.
branches.cn: 把报纸叫作 newsprint 是转喻：材料代指成品。

branches.en: The visual feel of the paper becomes a named surface in design.
branches.cn: 纸张的外观感受在设计里成了有名字的表面质感。

branches.en: The industry sense widens the material into a whole trade and tradition.
branches.cn: 行业义把材料扩大成整个行业与传统。

branches.en: New sheets and discarded sheets are the same material at two moments of use.
branches.cn: 新纸和废报是同一材料在使用的两个阶段。

intro.en: Newsprint is a transparent English compound, built from two common words rather than from a Latin root.
intro.cn: newsprint 是透明的英语复合词，由两个常用词拼成，并不依赖拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The print half goes back to Latin premere through Old French, while news has no clear Latin ancestor.
latinIntro.cn: print 这一半经古法语上溯拉丁语 premere（压），而 news 没有明确的拉丁祖先。

items.example: News is the first half of newsprint.
items.exampleCN: news 是 newsprint 的前一半。

items.example: Print is the second half of newsprint.
items.exampleCN: print 是 newsprint 的后一半。

items.meaningCN: news 内部已含的旧复数词尾
items.example: The s in news came from an old plural.
items.exampleCN: news 里的 s 来自旧的复数形式。

items.example: Newspaper swaps print for paper.
items.exampleCN: newspaper 把 print 换成了 paper。

items.example: Newsletter shares the news first half.
items.exampleCN: newsletter 共享 news 词头。

items.meaning: machines and people that print news
items.example: The press feeds newsprint.
items.exampleCN: 印报机吃新闻纸。

items.example: Premere lies behind print.
items.exampleCN: premere 是 print 深处的源头。

items.example: Newsprint is mostly pulp.
items.exampleCN: newsprint 主要是纸浆。

items.example: Recycle old newsprint into boxes.
items.exampleCN: 把旧新闻纸回收做纸盒。

latinEntries.example: Premere is the distant source of print.
latinEntries.exampleCN: premere 是 print 的远祖。

latinEntries.example: Prelum and print share the pressing image.
latinEntries.exampleCN: prelum 与 print 共享「压」的意象。

definition_zh: 新闻短片；新闻纪录片；新闻片行业
definition_en: a short film of news events shown in cinemas before the main feature, or the printed press compared to moving footage
core_image: 老电影院里，幕布上跳动着黑白画面，片头字幕写着当周要闻
scene: 战前的电影院里，灯光暗下，观众先看到一段黑白新闻片。Every visit to the cinema began with a newsreel of the week.
sceneCN: 这里 newsreel 是「新闻短片」（第 1 个义项：正片前放映的新闻影片）；句意为每回去电影院，开头都是一段一周新闻片。

pos.zh: 新闻短片；新闻纪录片；新闻片

derivatives.zh: 本词第一部分，义为「新闻；消息」
本词第二部分，义为「卷轴；一卷胶片」
由本词加 footage 构成的复合说法，义为「新闻片素材」
同一 news 词族，义为「新闻记者」

senses.title: A short film of the week
senses.definition: a short film presenting news events, once shown in cinemas before the main picture
senses.definitionCN: 报道新闻事件的短片，过去在电影院放正片之前放映
senses.example: The newsreel showed the new bridge opening.
senses.exampleCN: 新闻短片里放了大桥通车的画面。
senses.why: News supplies the content and reel the physical roll of film, so the word names a roll that carries the news.
senses.whyCN: news 提供内容，reel 指一卷实体胶片，合起来就是「载着新闻的一卷片子」。

senses.title: Old footage as a record
senses.definition: historical news footage used later in documentaries and archives
senses.definitionCN: 后来被纪录片和档案馆使用的历史新闻片素材
senses.example: The film opens with grainy newsreel from the war.
senses.exampleCN: 影片以战争年代颗粒粗大的新闻片开场。
senses.why: The films outlived the cinemas, so the word now labels the surviving footage used as a historical record.
senses.whyCN: 影片比当年的影院活得更久，于是这个词转指存留下来、当作历史记录的影像素材。

senses.title: The newsreel trade
senses.definition: the industry that made and distributed cinema news films
senses.definitionCN: 制作与发行影院新闻片的行业
senses.example: He spent thirty years working in newsreel.
senses.exampleCN: 他在新闻片行业干了三十年。
senses.why: As with other craft nouns, the product stands for the whole trade that makes it.
senses.whyCN: 和许多工艺名词一样，产品本身代指整个制作它的行业。

senses.title: Cinema as a news medium
senses.definition: the cinema as a means of spreading news, contrasted with print
senses.definitionCN: 作为传播新闻手段的电影，与纸媒形成对照
senses.example: Before television, newsreel was the only moving picture news.
senses.exampleCN: 在电视出现之前，新闻片是唯一的动态新闻。
senses.why: When comparing media, the word stands for the whole channel and not one film on a screen.
senses.whyCN: 比较不同媒介时，这个词代表的是整个渠道，而不是幕布上的某一部片子。

senses.title: A rapid review of events
senses.titleCN: 一连串飞快闪过的新闻
senses.definition: a rapid sequence of news items passing quickly like a film
senses.definitionCN: 一串像电影镜头一样飞快闪过的新闻事件
senses.example: My year passed like a newsreel of small disasters.
senses.exampleCN: 这一年像一串小灾小难的新闻短片从我眼前掠过。
senses.why: The quick cutting of newsreels makes the word a metaphor for any rush of events.
senses.whyCN: 新闻片快速切换镜头的手法，使这个词成为比喻，指任何一连串急速发生的事。

intro.en: Newsreel is a twentieth-century English compound of news and reel, the reel being the spool that held film.
intro.cn: newsreel 是二十世纪英语把 news 与 reel（绕胶片的卷轴）拼成的复合词。

items.en: Newes is the plural of an old word for something new, giving news.
items.cn: newes 是古词「新事物」的复数，后来变成 news。

items.en: Reel comes from Old English hreol, a revolving spool or a lively dance motion.
items.cn: reel 来自古英语 hreol，指旋转的线轴，也指打转的舞步。

items.en: The reconstructed form hrehula, meaning something wound or spun, lies behind the reels.
items.cn: 一般认为其原始日耳曼语重构形式 hrehula（缠绕旋转之物）是这些「卷轴」词的源头。

items.en: Once film came on spools, newsreel named the short news film shown in cinemas.
items.cn: 电影胶片开始绕在卷轴上之后，newsreel 便指影院放映的新闻短片。

items.en: From the nineteen thirties to the fifties the newsreel was standard in cinemas and shared footage with early television.
items.cn: 二十世纪三十到五十年代，新闻片是影院标配，也和早期电视共用素材。

items.en: After television replaced it, the word survives mostly for historical footage and for metaphorical use.
items.cn: 被电视取代之后，这个词主要残留于历史素材与比喻用法中。

note.en: Newsreel is a news compound, close to other news words and to the moving-image news it once was.
note.cn: newsreel 是 news 词族的复合词，与别的 news 词以及它当年的「动态新闻」同类表达相邻。

entries.definition: a spool that holds film or thread
entries.definitionCN: 绕胶片或线的卷轴；也是本词的后半部分

entries.definition: cheap paper used for newspapers
entries.definitionCN: 新闻纸；与 newsreel 共享 news 词头，但指纸张材料

entries.definition: a regular short bulletin of news
entries.definitionCN: 简讯；与 newsreel 共享 news 词头，但指定期印刷的简报

entries.definition: a factual film giving a record of real events
entries.definitionCN: 纪录片；记录真实事件的影片

entries.definition: a length of filmed material
a programme sent out by radio or television

normalIntro.en: Newsreel is news on a reel: one spool of film carrying the week.
normalIntro.cn: newsreel 就是装在一卷卷轴上的新闻：一卷胶片讲完这一周。

normal.en: News plus reel gives one spool of film carrying the news.
normal.cn: news 加 reel 就是「一卷载着新闻的胶片」。

normal.en: The plural newsreels is regular, so the word behaves like an ordinary countable noun.
normal.cn: 复数 newsreels 按常规变化，说明它是普通可数名词。

normal.en: A reel is what a spool winds film onto, which explains why film reels share the word.
normal.cn: reel 是绕胶片的卷轴，所以「胶片卷」也叫 reel。

normal.en: Newsreel was played before the main film, so cinema-goers saw the week before the story.
normal.cn: 新闻片在正片前放映，所以观众是先看这一周，再看故事片。

normal.en: Compare newsprint: newsprint is paper news, newsreel is filmed news.
normal.cn: 对比 newsprint：newsprint 是纸上的新闻，newsreel 是拍成胶片的新闻。

abstract.en: Picture a spool spinning while black and white crowds march on the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象卷轴飞转，黑白画面里人群在幕布上走过。

abstract.en: Imagine a week of events squeezed into ten minutes before the feature.
abstract.cn: 想象一周的事情被压进正片前的十分钟里。

abstract.en: Think of a projector screeching as the spool runs out.
abstract.cn: 想象胶片放完时放映机发出刺耳的响声。

examples.en: Archive newsreels are a rich source for historians.
examples.cn: 档案新闻片是历史学者丰富的资料来源。

examples.en: The opening newsreel shows the crowds waiting in the rain.
examples.cn: 开场新闻片里，人群在雨中等待。

examples.en: Television closed most newsreels down by the sixties.
examples.cn: 到六十年代，电视让大多数新闻片停办了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「纽斯瑞尔」可谐音记作「牛撕卷儿」，想象一头牛撕开一圈电影胶片；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语复合词：news（新闻）+ reel（卷轴，古英语 hreol，原始日耳曼语重构形式 hrehula）→ newsreel，字面即「卷在轴上的新闻胶片」。

sensesIntro.en: Newsreel names the cinema short film, then the surviving footage, the trade, the medium, and any rapid rush of events.
sensesIntro.cn: newsreel 先指影院新闻短片，再指留存下来的片源、这一行业、这一媒介，最后比喻飞快闪过的一连串事件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a spool of film unrolling the week in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中一卷胶片把这一周徐徐展开。

branches.en: The cinema short is the literal sense: a reel of news film.
branches.cn: 影院短片是本义：一卷新闻胶片。

branches.en: When the cinemas closed, the films themselves became the archive sense.
branches.cn: 影院消失之后，影片本身就变成了档案素材义。

branches.en: The product lends its name to the trade that produced it.
branches.cn: 产品把名字借给了生产它的行业。

branches.en: The medium sense treats the word as the name of a channel of news.
branches.cn: 媒介义把这个词当作一种新闻渠道的名称。

branches.en: Old footage shown quickly and a rush of events share the same flickering rhythm.
branches.cn: 快放的老片与飞快闪过的事件共享同一种跳动的节奏。

intro.en: Newsreel is a plain English compound, so its interest lies in how the two words combine rather than in Latin parts.
intro.cn: newsreel 是平实的英语复合词，看点在于两个词的组合方式，而不是拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: news grew from an English word for something new, and reel descends from an Old English spool word.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁词：news 源自英语中表示「新事物」的词，reel 源自古英语的卷轴词。

items.example: News is the first half of newsreel.
items.exampleCN: news 是 newsreel 的前一半。

items.meaning: a spool for film or thread
items.example: Reel is the second half of newsreel.
items.exampleCN: reel 是 newsreel 的后一半。

items.example: Hreol is the Old English ancestor of reel.
items.exampleCN: hreol 是 reel 的古英语祖先。

items.meaningCN: news 内部已含的旧复数词尾
items.example: The s in news came from an old plural.
items.exampleCN: news 里的 s 来自旧的复数形式。

items.example: Newsprint swaps reel for print.
items.exampleCN: newsprint 把 reel 换成了 print。

items.example: Footage is counted like reel in the trade.
items.exampleCN: 在业内，素材和胶片卷一样按长度计量。

items.example: Cinema showed each newsreel before the feature.
items.exampleCN: 电影院在正片前放每一段新闻片。

items.example: Archive newsreels survive as records.
items.exampleCN: 档案新闻片作为记录留存下来。

definition_zh: 单页新闻纸；传单式启事；简报；消息灵通的报纸
definition_en: a single sheet of paper giving the news, either a simple handout or, more rarely, a lively popular newspaper
core_image: 一张油印的单页纸，被钉在公告板上，边角已经卷起
scene: 小镇的布告栏前围了几个人，一张油印纸贴着新消息。The newssheet reported the market prices for the coming week.
sceneCN: 这里 newssheet 是「单页简报」（第 1 个义项：只印在一张纸上的新闻或启事）；句意为那张简报登了下周的市场行情。

pos.zh: 单页新闻纸；传单式启事；简报

derivatives.zh: 本词第一部分，义为「新闻；消息」
本词第二部分，义为「一张纸；薄片」
同一构词方式，义为「报纸」，指多页的正式日报
同类事物，义为「单面大张印刷品」

senses.title: A single sheet of news
senses.definition: a small publication printed on one sheet and given free or sold cheaply
senses.definitionCN: 只印在一张纸上的小型出版物，免费发放或廉价出售
senses.example: The newssheet listed the farmers market prices.
senses.exampleCN: 这张单页简报列出了农贸市场的价格。
senses.why: News gives the content and sheet the physical form, so the word literally names one sheet carrying the news.
senses.whyCN: news 给出内容，sheet 给出形制，字面就是「一张载着消息的纸」。

senses.title: A rough handout
senses.definition: a rough, quickly made leaflet handed out on the street or pinned on a wall
senses.definitionCN: 粗制、赶印的传单，在街头散发或贴在墙上
senses.example: He folded the newssheet and put it in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把传单折起来塞进口袋。
senses.why: Since the form is cheap and single, the word also implies something improvised rather than a finished paper.
senses.whyCN: 因为形制廉价、只有一张，这个词也暗示它是临时凑出来的，而非正式报纸。

senses.title: A community bulletin
senses.definition: the short circular of a school, club, or village that keeps members in touch
senses.definitionCN: 学校、社团或村庄用来联络成员的小型简讯
senses.example: The church newssheet announces the winter fair.
senses.exampleCN: 教会简报公布了冬季游乐会的消息。
senses.why: A single sheet is enough for a small group, so the word grew into the bulletin sense.
senses.whyCN: 对一个小群体来说一张纸就够用，于是这个词长出了「简报」这一义项。

senses.title: A paper with the latest
senses.definition: a lively newspaper that prints the most recent news and gossip
senses.definitionCN: 刊载最新消息与八卦、办得热闹的报纸
senses.example: That newssheet was the first to print the story.
senses.exampleCN: 那份小报是第一个登出这则消息的。
senses.why: Older usage praised a paper that printed the freshest news, and the compound kept that admiring sense.
senses.whyCN: 较早的用法里，这个词是称赞一份报纸「登的是最新消息」，这种褒义被保留下来。

senses.title: Like a sheet of news
senses.definition: a very short piece of writing that fits on one sheet in newspaper style
senses.definitionCN: 符合报纸体例、一页纸就能写完的短文
senses.example: Her column reads like a newssheet of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的专栏读起来就像一页周报。
senses.why: The short form becomes a metaphor for writing that is brief, plain, and full of news.
senses.whyCN: 单页的形式被拿来比喻简短、直白、塞满消息的文字。

intro.en: Newssheet is an English compound of news and sheet, with the sense of a sheet printed with news dating from the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: newssheet 是 news 与 sheet 的英语复合词，「印着新闻的纸页」这一义项一般认为可追溯到十六世纪。

items.en: Newes is the plural of an old word for something new, giving news.
items.cn: newes 是古词「新事物」的复数，后来变成 news。

items.en: Sceat is one of the oldest English words for a broad flat piece of cloth or paper.
items.cn: sceat 是最古老的英语词之一，指宽而平的一片布料或纸。

items.en: The reconstructed form skauta, meaning a corner or a projecting piece, lies behind sheet.
items.cn: 一般认为 sheet 的源头是原始日耳曼语重构形式 skauta，意为「一角、突出的一片」。

items.en: Cheap hand printing lets a single sheet circulate each week, and news sheet names it.
items.cn: 手工印刷变得便宜，一张纸就能每周流通，于是出现了表示这种纸页的说法。

items.en: Popular papers eager for fresh news are praised in older writing as newssheets.
items.cn: 十九世纪的旧文献里，抢最新消息的通俗报纸会被称作 newssheet。

items.en: Today newssheet usually names a small bulletin for a school, club, or village.
items.cn: 今天这个词通常指学校、社团或村庄的小型简报。

note.en: Newssheet is a news compound on the edge of the paper world, closest to leaflets, bulletins, and the newspapers it rarely grows into.
note.cn: newssheet 处在纸媒词群的边缘，与传单、简报以及偶尔长成的报纸最近。

entries.definition: a broad flat piece of paper
entries.definitionCN: 一张纸；薄片；也是本词的后半部分

entries.definition: cheap paper used for newspapers
entries.definitionCN: 新闻纸；与 newssheet 共享 news 词头，但指纸张材料

entries.definition: a regular short bulletin
entries.definitionCN: 简讯；与 newssheet 意义最接近，但强调定期寄递

entries.definition: a small printed sheet given to people
entries.definitionCN: 传单；散发给人的印刷小张纸

entries.definition: a short official statement of news
a handbill handed out to passers-by

normalIntro.en: Newssheet is news squeezed onto a sheet, more leaflet than newspaper.
normalIntro.cn: newssheet 就是把新闻塞进一张纸里，更像传单而不是报纸。

normal.en: News plus sheet gives a single sheet of news.
normal.cn: news 加 sheet 就是「一张新闻纸」。

normal.en: Sheet goes back to Old English sceat, one of the oldest words for a flat piece.
normal.cn: sheet 可上溯古英语 sceat，是最古老的「平片」词之一。

normal.en: Newssheet is countable, so its plural newsheets is a pile of handouts, not a product sold.
normal.cn: newssheet 可数，复数 newssheets 指一叠传单，而不是可售的成品。

normal.en: Newspaper is the serious relative; newssheet stays small, quick, and local.
normal.cn: newspaper 是正经的亲戚；newssheet 始终又小又快又本地。

normal.en: Newssheet sits between newsletter and leaflet: regular like the one, thin like the other.
normal.cn: newssheet 介于 newsletter 与 leaflet 之间：像前者一样按期出，像后者一样只有一张。

abstract.en: Picture a scrawled sheet pinned to a village board, curling at the corners.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手写潦草的纸钉在村口布告栏上，边角卷起。

abstract.en: Imagine a hand passing you one thin page on the street.
abstract.cn: 想象有人在大街上把一张薄纸递到你手里。

abstract.en: Think of a school notice that fits on a single page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张学校通知，一页纸就写得下。

examples.en: The newssheet is pinned up by the school gate.
examples.cn: 那份简报贴在校园门口。

examples.en: They printed a newssheet once a month for the town.
examples.cn: 他们每月为镇上印一期简报。

examples.en: A rough newssheet on the noticeboard warned of the road closures.
examples.cn: 公告栏上一张粗糙的简报提醒了封路消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「纽斯希特」可谐音记作「牛撕细纸」，想象一头牛撕开一张薄薄的新闻纸；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 现代英语复合词：news（新闻）+ sheet（一张纸，古英语 sceat，原始日耳曼语重构形式 skauta）→ newssheet，字面即「一张新闻纸」。

sensesIntro.en: Newssheet narrows the idea of a sheet of news from the literal single page, to a rough handout, to a local bulletin, and widens once to a lively paper.
sensesIntro.cn: newssheet 从字面的一页新闻纸出发，收窄为粗糙传单与社区简报，又偶尔放宽为一份抢新闻的报纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one curling sheet of paper on which the news was printed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张边角卷起、印满消息的纸。

branches.en: The single sheet of news is the literal sense of the compound.
branches.cn: 一页新闻纸是这个词造字的字面义。

branches.en: Because it is cheap and thin, the sheet reads as a rough handout.
branches.cn: 因为廉价又单薄，这张纸就被读成粗糙的传单。

branches.en: A handout passed around a small community turns into a regular bulletin.
branches.cn: 在小群体里传阅的传单，逐渐变成定期的简报。

branches.en: Old praise for a paper with the freshest news kept an approving sense alive.
branches.cn: 旧时对「登最新消息的报纸」的赞誉，让一种褒义用法延续下来。

branches.en: The bulletin and the sheet-sized column share a single-page plainness.
branches.cn: 社区简报与一页纸式的专栏，共享单页、直白的特点。

intro.en: Newssheet is a plain English compound of two native words, with no prefix or suffix of its own.
intro.cn: newssheet 是两个英语本土词构成的普通复合词，本身没有前后缀。

latinIntro.en: Neither half is Latin: news grew from an English word for something new, and sheet descends from Old English sceat.
latinIntro.cn: 两半都不是拉丁词：news 源自英语中表示「新事物」的词，sheet 源自古英语 sceat。

items.exampleCN: sceat 是 sheet 的古英语祖先。

items.meaningCN: news 内部已含的旧复数词尾
items.example: The s in news came from an old plural.
items.exampleCN: news 里的 s 来自旧的复数形式。

items.example: Newspaper swaps sheet for paper.
items.exampleCN: newspaper 把 sheet 换成了 paper。

items.meaning: a small printed sheet for handouts
items.example: A leaflet is a newssheet made to advertise.
items.exampleCN: 传单就是用来做广告的单页新闻纸。

items.example: A club prints a bulletin or newssheet.
items.exampleCN: 社团印的是公告或简报。

items.example: Print a newssheet for Friday.
items.exampleCN: 印一份周五的简报。

items.example: Noticeboard is where a newssheet hangs.
items.exampleCN: 简报就挂在布告栏上。

definition_zh: 壁龛；合适的位置或工作；生态位；商机；缝隙市场
definition_en: a shallow recess in a wall, an especially suitable place or role, and in biology a species place in an ecosystem
core_image: 墙面上凹进去的一小块空间，刚好放下一尊雕像
scene: 教堂墙面上凹进去一小块地方，正好安放一尊石雕圣像。In the old church, a dusty niche in the wall held a small stone saint.
sceneCN: 这里 niche 是「壁龛」（第 1 个义项：墙面上凹进去用来放东西的小空间）；句意：在古旧的教堂里，墙上一个积灰的壁龛里安放着一尊石头圣像。

pos.zh: 壁龛；合适的位置或工作；生态位；商机
专门针对特定小群体的（作定语）

collocations.zh: 找到合适的位置；找到自己的定位
开辟出一片天地；确立一席之地

derivatives.zh: 有壁龛的；置于壁龛中的（由名词加 -ed 构成）
没有合适位置的；缺乏专属定位的（较少用）

senses.title: A recess in a wall
senses.definition: a shallow space cut or built into a wall, often to hold a statue, a lamp, or small objects
senses.definitionCN: 在墙面上挖出或砌出的浅凹处，常用来放雕像、灯或小物件
senses.example: A brass lamp stood in the niche beside the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门旁的壁龛里放着一盏铜灯。
senses.why: The French noun means a nest in a wall, from Italian nicchia, and the hollow itself is the original image.
senses.whyCN: 法语名词本义是「墙上的一个巢」，来自意大利语 nicchia，凹进去的空间正是这个词最早的形象。

senses.title: A comfortable place
senses.titleCN: 合适的位置；惬意的角落
senses.definition: a position or place that suits a person or thing especially well and feels protected
senses.definitionCN: 特别适合某人或某物、让人感到被保护的位置或地方
senses.example: By the fire he found his own quiet niche.
senses.exampleCN: 炉火边他找到了属于自己的安静角落。
senses.why: If a niche is the space that holds a statue exactly, it naturally comes to mean the spot that fits one person exactly.
senses.whyCN: 壁龛恰好承托一尊雕像，这个「正好合身」的特点自然引申为某人恰如其分的位置。

senses.title: A suitable role or job
senses.titleCN: 合适的工作；恰当的角色
senses.definition: a job, role, or activity for which someone is especially suited
senses.definitionCN: 特别适合某人的工作、角色或活动
senses.example: Teaching part time gave her a niche in the conservation world.
senses.exampleCN: 兼职教书让她在文物保护领域有了合适的位置。
senses.why: Careers copied the wall image: each person looks for the opening that fits, an office carved for them alone.
senses.whyCN: 职业领域沿用了「墙面上的凹处」这一形象：每个人都寻找恰好合身的缺口，一个像是为自己凿出来的职位。

senses.title: An ecological niche
senses.definition: the role and position of a species within its environment, including how it feeds and reproduces
senses.definitionCN: 物种在其环境中的角色与位置，包括它如何取食和繁殖
senses.example: Two species that share a niche will compete for the same food.
senses.exampleCN: 共用一个生态位的两个物种会争夺同样的食物。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the word: just as each object needs its own hollow in a shelf, each species occupies its own slot in an ecosystem.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用这个词：正如每件物品都需要架子上自己的凹槽，每个物种在生态系统里也占据自己的位置。

senses.title: A gap in the market
senses.definition: a small, specialized part of a market that a business can serve profitably
senses.definitionCN: 市场上较小而有专门需求的片段，企业可以从中获利
senses.example: The bakery built its business on a niche: gluten free bread.
senses.exampleCN: 这家面包店靠一个细分市场起家：无麸质面包。
senses.why: Business language keeps the image: a niche is a narrow opening that big firms overlook, where a small firm can fit perfectly.
senses.whyCN: 商业语言保留了这个形象：壁龛是一道大公司忽视的窄缝，小公司却恰恰能严丝合缝地嵌进去。

senses.title: The adjective use
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean aimed at a small, specific group of people
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示面向某一小群特定的人
senses.example: These niche magazines sell to a very small readership.
senses.exampleCN: 这些小众杂志的读者群非常小。
senses.why: The noun turned into a modifier, so any product, hobby, or service can now be called niche if it serves only a narrow group.
senses.whyCN: 名词转作修饰语后，任何只服务一小群人的产品、爱好或服务都可以称作小众。

intro.en: Niche comes from French niche, a recess in a wall, probably from Italian nicchia, itself of uncertain origin.
intro.cn: niche 来自法语 niche（墙上的凹处），一般认为是经由意大利语 nicchia 而来，更深层的来源不确定。

items.en: Nicchia names a shell like hollow, and its origin is uncertain.
items.cn: nicchia 指贝壳似的凹处，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Niche means a recess, often a simple dog like nest in a wall.
items.cn: niche 意为墙上凹处，早期也指墙上留出的一个洞。

items.en: English borrows the word for a shallow recess that holds a statue or lamp.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，指用来放雕像或灯的浅凹处。

items.en: In 1820 the Swedish chemist Berzelius is credited with naming the element, and English takes the word from Swedish or German usage of the same ore name.
items.cn: 一般认为到十九世纪二十年代由瑞典化学家贝采利乌斯正式为这种元素定名，英语则借用了瑞典语或德语对同一矿石名称的用法。

items.en: The sense widens to a suitable place or role in life, as in finding a niche.
items.cn: 词义扩展到生活中合适的位置或角色，如找到自己的定位。

items.en: Ecology adopts ecological niche, and business adopts niche market.
items.cn: 生态学采用生态位这一说法，商业界有了细分市场。

note.en: Niche sits beside its homophones and near synonyms: the spelling kn- is a different root, and words for hollows or market gaps describe similar pictures.
note.cn: niche 与同音词、近义词相邻：写成 kn- 的词是另一个词根，而表示凹处或市场空隙的词描绘着相似的画面。

entries.definition: an older spelling of niche, now considered nonstandard
entries.definitionCN: niche 的旧拼法，现已视为不规范

entries.definition: a person trained to help women give birth; only the ending sounds alike, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 助产士；只是词尾读音相似，词源不同

entries.definition: a baked dumpling filled with potato or cheese; just spelling under English rules, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 一种烤制的面食团子；只是按照英语规则读音相近，词源不同

a field or product in which a person or firm is expert
a part of a market or audience

normalIntro.en: Niche is a hollow that fits exactly: a wall opening, a suitable job, or a narrow gap in the market.
normalIntro.cn: niche 是一个恰好合身的凹处：墙上的开口、适合自己的工作、或者市场上的一道窄缝。

normal.en: Find a niche means to discover the place where you belong.
normal.cn: find a niche 指找到属于自己的位置。

normal.en: A niche market serves only a small, specific group of buyers.
normal.cn: niche market 只服务一小群特定买家。

normal.en: An ecological niche is a species place in nature.
normal.cn: ecological niche 是物种在自然中的位置。

normal.en: Carve out a niche uses the image of cutting a hollow into stone.
normal.cn: carve out a niche 借用了在石头上凿出凹处的画面。

normal.en: Compare recess: recess is the plain physical hollow, while niche also carries the ideas of fit and belonging.
normal.cn: 对比 recess：recess 只是物理上的凹处，而 niche 还带有「合身、归属」的意味。

abstract.en: Picture a statue standing in a wall hollow built just for it.
abstract.cn: 想象一尊雕像立在专为它砌出的墙洞中。

abstract.en: Imagine a key slot in a door that accepts only one key.
abstract.cn: 想象门上一道只接受一把钥匙的锁孔。

abstract.en: Think of a small shop that serves one product no big store carries.
abstract.cn: 想象一家小店只卖大商店不卖的那一样东西。

examples.en: The statue was placed in a niche above the altar.
examples.cn: 雕像被安放在祭坛上方的一个壁龛里。

examples.en: After years of training, she finally found her niche in forensic biology.
examples.cn: 经过多年训练，她终于在法医生物学领域找到了自己的位置。

examples.en: Small firms often survive by serving a niche market.
examples.cn: 小公司常常靠服务细分市场而生存。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内池」——墙面往里凹陷成一个小池子放雕像，就是壁龛；再由「刚好合适的凹槽」联想到适合自己的工作与市场缺口。这只是拆字联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定。一般认为是意大利语 nicchia（贝壳状凹处）→ 法语 niche（墙上的凹处）→ 英语 niche（壁龛），核心义「恰好合身的凹处」再引申到位置、职位、生态位与市场缺口。

sensesIntro.en: Niche starts as a literal hollow in a wall, becomes a place or job that fits a person exactly, then a species slot in nature and a narrow opening in a market.
sensesIntro.cn: niche 先指墙上真实的凹处，再指恰好适合某人的位置或工作，然后指物种在自然中的位置，以及市场上的窄缝。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hollow in a wall that holds one object exactly.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙面上一个恰好容纳一件物品的凹处。

branches.en: The wall recess is the concrete original sense.
branches.cn: 墙上的凹处是最具体的本义。

branches.en: The fitting hollow becomes a comfortable spot.
branches.cn: 合身的凹处变成了舒适的角落。

branches.en: A career opening inherits the fit image.
branches.cn: 职业机会继承了「合身」的形象。

branches.en: Biology and business both map the hollow onto a narrow available slot.
branches.cn: 生态学与商学都把「凹处」投射到一个狭窄的可用位置。

branches.en: The modifier use names anything aimed at one narrow group.
branches.cn: 作定语时指任何面向某一小群体的东西。

intro.en: Niche is a borrowed word with no productive English affix; its family is formed by plural, adjective ending, and noun modifiers.
intro.cn: niche 是借词，本身不含可产的英语词缀；它的词族依靠复数、形容词词尾和名词修饰构成。

latinIntro.en: The word has no classical Latin source; it reaches English through Italian and French, so no Latin cognates are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有古典拉丁语来源，经由意大利语和法语进入英语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The lamp sits in a niche of the wall.
items.exampleCN: 灯放在墙上的壁龛里。

items.example: The ending in niches keeps the soft sound.
items.exampleCN: niches 中的词尾保留了柔和的读音。

items.example: Niched walls hold small statues.
items.exampleCN: 带壁龛的墙用来安放小雕像。

items.example: The firm sells to a niche market.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司的产品面向细分市场。

items.example: Each bird has its own ecological niche.
items.exampleCN: 每种鸟都有自己的生态位。

items.meaning: a product for a narrow group
items.example: A niche product needs loyal buyers.
items.exampleCN: 小众产品需要忠实的买家。

items.example: The rare form nicheless is hardly used today.
items.exampleCN: nicheless 这一罕见形式今天几乎不用。

items.example: Many graduates try to find a niche quickly.
items.exampleCN: 许多毕业生设法尽快找到自己的位置。

items.meaning: to build a small special position
items.example: The small farm carved out a niche in the cheese trade.
items.exampleCN: 这家小农场在奶酪行业开辟出一片天地。

definition_zh: 镍；五分硬币；镍合金
definition_en: a hard silver white metal used in alloys and coins, and in North America a coin worth five cents
core_image: 一枚闪亮的银白色金属币，捏在指间又硬又沉
scene: 在旧报纸的价格栏里，铜和镍的价格一起往上跳。On the old price page, copper and nickel had both jumped in a single morning.
sceneCN: 这里 nickel 是「镍」（第 1 个义项：一种银白色硬金属）；句意：在旧报纸的行情版上，铜和镍在一个上午里都大幅上涨。

pos.zh: 镍；五分硬币；镍合金
给……镀镍

collocations.zh: 一点一点地花小钱；琐碎地压价
每一……五分钱（表价格很低）

derivatives.zh: 含镍的（nickel 加 -ferous「含有」构成）
早期投币电影院或自动点唱机，因投入五分硬币而得名
白铜；铜镍合金（拉丁 cuprum「铜」与 nickel 组合）

senses.title: The metal itself
senses.definition: a hard, silver white metal that resists rust and is used in alloys, plating, and batteries
senses.definitionCN: 一种坚硬、银白色的金属，抗锈，用于合金、电镀和电池
senses.example: Stainless steel contains chromium and nickel.
senses.exampleCN: 不锈钢里含有铬和镍。
senses.why: Miners in the sixteenth century blamed a mischievous spirit for the reddish ore, and the metal kept that earthy, stubborn image.
senses.whyCN: 十六世纪的矿工把这种偏红的矿石归咎于一个捣乱的精灵，镍便带着这种顽固、难以冶炼的印象流传下来。

senses.title: The five cent coin
senses.definition: a North American coin worth five cents, named after the metal it was once made of
senses.definitionCN: 北美的一种价值五分的硬币，因最初所用的金属而得名
senses.example: She dropped a nickel into the tin cup.
senses.exampleCN: 她往铁杯里丢了一枚五分镍币。
senses.why: When the new small coin was struck, the cheapest hard metal gave it both its body and its name.
senses.whyCN: 当那枚新小硬币被铸造出来时，最便宜又坚硬的金属既给了它身体，也给了它名字。

senses.title: A nickel alloy
senses.definition: any metal mixture containing nickel, such as cupronickel used for coins and marine fittings
senses.definitionCN: 任何含镍的金属混合物，例如用于硬币和船用配件的白铜
senses.example: The ship fittings were made from a tough nickel alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 船上的配件由一种坚韧的镍合金制成。
senses.why: A metal that refuses to rust on its own becomes even tougher when melted together with copper, so the alloy is the metal turned into a family.
senses.whyCN: 一种本身不易生锈的金属与铜熔合后会更加坚韧，于是合金就成了这种金属的「家族」。

senses.title: To coat with nickel
senses.definition: to cover a surface with a thin layer of nickel, usually by electricity
senses.definitionCN: 通常通过电流，在表面上覆盖一层薄薄的镍
senses.example: The workshop nickels the brass keys before it sells them.
senses.exampleCN: 工坊在出售黄铜钥匙前会给它们镀镍。
senses.why: Because the metal is hard and shiny, factories use it as a thin skin, turning the noun into a verb of coating.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种金属坚硬又有光泽，工厂把它当作一层薄薄的外皮，名词于是转成了「镀」的动词。

senses.title: A tiny amount of money
senses.definition: in informal North American use, a very small sum of money that hardly matters
senses.definitionCN: 在北美口语中，指几乎无关紧要的极少的钱
senses.example: He would not spend a nickel on that old radio.
senses.exampleCN: 他连一分钱也不会花在那台旧收音机上。
senses.why: A coin worth five cents is the smallest everyday unit of value, so a nickel stands for any trivial amount.
senses.whyCN: 一枚只值五分的硬币是日常最小面值，于是 nickel 就代表任何微不足道的金额。

intro.en: Nickel comes from German Nickel, a miner insult meaning Old Nick, the devil, or else a troublesome goblin.
intro.cn: nickel 来自德语 Nickel，是矿工骂人的话，意为「老尼克」（魔鬼）或捣蛋的小妖精。

items.en: Nickel is a short form of Nikolaus, used as a name for a mischievous goblin.
items.cn: Nickel 是 Nikolaus 的简称，用来指捣蛋的小妖精。

items.en: Miners in Saxony call the reddish ore Kupfernickel, the goblin copper, because it yields no copper.
items.cn: 萨克森的矿工把偏红的矿石叫做「妖精铜矿」，因为它炼不出铜。

items.en: Swedish chemists record the new metal as nickel in 1751, keeping the ore name but dropping the goblin word for copper.
items.cn: 瑞典化学家在 1751 年把这种新金属记为 nickel，保留了矿石名，却去掉了指铜的妖精字样。

items.en: English adopts nickel from Swedish, and the element symbol Ni follows.
items.cn: 英语从瑞典语借入 nickel，元素符号 Ni 也由此而来。

items.en: The United States mints a five cent coin from a copper nickel mix, and people call it a nickel.
items.cn: 美国用铜镍合金铸造五分硬币，人们就叫它 nickel。

note.en: Nickel sits beside other metals with similar colours and names, and beside unit of money words that share its coin image.
note.cn: nickel 与颜色、名称相似的其他金属相邻，也与共享「硬币」意象的货币词相邻。

entries.definition: a small cut or notch; just a shortened spelling, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 小切口；只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: an early cinema or jukebox that worked with coins
entries.definitionCN: 投币式早期影院或点唱机

entries.definition: containing nickel
a hard silver white metal used in magnets and batteries
entries.definitionCN: 钴（用于磁体和电池的银白色硬金属）

entries.definition: chromium, a shiny metal used for plating
a North American coin worth ten cents

normalIntro.en: Nickel is the stubborn silver metal that also names a small coin and a cheap unit of money.
normalIntro.cn: nickel 是一种顽固的银白色金属，同时也是一枚小硬币、一个廉价货币单位的名字。

normal.en: Nickel and dime breaks down into two small coins.
normal.cn: nickel and dime 一语里藏着一大一小两枚硬币。

normal.en: Nickel alloy is a family of tough mixtures with that metal.
normal.cn: nickel alloy 是以这种金属为主要成分的一系列坚韧合金。

normal.en: A nickel is the smallest coin in everyday American use.
normal.cn: nickel 是美国人日常使用的最小面额硬币。

normal.en: Cupronickel joins Latin cuprum for copper with nickel, which explains the whitish coin metal.
normal.cn: cupronickel 把表示铜的拉丁词 cuprum 与 nickel 拼在一起，说明了铸币金属的银白色。

normal.en: Compare copper: copper is the red metal, and the goblin ore was called false copper because it looked similar.
normal.cn: 对比 copper：铜是红色金属，那种妖精矿石正因外观相似才被叫做假铜。

abstract.en: Picture a small goblin swapping the copper in your ore for something hard and stubborn.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小妖精把你矿石里的铜换成了又硬又难对付的东西。

abstract.en: Imagine a silver coin so worn that its shine has gone dull.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚磨得失去光泽的银色硬币。

abstract.en: Think of a factory bath that leaves a thin bright skin on a key.
abstract.cn: 想象一道工厂镀槽，在一把钥匙上留下一层薄薄的亮皮。

examples.en: Nickel makes steel stronger and more resistant to rust.
examples.cn: 镍能让钢更坚固、更耐锈。

examples.en: He paid five dollars and twenty nickels for the ticket.
examples.cn: 他用五美元加二十枚五分镍币买了这张票。

examples.en: The company nickels the small parts before assembly.
examples.cn: 公司在装配前给小零件镀镍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「霓扣」——银白色的金属做成亮闪闪的硬币，像霓虹灯一样反光；再加扣子式的小圆片，就是镍与五分镍币。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源较清楚：德语 Nickel（Nikolaus 的简称，指捣蛋的小妖精）→ 矿产名 Kupfernickel（妖精铜；曾误记作 koppar nickel）→ 瑞典语 nickel → 英语 nickel，核心义「银白色硬金属」，再引申为五分硬币。

sensesIntro.en: Nickel names one hard silver metal first, then the five cent coin made from it, the alloys it forms, the act of plating with it, and a negligible amount of money.
sensesIntro.cn: nickel 先指一种银白色的硬金属，再指用它铸成的五分硬币，然后指它形成的合金、镀镍这一动作，以及微不足道的一点钱。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard silver coin pinched between two fingers.
core.cn: 核心意象：两指捏着一枚坚硬的银白色硬币。

branches.en: The metal is the historical base of every other sense.
branches.cn: 金属义是所有其他义项的历史根基。

branches.en: The coin takes the metal name directly.
branches.cn: 硬币直接沿用了金属的名字。

branches.en: The alloy sense widens the metal into its mixtures.
branches.cn: 合金义把这种金属扩展到它的混合物。

branches.en: The coin becomes a measure of small money.
branches.cn: 硬币义进而成为小额金钱的计量单位。

branches.en: Because the metal is hard, it is used as a coating.
branches.cn: 因为金属坚硬，它被用作镀层。

intro.en: Nickel is a German loanword; English builds compounds and compounds with it rather than adding Latin affixes.
intro.cn: nickel 是德语借词；英语主要围绕它构成复合词和组合，而不是加拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: The metal name itself is German, but classical Latin supplies the element symbols and words used in its compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 金属名本身来自德语，不过古典拉丁语为它的化合物提供了元素符号与词汇。

items.example: Nickel resists rust well.
items.exampleCN: 镍很耐锈。

items.example: The ending -el gives Nickel a familiar ring, as in Nikolaus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -el 让 Nickel 带有亲昵口吻，相当于 Nikolaus 的昵称。

items.example: They nickel the brass fittings.
items.exampleCN: 他们给黄铜配件镀镍。

items.example: The parts were nickeled last week.
items.exampleCN: 这些零件上周镀了镍。

items.example: The suffix -ous appears in nickeliferous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 出现在 nickeliferous 中。

items.example: The suffix -ferous makes nickeliferous mean nickel bearing.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ferous 使 nickeliferous 意为「含镍的」。

items.example: Cuprum plus nickel gives cupronickel.
items.exampleCN: cuprum 加 nickel 构成 cupronickel。

items.example: The symbol Ni comes from the German name.
items.exampleCN: 元素符号 Ni 取自德语名称。

definition_zh: 使轻微烦恼；小操心；挑小毛病；耗时费力地做
definition_en: to worry someone slightly for a long time, to criticize small details, or to work slowly at something fiddly
core_image: 一只小虫在身上轻轻不停地咬，赶不走也抓不住
scene: 那份邮件里有一处不对劲，整晚都在他心里轻轻发痒。Something in that email made him uneasy, and the doubt nagged and niggled at him all night.
sceneCN: 这里 niggle 是「使轻微烦恼」（第 1 个义项：小事持续令人隐隐不安）；句意：那封邮件里有些地方让他不安，那份疑虑整晚都在他心头轻轻作痛。

pos.zh: 使轻微烦恼；小操心；挑剔小毛病；费神地做；小步移动
小烦恼；小挑剔；小毛病

derivatives.zh: niggling 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「琐碎的、令人烦躁不安的」
niggler 由动词加 -er 构成，义为「爱挑剔小事的人」
niggly 由动词加 -y 构成，义为「有点烦人的、琐碎的」（非正式）

senses.title: To worry slightly and steadily
senses.definition: to make someone feel a small, constant worry or unease that keeps coming back
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生一种持续存在、反复冒出来的轻微担忧或不安
senses.example: A doubt niggled at him all the way home.
senses.exampleCN: 回家路上一丝疑虑一直隐隐困扰着他。
senses.why: The word likely comes from a dialect verb meaning to gnaw or nibble, so the image is a small creature chewing away at the edge of a thought.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一般认为来自方言动词，意为「啃咬、小口咬」，所以意象是一只小动物一点点啃着念头的边缘。

senses.title: To pick at small faults
senses.definition: to complain about or criticize small details that are not really important
senses.definitionCN: 对并不重要的细小之处抱怨或批评
senses.example: Stop niggling over every comma in the report.
senses.exampleCN: 别再为报告里每一个逗号挑刺了。
senses.why: If a tiny creature keeps nibbling, a person who keeps finding small faults acts the same way: many small bites instead of one big complaint.
senses.whyCN: 小东西一点一点地咬，总找小毛病的人也一样：不是一次大抱怨，而是许多小口啄食。

senses.title: To fuss over a job
senses.definition: to spend a long time on small or fiddly work, often without much progress
senses.definitionCN: 花很长时间处理细小繁琐的工作，常常进展不大
senses.example: She niggled away at the accounts until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 她在账目上磨蹭到半夜。
senses.why: Slow, repeated small actions match the nibbling image, so doing a job in tiny, fussy steps is also to niggle.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢而反复的小动作正对应「啃咬」的意象，所以一件活被拆成细碎恼人的步骤来做也叫 niggle。

senses.title: To move in small steps
senses.definition: in some British dialect use, to move along slowly and awkwardly in small steps
senses.definitionCN: 在英国部分方言中，指笨拙地一小步一小步地慢慢移动
senses.example: The old van niggled up the hill in low gear.
senses.exampleCN: 旧货车挂着低速挡一点点爬上坡。
senses.why: The teeth of small forward movements repeat the same rhythm as small bites, so slow shuffling motion took the word as well.
senses.whyCN: 向前小挪的动作与「小口咬」是同一个节奏，于是缓慢挪动这一义也归入了这个词。

senses.title: A small annoyance
senses.definition: a small problem, discomfort, or worry that is annoying but not serious
senses.definitionCN: 令人烦恼但不严重的细小问题、不适或担忧
senses.example: He has a nagging niggle in his shoulder after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛后他肩膀隐隐作痛。
senses.why: Any tiny annoying thing can be named by the same word, because it behaves like a small biting insect: it is brief but hard to ignore.
senses.whyCN: 任何细小恼人的事都能用这个词：它像一只小咬虫，时间不长却难以忽视。

intro.en: Niggle is probably from a Scandinavian or dialect verb meaning to gnaw or nibble; its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: niggle 一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语或方言中表示「啃咬」的动词，更早的来源不确定。

items.en: A verb with the sense to nibble or gnaw is recorded in northern English dialect.
items.cn: 英格兰北部方言中记载了表示「小口咬、啃」的动词。

items.en: An early record gives a Latin gloss for a small nibbling bite, the earliest written trace of the nibbling sense.
items.cn: 早期记录中有一处拉丁语注释表示「小块啃咬」的意思，是最早的书面痕迹。

items.en: The verb appears with the sense of finding small faults or wasting time on trifles.
items.cn: 动词出现「挑小毛病、在琐事上消磨时间」的用法。

items.en: The meaning widens to slight, persistent worry, as in a niggling doubt.
items.cn: 词义扩展为持续不断的轻微担忧，如令人隐隐不安的疑虑。

items.en: The noun niggle names a small annoyance, especially in British and Australian English.
items.cn: 名词 niggle 指小烦恼，多见于英式与澳大利亚英语。

note.en: Niggle sits beside similar sounding words with unrelated roots, and beside ordinary words for small worries and small criticisms.
note.cn: niggle 与一些读音相近但词根无关的词相邻，也与表示小担忧、小挑剔的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: to move with quick small twisting movements; only the shape of the spelling is similar, the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 扭动；只是词形相近，词源不同

entries.definition: to make something move with short quick shakes; the root is different
small but annoying and hard to get rid of
entries.definitionCN: 令人烦躁的；难以摆脱的

entries.definition: to cause someone to feel anxious
to make someone slightly angry
unnecessary worry or fussy complaint

normalIntro.en: Niggle is a small thing that will not let go: a doubt that bites away, a critic who picks at commas, a task that drags on.
normalIntro.cn: niggle 是甩不掉的小事：反复啃咬的疑虑、专挑逗号的挑剔者、拖拖拉拉的任务。

normal.en: A niggle of doubt is a small worry that keeps returning.
normal.cn: a niggle of doubt 是反复出现的细微疑虑。

normal.en: Niggle away at a problem means to worry it slowly, one small piece at a time.
normal.cn: niggle away at a problem 指一点一点地、缓慢地琢磨难题。

normal.en: The adjective niggling adds -ing, as in a niggling headache.
normal.cn: 形容词 niggling 由动词加 -ing 构成，如隐约难消的头痛。

normal.en: In British English a niggle can be a small injury that keeps bothering a player.
normal.cn: 在英式英语里，niggle 也可指困扰运动员的轻微伤病。

normal.en: Compare nag: nag is a repeated complaint from someone else, while niggle is the small worry that bites from inside.
normal.cn: 对比 nag：nag 是别人反复的唠叨，niggle 则是从内心轻轻咬人的小担忧。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito that circles your ear and will not settle.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子绕着耳朵转，怎么也停不下来。

abstract.en: Imagine a splinter under the skin that only stings when you press.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤里的一根刺，只在被按到时才微微刺痛。

abstract.en: Think of a loosening shoelace that you retie again and again.
abstract.cn: 想象一条松开的鞋带，你一遍又一遍地重新系上。

examples.en: A small doubt niggled at her before the interview.
examples.cn: 面试前一丝小小的疑虑一直困扰着她。

examples.en: He ignores the niggles and keeps editing every line.
examples.cn: 他无视那些小烦恼，继续逐行修改。

examples.en: The nagging niggling pain in his knee stopped him running.
examples.cn: 膝盖上隐隐作痛的毛病让他无法跑步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「你哥了」——你哥总在旁边挑你小毛病，一句话一句轻轻地念叨，让人隐隐烦躁。这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 一般认为来自斯堪的纳维亚语或英格兰北部方言中表示「小口啃咬」的动词，源头不确定；核心义「小口、反复、缓慢地咬」引申为持续的小烦恼、挑剔小毛病与琐碎耗时的工作。

sensesIntro.en: Niggle begins with the picture of something small biting repeatedly, which grows into slight worry, small fault finding, then fussy work, slow shuffling, and finally the noun for a minor annoyance.
sensesIntro.cn: niggle 从「小东西反复啃咬」的画面出发，发展为轻微担忧、挑剔小毛病、琐碎耗时的工作和小步挪动，最后成为名词「小烦恼」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tiny insect that keeps biting and cannot be brushed off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只赶不走、反复轻咬的小虫。

branches.en: A repeated bite becomes a persistent small worry.
branches.cn: 反复的轻咬变成挥之不去的轻微担忧。

branches.en: Many small bites make the fault finder.
branches.cn: 许多小口咬合在一起，就出现了挑剔者。

branches.en: Slow nibbling names work done in tiny steps.
branches.cn: 缓慢啃咬的动作指一件活被拆成极小的步骤来做。

branches.en: Moving in small steps keeps the same rhythm.
branches.cn: 小步挪动延续了相同的节奏。

branches.en: The feeling and the thing that causes it share one word.
branches.cn: 这种感觉与引起它的东西共用同一个词。

intro.en: Niggle is a short native verb with a dialect background; English extends it with -ing, -er, and -y rather than Latin affixes.
intro.cn: niggle 是带有方言色彩的简短本土动词；英语用 -ing、-er、-y 扩展它，而不是拉丁词缀。

latinIntro.en: Niggle has no classical Latin root, so the classical Latin items here are only the near verbs for gnawing and worrying.
latinIntro.cn: niggle 没有古典拉丁语词根，这里列出的古典拉丁语条目只是表示「啃咬、烦扰」的邻近动词。

items.example: The doubt keeps niggling at me.
items.exampleCN: 这个疑虑一直隐隐困扰我。

items.example: The ending -le in niggle suggests small repeated bites.
items.exampleCN: niggle 中的 -le 暗示小而反复的咬。

items.example: The suffix -ing gives niggling.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ing 构成 niggling。

items.example: The suffix -er gives niggler.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 niggler。

items.example: The suffix -y gives niggly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 构成 niggly。

items.example: The idea niggled at his mind.
items.exampleCN: 那个念头在他脑中萦绕不去。

items.example: A niggle of fear stayed all day.
items.exampleCN: 一丝恐惧整日不散。

items.example: The niggly details took hours.
items.exampleCN: 那些琐碎的细节花了好几个小时。

items.meaning: a person who picks at small faults
items.example: The niggler rewrote every comma.
items.exampleCN: 那个爱挑刺的人把每个逗号都改了。
